     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→Dispersal Draft is a web application for running async auction drafts for fantasy football. It uses FastAPI with WebSockets for real-time updates, Jinja2 templates for the frontend.
     8→
     9→**Current State:** Single-tenant with JSON file persistence (one draft at a time)
    10→**Target State:** Multi-tenant platform with SQLite persistence (see Migration Plan below)
    11→
    12→## Core Commands
    13→
    14→### Development
    15→```bash
    16→# Activate virtual environment
    17→source venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
    18→venv\Scripts\activate     # Windows
    19→
    20→# Install dependencies
    21→pip install -r requirements.txt
    22→
    23→# Run development server with auto-reload
    24→uvicorn app.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
    25→
    26→# Run production server
    27→uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
    28→```
    29→
    30→### Access Points
    31→- Admin Panel: `http://localhost:8000/admin?admin_token=<TOKEN>`
    32→- Manager View: `http://localhost:8000/draft?token=<MANAGER_TOKEN>`
    33→- Health Check: `http://localhost:8000/health`
    34→
    35→### Configuration (Current)
    36→Environment variables are loaded from `.env` file:
    37→- `ADMIN_TOKEN` - Secret token for admin access (default: admin-secret-token)
    38→- `RESEND_API_KEY` - Optional API key for email notifications via Resend
    39→- `FROM_EMAIL` - Email address for sending notifications
    40→- `DRAFT_URL` - Base URL for draft links in emails
    41→
    42→Note: These will change during migration. See "Migration Plan" section below for target environment variables.
    43→
    44→### State Management (Current - Will Change)
    45→Draft state is persisted to `draft_state.json` in the working directory. To reset the draft completely, delete this file and restart the server.
    46→
    47→Note: This will be replaced by SQLite database during migration. See "Migration Plan" section below.
    48→
    49→## Architecture
    50→
    51→### Application Structure
    52→
    53→```
    54→app/
    55→├── main.py           # FastAPI app, WebSocket endpoint, background tasks
    56→├── state.py          # DraftState class with JSON persistence and business logic
    57→├── models.py         # Data models (Player, Manager, Bid, Auction, etc.)
    58→├── websocket.py      # ConnectionManager for WebSocket broadcasts
    59→├── auth.py           # Token-based authentication helpers
    60→├── email.py          # Email notification sending via Resend
    61→├── routers/
    62→│   ├── admin.py      # Admin endpoints (config, managers, players, control)
    63→│   ├── draft.py      # Draft endpoints (bid, nominate, auction view)
    64→│   └── manager.py    # Manager endpoints (profile, email settings, bid history)
    65→├── templates/        # Jinja2 HTML templates
    66→└── static/           # CSS and static assets
    67→```
    68→
    69→### Key Design Patterns
    70→
    71→**State Management**
    72→- `DraftState` (state.py) is the single source of truth for all draft data
    73→- All state changes go through methods on `DraftState` which automatically save to JSON
    74→- Cross-platform file locking (msvcrt on Windows, fcntl on Unix) prevents corruption
    75→- Singleton pattern via `get_state()` ensures one state instance per process
    76→
    77→**Real-Time Updates**
    78→- WebSocket connections managed by `ConnectionManager` (websocket.py)
    79→- All state-changing operations broadcast updates to connected clients
    80→- Background task in main.py polls every 30 seconds to check auction expiry and scheduled pause windows
    81→- WebSocket messages follow format: `{"event": "...", "data": {...}}`
    82→
    83→**Auction Timer Management**
    84→- Auctions have `end_time` (datetime) set when created
    85→- On manual/scheduled pause: remaining seconds calculated and stored in `auction_remaining_seconds` dict
    86→- On resume: new `end_time` calculated by adding remaining seconds to current time
    87→- Background task compares `end_time` to current time to detect expiry
    88→
    89→**Proxy Bidding System**
    90→- Each bid has `max_bid` (private, known only to bidder) and `current_bid` (public, minimum needed to win)
    91→- When a new bid arrives, state.py recalculates winning bid and current amounts
    92→- Similar to eBay proxy bidding: system automatically bids minimum increment over previous winner up to your max
    93→
    94→**Nomination Queue**
    95→- Circular queue (`NominationQueue` in models.py) tracks whose turn it is
    96→- Only managers with `in_nomination_pool=True` participate in rotation
    97→- Auto-nomination kicks in after `nomination_timeout_hours` if current nominator doesn't act
    98→- Queue advances after each successful nomination or auto-nomination
    99→
   100→**Scheduled Pause Windows**
   101→- `PauseWindow` objects define daily pause periods (e.g., 22:00-08:00 for overnight)
   102→- Background task checks if current time falls within any enabled window
   103→- Automatically pauses/resumes draft and freezes/restores auction timers
   104→- Windows can span midnight (handled by time comparison logic in `is_currently_in_window()`)
   105→
   106→### Data Models (models.py)
   107→
   108→All models use dataclasses with `to_dict()` / `from_dict()` for JSON serialization:
   109→
   110→- **Player**: id, name, position, team, age, sleeper_id
   111→- **Manager**: id, name, token (UUID), email, budget (Decimal), won_players, email_notifications, in_nomination_pool
   112→- **Bid**: id, player_id, manager_id, max_bid (Decimal), current_bid (Decimal), timestamp, is_winning
   113→- **Auction**: id, player_id, end_time, nominator_id, winning_bid_id, bid_history, is_complete, winner_id, final_price
   114→- **DraftConfig**: timer_duration_hours, timer_extension_hours, max_concurrent_auctions, starting_budget, nomination_timeout_hours, min_bid, bid_increment, pause_windows
   115→- **PauseWindow**: start_hour, start_minute, end_hour, end_minute, enabled, name
   116→- **NominationQueue**: order (list of manager IDs), current_index, last_nomination_time
   117→- **DraftStatus**: LOBBY, ACTIVE, PAUSED, COMPLETE (enum)
   118→
   119→### Router Responsibilities
   120→
   121→**admin.py**
   122→- Configure draft settings (timers, budget, concurrent auctions)
   123→- Add/remove managers and players
   124→- Import players from CSV or Sleeper API
   125→- Start/pause/resume draft
   126→- Manage scheduled pause windows (add, toggle, remove)
   127→- Undo bids, adjust budgets, force-end auctions
   128→- Export draft results to CSV
   129→
   130→**draft.py**
   131→- Main draft view (GET /draft) - renders draft.html with full state
   132→- Place bid (POST /draft/bid) - validates budget, processes proxy bid, broadcasts updates
   133→- Nominate player (POST /draft/nominate) - starts new auction if slots available
   134→- Pass nomination (POST /draft/pass) - skips current nominator's turn
   135→- View specific auction (GET /draft/auction/{id})
   136→
   137→**manager.py**
   138→- Get manager profile (GET /manager/me)
   139→- Update email settings (POST /manager/me/email) for notifications
   140→- View bid history (GET /manager/me/bids)
   141→- View remaining player pool (GET /manager/remaining-players)
   142→- Public manager list (GET /manager/all)
   143→
   144→### WebSocket Events
   145→
   146→**Client → Server**
   147→- `ping` - keepalive
   148→- `place_bid` - submit bid (routed to draft.process_bid)
   149→- `nominate` - nominate player (routed to draft.process_nomination)
   150→- `pass` - skip nomination (routed to draft.process_pass)
   151→
   152→**Server → Client**
   153→- `pong` - ping response
   154→- `auction_started` - new auction created
   155→- `auction_ended` - auction completed with winner
   156→- `bid_placed` - new bid on auction (with updated current_bid and winner)
   157→- `manager_joined` / `manager_left` - connection status
   158→- `nomination_turn` - whose turn to nominate
   159→- `draft_status` - draft status changed (active/paused/complete)
   160→- Paused payload with remaining seconds for each auction
   161→
   162→### External Integrations
   163→
   164→**Sleeper API**
   165→- Import players from Sleeper league using `sleeper-api-wrapper` library
   166→- Fetches league rosters and player details (position, team, age)
   167→- Admin can enter Sleeper league ID to bulk-import players
   168→
   169→**Resend Email**
   170→- Optional email notifications when managers are outbid
   171→- Requires `RESEND_API_KEY`, `FROM_EMAIL`, `DRAFT_URL` environment variables
   172→- Sent via `send_outbid_notification()` in email.py
   173→
   174→## Development Notes
   175→
   176→### Timer Freeze/Resume Logic
   177→The pause/resume system must preserve exact remaining time for auctions. When pausing:
   178→1. Calculate seconds remaining for each active auction (`end_time - now`)
   179→2. Store in `auction_remaining_seconds` dict
   180→3. Set `paused_at` timestamp
   181→
   182→When resuming:
   183→1. Calculate new `end_time` for each auction (`now + remaining_seconds`)
   184→2. Clear `auction_remaining_seconds` and `paused_at`
   185→
   186→This ensures timers properly freeze and resume regardless of how long the pause lasted.
   187→
   188→### Background Task Behavior
   189→The `check_auctions()` task in main.py runs continuously:
   190→- Every 30 seconds, checks for expired auctions and scheduled pause windows
   191→- When paused, broadcasts remaining time every 30s but doesn't process auction expiry
   192→- Auto-pauses when entering scheduled window, auto-resumes when exiting
   193→- Handles nomination timeouts and auto-nomination
   194→
   195→### Authentication
   196→Token-based authentication only (no passwords):
   197→- Admin token from environment variable or default
   198→- Manager tokens are UUIDs generated on manager creation
   199→- All endpoints require either admin token or valid manager token
   200→- Tokens passed as query params (`?token=...` or `?admin_token=...`)
   201→
   202→### Decimal Precision
   203→All money amounts (bids, budgets, prices) use Python's `Decimal` type for precision. When serializing to JSON, convert to string. When deserializing, convert back to Decimal.
   204→
   205→## Common Development Tasks
   206→
   207→### Adding a New Auction Rule
   208→1. Update `DraftConfig` in models.py with new field
   209→2. Add serialization in `to_dict()` / `from_dict()`
   210→3. Update admin.py form handler to accept new config value
   211→4. Update admin.html template to add form field
   212→5. Implement logic in state.py methods (e.g., `place_bid`, `create_auction`)
   213→
   214→### Adding a New WebSocket Event
   215→1. Define event handler in main.py `handle_ws_message()`
   216→2. Add broadcasting method to ConnectionManager in websocket.py
   217→3. Update frontend JS in templates to handle new event type
   218→4. Broadcast from router after state change
   219→
   220→### Modifying State Persistence
   221→All changes to DraftState fields should call `self._save()` to persist to JSON. The state is automatically loaded on startup via `get_state()` singleton.
   222→
   223→---
   224→
   225→## Migration Plan: Multi-Tenant Platform
   226→
   227→The application is being migrated from single-tenant to multi-tenant. See `Website Migration.md` for the full plan. Key changes:
   228→
   229→### Target Architecture
   230→
   231→**Authentication Model (Token-based, no passwords):**
   232→- **Super Admin Token**: Environment variable (`SUPER_ADMIN_TOKEN`), platform-wide access
   233→- **Commissioner Token**: UUID per draft, grants admin access to that specific draft
   234→- **Manager Tokens**: UUID per manager per draft, grants participant access
   235→
   236→**Draft Creation Flow:**
   237→1. Visitor submits request form (name, email, draft name) at `/request-draft`
   238→2. Super admin reviews and approves/rejects at `/super-admin`
   239→3. On approval, system emails requester a one-time creation link
   240→4. Requester uses link to create draft, receives commissioner token via email
   241→5. Commissioner uses token to access `/drafts/{draft_id}/admin`
   242→
   243→### Database Schema (SQLite)
   244→
   245→```
   246→draft_requests    - pending/approved/rejected requests for new drafts
   247→drafts            - commissioner_email, commissioner_token, name, status, draft_type
   248→managers          - draft_id FK, token, name, email, budget
   249→players           - draft_id FK, name, position, team
   250→auctions          - draft_id FK, player_id, end_time, status
   251→bids              - draft_id FK, auction_id, manager_id, max_bid, current_bid
   252→draft_config      - draft_id FK, timer settings, budget settings
   253→pause_windows     - draft_id FK, time windows for auto-pause
   254→nomination_queue  - draft_id FK, rotation order
   255→```
   256→
   257→### URL Structure Changes
   258→
   259→| Current | Target |
   260→|---------|--------|
   261→| `/admin?admin_token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}/admin?token=X` |
   262→| `/draft?token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}?token=X` |
   263→| `/manager/me?token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}/manager/me?token=X` |
   264→| `/ws?token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}/ws?token=X` |
   265→| N/A | `/request-draft` (public) |
   266→| N/A | `/super-admin?token=X` |
   267→| N/A | `/create-draft?token=X` (one-time approval link) |
   268→
   269→### Key Files to Change
   270→
   271→| File | Change |
   272→|------|--------|
   273→| `app/database.py` | New - SQLite connection, migrations |
   274→| `app/state_db.py` | New - DraftStateDB class (replaces singleton) |
   275→| `app/state.py` | Deprecated after migration |
   276→| `app/auth.py` | Add draft_id scoping, commissioner token validation |
   277→| `app/routers/admin.py` | Prefix with `/drafts/{draft_id}/admin` |
   278→| `app/routers/draft.py` | Prefix with `/drafts/{draft_id}` |
   279→| `app/routers/manager.py` | Prefix with `/drafts/{draft_id}/manager` |
   280→| `app/routers/requests.py` | New - draft request/approval flow |
   281→| `app/routers/super_admin.py` | New - platform management |
   282→| `app/websocket.py` | Track connections by `(draft_id, token)` |
   283→| `app/main.py` | Background task iterates all active drafts |
   284→
   285→### Environment Variables (Target)
   286→
   287→| Variable | Description |
   288→|----------|-------------|
   289→| `DATABASE_PATH` | SQLite database path (default: `./data/drafts.db`) |
   290→| `SUPER_ADMIN_TOKEN` | Token for super admin access |
   291→| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Resend API key for all emails |
   292→| `FROM_EMAIL` | Sender email address |
   293→| `DRAFT_URL` | Base URL for email links |
   294→| `VENMO_USERNAME` | Optional tip link |
   295→
   296→### Migration Phases
   297→
   298→1. **Phase A**: Database foundation (SQLite, migrations, schema)
   299→2. **Phase B**: Request & approval system (public form, super admin review)
   300→3. **Phase C**: DraftStateDB class (replaces JSON singleton)
   301→4. **Phase D**: Router migration (add draft_id to all routes)
   302→5. **Phase E**: Background task refactor (batch queries across drafts)
   303→6. **Phase F**: Email notifications (wire up outbid/won emails)
   304→7. **Phase G**: Super admin features (all drafts view, impersonation)
   305→8. **Phase H**: Deployment (Render, domain, SSL)
   306→
   307→### Implementation Notes
   308→
   309→- Business logic in `DraftState` methods (proxy bidding, nomination queue, pause/resume) remains unchanged - just needs to read/write SQLite instead of JSON
   310→- WebSocket broadcasts must be scoped to draft - use `broadcast_to_draft(draft_id, message)`
   311→- Background task should catch per-draft errors without crashing the whole loop
   312→- Manager tokens remain UUIDs, just scoped to their draft
   313→- Commissioner token is separate from manager tokens (admin vs participant access)
   314→

     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→iOS app implementing the Koch method for learning Morse code. Single-user, supports 26 letters (Koch order: K M R S U A P T L O W I N J E F Y V G Q Z H B C D X) plus digits 0-9 for callsigns and RST reports.
     8→
     9→## Build & Run
    10→
    11→Uses XcodeGen for project configuration. The `project.yml` file defines the project structure.
    12→
    13→```bash
    14→# Regenerate Xcode project, build, and test
    15→make generate  # Regenerate xcodeproj from project.yml
    16→make build     # Build the app
    17→make test      # Run all tests
    18→make clean     # Clean build artifacts
    19→
    20→# Or manually
    21→xcodegen generate
    22→xcodebuild -scheme KochTrainer -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro'
    23→```

    88→## Core Rules

    90→This document defines the core guidelines applied during development.

    92→
    93→### 1. Core Principles
    94→
    95→**Details: [Philosophy](./guides/philosophy.md)**
    96→
    97→<rule type="critical" id="core-principles">
    98→- **Ask when uncertain**
    99→  If requirements are unclear, ask questions instead of assuming.
   100→  Wrong assumptions cause rework; questions ensure accurate implementation.
   101→
   102→- **Simplicity first**
   103→  Choose the simplest approach that meets requirements.
   104→  Complex solutions increase bug probability and make maintenance harder.
   105→  </rule>
   106→
   107→<examples>
   108→<example type="correct">
   109→<scenario>User: "Add caching for performance improvement"</scenario>
   110→<response>
   111→Before adding caching, I'd like to clarify a few things:
   112→
   113→1. What data should be cached?
   114→2. How should cache expiration be configured?
   115→3. Do you prefer memory-based (Redis) or file-based caching?
   116→
   117→Please provide this information so I can suggest an appropriate solution.
   118→</response>
   119→<reason>Clarified requirements first instead of making assumptions</reason>
   120→</example>
   121→
   122→<example type="incorrect">
   123→<scenario>User: "Add caching for performance improvement"</scenario>
   124→<response>
   125→[Starts implementing Redis caching without confirming requirements]
   126→</response>
   127→<reason>Made assumptions about cache type, target data, and TTL.
   128→Should clarify requirements first</reason>
   129→</example>
   130→</examples>
   131→
   132→### 2. Code Modification
   133→
   134→**Details: [Technical Standards](./guides/technical-standards.md)**
   135→
   136→<rule type="critical" id="code-modification">
   137→- **Read code first**
   138→  Don't guess without reading the code.
   139→  If the user mentions a specific file, always read it first.
   140→  Understand existing style, conventions, and abstractions before implementing.
   141→
   142→- **Minimal changes**
   143→  Only modify what was requested.
   144→  Unnecessary changes increase bug risk, complicate code reviews,
   145→  and interfere with git blame tracking.
   146→
   147→- **Preserve existing behavior**
   148→  Don't refactor without explicit request.
   149→  Other code may depend on existing behavior.
   150→  </rule>
   151→
   152→<examples>
   153→<example type="correct">
   154→<scenario>User: "Fix the null check in getUserEmail() function"</scenario>
   155→<response>
   156→
   157→```javascript
   158→// Before
   159→function getUserEmail(user) {
   160→  return user.email.toLowerCase();
   161→}
   162→
   163→// After - Only added the requested null check
   164→function getUserEmail(user) {
   165→  if (!user || !user.email) {
   166→    return null;
   167→  }
   168→  return user.email.toLowerCase();
   169→}
   170→```
   171→
   172→</response>
   173→<reason>Only modified the null check, left other parts unchanged</reason>
   174→</example>
   175→
   176→<example type="incorrect">
   177→<scenario>User: "Fix the null check in getUserEmail() function"</scenario>
   178→<response>
   179→
   180→```javascript
   181→// Refactored entire module, renamed function, changed structure
   182→class UserService {
   183→  static getEmailAddress(userObject) {
   184→    return userObject?.email?.toLowerCase() ?? "";
   185→  }
   186→  // "While at it" added 10 other methods
   187→}
   188→```
   189→
   190→</response>
   191→<reason>Performed large-scale refactoring beyond request scope.
   192→Should have only fixed the null check as requested</reason>
   193→</example>
   194→</examples>
   195→
   196→### 3. Testing
   197→
   198→**Details: [Quality Assurance](./guides/quality-assurance.md)**
   199→
   200→<rule type="critical" id="testing">
   201→- **Tests required**
   202→  All code must have tests.
   203→  Tests document functionality and prevent regressions.
   204→
   205→- **Maintain test integrity**
   206→  Don't modify tests to make them pass.
   207→  If tests fail, fix the code.
   208→
   209→- **No hardcoding**
   210→  Don't write solutions that only work for test cases.
   211→  Implement actual logic that solves the problem generally.
   212→  </rule>
   213→
   214→<examples>
   215→<example type="correct">
   216→<scenario>User: "Add a discount calculation function"</scenario>
   217→<response>
   218→First, I'll write the tests:
   219→
   220→```python
   221→def test_calculate_discount():
   222→    assert calculate_discount(100, 0.1) == 10
   223→    assert calculate_discount(100, 0) == 0
   224→    assert calculate_discount(0, 0.5) == 0
   225→
   226→def test_calculate_discount_invalid():
   227→    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
   228→        calculate_discount(-100, 0.1)
   229→    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
   230→        calculate_discount(100, 1.5)
   231→```
   232→
   233→Now implementing:
   234→
   235→```python
   236→def calculate_discount(price: float, rate: float) -> float:
   237→    """Calculate discount amount."""
   238→    if price < 0:
   239→        raise ValueError("Price cannot be negative")
   240→    if rate < 0 or rate > 1:
   241→        raise ValueError("Rate must be between 0 and 1")
   242→    return price * rate
   243→```
   244→
   245→</response>
   246→<reason>Wrote tests first, then implemented with general logic</reason>
   247→</example>
   248→
   249→<example type="incorrect">
   250→<scenario>Existing tests fail after code changes</scenario>
   251→<response>
   252→
   253→```python
   254→# Commented out failing test
   255→# def test_user_validation():
   256→#     assert validate_user(user) == True
   257→```
   258→
   259→</response>
   260→<reason>Deleted/disabled tests instead of fixing the problem.
   261→When tests fail, fix the code</reason>
   262→</example>
   263→</examples>

   265→### 4. Data Safety
   266→
   267→**Details: [Security](./guides/security.md)**
   268→
   269→<rule type="critical" id="data-safety">
   270→- **Approve destructive queries**
   271→  Get approval before running DELETE, UPDATE, ALTER queries.
   272→  Data loss can be difficult or impossible to recover.
   273→
   274→- **Production caution**
   275→  Verify in test environment first.
   276→  Operations affecting production data require additional confirmation.
   277→  </rule>
   278→
   279→<examples>
   280→<example type="correct">
   281→<scenario>User: "Delete old user records"</scenario>
   282→<response>
   283→Before deleting data, I need some clarification:
   284→
   285→1. How do you define "old users"? (e.g., no login for 6+ months)
   286→2. Is this production DB or test DB?
   287→3. Should I create a backup before deletion?
   288→4. Would you like to preview records with SELECT first?
   289→
   290→```sql
   291→-- First, let's preview what will be deleted
   292→SELECT COUNT(*), MIN(last_login), MAX(last_login)
   293→FROM users
   294→WHERE last_login < NOW() - INTERVAL 6 MONTH;
   295→```
   296→
   297→I'll execute DELETE after your approval.
   298→</response>
   299→<reason>Requested confirmation before destructive operation and provided preview</reason>
   300→</example>
   301→
   302→<example type="incorrect">
   303→<scenario>User: "Clean up the database"</scenario>
   304→<response>
   305→
   306→```sql
   307→-- Executed destructive queries without confirmation
   308→DELETE FROM users WHERE created_at < '2023-01-01';
   309→ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN old_status;
   310→TRUNCATE TABLE logs;
   311→```
   312→
   313→</response>
   314→<reason>Executed destructive queries without confirmation or approval.
   315→Operations with data loss risk always require prior approval</reason>
   316→</example>
   317→</examples>
   318→
   319→### 5. Problem Solving
   320→
   321→**Details: [Process](./guides/process.md)**
   322→
   323→<rule type="critical" id="problem-solving">
   324→- **Fix root cause**
   325→  Avoid band-aids or hiding symptoms.
   326→  Fixing the root cause prevents the problem from recurring.
   327→
   328→- **Reassess after 3 attempts**
   329→  If unresolved after 3 attempts, stop and consider different approaches.
   330→  Repeating the same method is inefficient.
   331→  </rule>
   332→
   333→<examples>
   334→<example type="correct">
   335→<scenario>Error: "Database connection timeout"</scenario>
   336→<response>
   337→Let me find the root cause of this error:
   338→
   339→1. Check logs: When did this start?
   340→2. Connection pool settings: What's the max connection count?
   341→3. Query performance: Are slow queries holding connections?
   342→4. Network: Is communication with DB server normal?
   343→
   344→Analysis result: Connection pool is limited to 10 and average requests are 50/sec.
   345→Root solution: I'll increase connection pool size and optimize connection timeout settings.
   346→</response>
   347→<reason>Investigated root cause and proposed appropriate solution</reason>
   348→</example>
   349→
   350→<example type="incorrect">
   351→<scenario>Error: "Database connection timeout"</scenario>
   352→<response>
   353→```python
   354→# Added try-catch to hide the error
   355→try:
   356→    db.connect()
   357→except TimeoutError:
   358→    pass  # Ignore error
   359→```
   360→</response>
   361→<reason>Band-aid that hides the problem without fixing root cause.
   362→Ignoring errors can lead to bigger problems later</reason>
   363→</example>
   364→</examples>

1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Identity
     6→
     7→`no-magic` is a collection of single-file, zero-dependency Python implementations of modern AI/ML algorithms. Each script is a complete, runnable program that trains a model from scratch and performs inference using only Python's standard library.
     8→
     9→**Repository status:** Planning/documentation phase. No implementation files exist yet. The engineering spec lives in `docs/implementation.md` (765 lines covering all 17 planned scripts).
    10→
    11→## Hard Constraints
    12→
    13→These are non-negotiable and override all other conventions:
    14→
    15→- **One `.py` file per algorithm.** No local imports, no `utils.py`, no companion files.
    16→- **Zero external dependencies.** Only Python stdlib: `os`, `math`, `random`, `json`, `struct`, `urllib`, `collections`, `itertools`, `functools`, `string`, `hashlib`, `time`. No NumPy, no PyTorch, no pip install.
    17→- **`python script.py` with zero arguments** runs the full train + inference loop.
    18→- **Under 10 minutes** on a laptop CPU (M-series Mac). No GPU.
    19→- **`random.seed(42)`** at the top of every script.
    20→- **Datasets auto-download** via `urllib` on first run, cached locally, max 5MB.
    21→- **No `requirements.txt`**, no `pyproject.toml`, no build tooling.
    22→
    23→## Running Scripts
    24→
    25→```bash
    26→python foundational/microgpt.py
    27→python alignment/microlora.py
    28→python systems/microattention.py
    29→```
    30→
    31→No virtual environments, no configuration, no setup.
    32→
    33→## Repository Structure
    34→
    35→```
    36→foundational/    # Core algorithms (GPT, RNN, BPE tokenizer, embeddings, RAG, diffusion, VAE)
    37→alignment/       # Training techniques (LoRA, DPO, PPO, MoE)
    38→systems/         # Inference optimizations (attention variants, KV-cache, quantization, Flash Attention, beam search)
    39→docs/
    40→  overview.md       # Philosophy and commenting standard
    41→  implementation.md # Engineering spec for all 17 scripts — read this before implementing anything
    42→```
    43→
    44→## Implementation Sequencing
    45→
    46→Scripts must be built in this order (from `docs/implementation.md`):
    47→
    48→| Phase | Scripts | Rationale |
    49→|-------|---------|-----------|
    50→| 1 | `microtokenizer.py`, `microembedding.py` | No autograd needed |
    51→| 2 | `microgpt.py`, `micrornn.py`, `microattention.py` | Establishes autograd `Value` class pattern |
    52→| 3 | `microrag.py`, `microlora.py` | Builds on Phase 2 |
    53→| 4 | `microdiffusion.py`, `microvae.py` | Independent algorithms |
    54→| 5 | `microdpo.py`, `microppo.py` | Requires stable base model |
    55→| 6 | `microquant.py`, `microkv.py`, `microflash.py` | Systems scripts, independent |
    56→| 7 | `microbeam.py`, `micromoe.py` | Final scripts |
    57→
    58→## Commenting Standard (Core Quality Bar)
    59→
    60→This is the primary review criterion. Every script must include all of these:
    61→
    62→1. **File thesis** — One-sentence docstring at the top stating what the script proves
    63→2. **Section headers** — `# === SECTION NAME ===` separating major phases (data loading, model definition, training loop, inference)
    64→3. **"Why" comments** — Explain reasoning, not what the code does
    65→4. **Math-to-code mappings** — Show equations with explicit variable correspondence
    66→5. **Intuition comments** — Why a technique works, not just how
    67→6. **Signpost comments** — Flag simplifying choices and note what production systems do differently
    68→7. **No obvious comments** — Every comment must add information the code doesn't convey
    69→
    70→Target ~30-40% comment density. The test: could a motivated engineer read the file top-to-bottom in one sitting and understand the algorithm without external references?
    71→
    72→## Code Style
    73→
    74→- Readability over cleverness — explicit loops over dense comprehensions when clearer
    75→- Descriptive names: `learning_rate` not `lr`, `hidden_dim` not `hd` (exceptions: math convention `x`, `z`, `mu`, `sigma`, loop indices, standard abbreviations `embd`, `attn`, `mlp`)
    76→- Functions named for what they compute: `rmsnorm`, `softmax`, `linear`
    77→- No classes unless the algorithm requires them (e.g., `Value` for autograd)
    78→- Consistent section ordering: imports → constants/hyperparameters → data loading → model definition → training loop → inference
    79→- 4-space indentation, 100 char max line length
    80→- Prefer `f-strings`, avoid global mutable state
    81→
    82→## Architectural Patterns
    83→
    84→**Scalar autograd (`Value` class):** Many scripts implement reverse-mode automatic differentiation from scratch. Used in: `microgpt`, `micrornn`, `microlora`, `microdpo`, `microppo`, `micromoe`.
    85→
    86→**Train + infer lifecycle:** Every script (except `microattention.py` and `microflash.py` which are forward-pass comparisons) trains a model and demonstrates inference.
    87→
    88→**Comparative implementations:** Some scripts demonstrate multiple variants side-by-side (`microattention` — all attention variants, `micrornn` — RNN vs GRU, `microbeam` — all decoding strategies).
    89→
    90→## Key References
    91→
    92→- Inspired by Karpathy's [micrograd](https://github.com/karpathy/micrograd), [makemore](https://github.com/karpathy/makemore), and `microgpt.py`
    93→- `CONTRIBUTING.md` contains the full quality checklist and PR requirements
    94→- Primary dataset: `names.txt` from Karpathy's makemore (~32K names), used across multiple scripts for direct architecture comparison
    95→

1→# context-evaluator
     2→
     3→AI agent documentation quality analyzer for AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files.
     4→
     5→This tool evaluates your AI agent instruction files using 17 specialized evaluators to identify issues and improvement opportunities. It helps ensure your documentation provides clear, actionable guidance for AI coding assistants.
     6→
     7→**An experimental project from [Packmind](https://github.com/PackmindHub/packmind).**
     8→
     9→---
    10→
    11→## How to Use
    12→
    13→### Option 1: Online (No Install)
    14→
    15→Visit **[https://context-evaluator.ai](https://context-evaluator.ai)** and paste your repository URL.
    16→
    17→### Option 2: Binary Release (No Dependencies)
    18→
    19→Download a standalone executable from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/PackmindHub/context-evaluator/releases). No runtime dependencies needed.
    20→
    21→Available platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon), macOS (Intel), Linux (x64), Windows (x64).
    22→
    23→```bash
    24→# Make executable (macOS/Linux)
    25→chmod +x ./context-evaluator-<platform>
    26→
    27→# Start the web UI
    28→./context-evaluator-<platform> api
    29→
    30→# Or run a CLI evaluation
    31→./context-evaluator-<platform> cli evaluate --url https://github.com/user/repo
    32→```
    33→
    34→Then open **http://localhost:3000** in your browser.
    35→
    36→### Option 3: From Source (requires Node 22+ and [Bun](https://bun.sh))
    37→
    38→```bash
    39→# Clone and install
    40→git clone https://github.com/PackmindHub/context-evaluator.git
    41→cd context-evaluator
    42→bun install
    43→
    44→# Start the application
    45→bun run dev
    46→```
    47→
    48→Then open **http://localhost:3000** in your browser.
    49→
    50→### Local Scanning Notes
    51→
    52→- Git clone operations run on your local machine
    53→- Private repositories may work if your git credentials are configured (SSH keys, credential helpers)
    54→- The homepage auto-detects which AI agents you have installed
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→## How it Works
    59→
    60→```
    61→Input (Git URL or Local Path)
    62→    ↓
    63→Clone Repository (if remote)
    64→    ↓
    65→Analyze Codebase (languages, frameworks, patterns)
    66→    ↓
    67→Find Documentation (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, linked files)
    68→    ↓
    69→Run 17 Evaluators via AI
    70→    ↓
    71→Rank by Impact
    72→    ↓
    73→Calculate Score & Grade
    74→    ↓
    75→Return Results
    76→```
    77→
    78→**Processing time:** 1-3 minutes depending on codebase size and AI provider.
    79→
    80→**Cost display:** Shows API costs when supported by the provider.
    81→
    82→---
    83→
    84→## Understanding Results
    85→
    86→Results are categorized into two types:
    87→
    88→- **Errors** (13 evaluators): Issues with existing content that need fixing
    89→- **Suggestions** (4 evaluators): Opportunities for new content based on codebase analysis
    90→
    91→Each issue includes:
    92→- Severity level (Critical, High, Medium, Low)
    93→- Location in your documentation
    94→- Problem description
    95→- Recommended fix
    96→
    97→---
    98→
    99→## Evaluators
   100→
   101→| # | Evaluator | Type | Description |
   102→|---|-----------|------|-------------|
   103→| 01 | Content Quality | Error | Detects human-focused, irrelevant, or vague content |
   104→| 02 | Structure & Formatting | Error | Identifies poor organization and inconsistent formatting |
   105→| 03 | Command Completeness | Error | Finds incomplete commands and missing prerequisites |
   106→| 04 | Testing Guidance | Error | Detects absent or unclear testing instructions |
   107→| 05 | Code Style Clarity | Error | Identifies missing or conflicting style guidelines |
   108→| 06 | Language Clarity | Error | Finds ambiguous language and undefined jargon |
   109→| 07 | Workflow Integration | Error | Detects missing git/CI workflow documentation |
   110→| 08 | Project Structure | Error | Identifies missing codebase organization explanations |
   111→| 09 | Security Awareness | Error | Finds exposed credentials and security risks |
   112→| 10 | Completeness & Balance | Error | Detects skeletal or over-detailed content |
   113→| 11 | Subdirectory Coverage | Suggestion | Recommends separate AGENTS.md for subdirectories |
   114→| 12 | Context Gaps | Suggestion | Discovers undocumented framework/tool patterns |
   115→| 13 | Contradictory Instructions | Error | Detects conflicting instructions across files |
   116→| 14 | Test Patterns Coverage | Suggestion | Discovers undocumented testing conventions |
   117→| 15 | Database Patterns Coverage | Suggestion | Discovers undocumented database/ORM patterns |
   118→| 17 | Markdown Validity | Error | Checks markdown syntax and link validity |
   119→| 19 | Outdated Documentation | Error | Verifies documented paths and files exist |
   120→
   121→---
   122→
   123→## AI Providers
   124→
   125→The tool supports multiple AI providers:
   126→
   127→| Provider | CLI Flag | Setup |
   128→|----------|----------|-------|
   129→| Claude Code | `--agent claude` (default) | [claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code) |
   130→| Cursor Agent | `--agent cursor` | [cursor.com](https://cursor.com) |
   131→| OpenCode | `--agent opencode` | [github.com/opencode-ai/opencode](https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode) |
   132→| GitHub Copilot | `--agent github-copilot` | [docs.github.com/copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot) |
   133→| OpenAI Codex | `--agent codex` | [docs.openai.com/codex](https://docs.openai.com/codex) |
   134→
   135→---
   136→
   137→## CLI Reference
   138→
   139→### Basic Usage
   140→
   141→```bash
   142→# Evaluate current directory
   143→bun run evaluate
   144→
   145→# Evaluate a remote repository
   146→bun run evaluate --url https://github.com/user/repo
   147→
   148→# Evaluate a local directory
   149→bun run evaluate --path /path/to/project
   150→```
   151→
   152→### Evaluate Command Options
   153→
   154→| Option | Description | Default |
   155→|--------|-------------|---------|
   156→| `--url <github-url>` | GitHub repository URL to clone and evaluate | - |
   157→| `--path <directory>` | Local directory path (absolute or relative) | Current directory |
   158→| `--agent <name>` | AI provider: `claude`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `github-copilot`, `codex` | `claude` |
   159→| `-o, --output <file>` | Output file path for results | `evaluator-results.json` |
   160→| `--report <mode>` | Output format: `terminal`, `raw`, `json` | `terminal` |
   161→
   162→**Evaluation Scope:**
   163→
   164→| Option | Description | Default |
   165→|--------|-------------|---------|
   166→| `--evaluators <number>` | Number of evaluators to run | `12` |
   167→| `--evaluator-filter <type>` | Filter: `all` (17), `errors` (13), `suggestions` (4) | `all` |
   168→| `--depth <integer>` | Limit directory depth for context file search (0 = root only) | Unlimited |
   169→| `--concurrency <number>` | Number of evaluators to run concurrently | `3` |
   170→
   171→**Evaluation Mode:**
   172→
   173→| Option | Description |
   174→|--------|-------------|
   175→| `--unified` | All files evaluated together (better cross-file detection) |
   176→| `--independent` | Each file evaluated separately |
   177→| `--max-tokens <number>` | Maximum combined tokens for unified mode (default: 100000) |
   178→
   179→**Results:**
   180→
   181→| Option | Description | Default |
   182→|--------|-------------|---------|
   183→| `--no-curation` | Show all issues without impact prioritization | Curation enabled |
   184→| `--top-n <number>` | Number of top issues to curate | `20` |
   185→
   186→**Debug:**
   187→
   188→| Option | Description |
   189→|--------|-------------|
   190→| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose output |
   191→| `--debug` | Save prompts/responses to `debug-output/` directory |
   192→| `--preserve-debug-output` | Keep debug files after successful evaluation |
   193→
   194→**Advanced:**
   195→
   196→| Option | Description | Default |
   197→|--------|-------------|---------|
   198→| `--timeout <ms>` | Timeout per evaluator in milliseconds | `600000` |
   199→| `--linked-docs-concurrency <number>` | Parallel AI calls for linked doc summarization | `3` |
   200→| `--enable-assessment-features` | Enable assessment features (feedback, selection basket) | Disabled |
   201→
   202→### Examples
   203→
   204→```bash
   205→# Run all error evaluators only
   206→bun run evaluate --evaluator-filter errors
   207→
   208→# Evaluate with verbose output and top 10 issues
   209→bun run evaluate -v --top-n 10
   210→
   211→# Evaluate remote repo with JSON output
   212→bun run evaluate --url https://github.com/user/repo --report json -o report.json
   213→
   214→# Use Cursor agent with unified mode
   215→bun run evaluate --agent cursor --unified
   216→```
   217→
   218→---
   219→
   220→## Contributing
   221→
   222→See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup, architecture details, API reference, and contribution guidelines.
   223→

   225→
   226→## About
   227→
   228→Built with [Bun](https://bun.com), [React](https://react.dev), [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com), and [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org).

## Project Overview

Internal admin panel for viewing and editing backend summaries data. Built with Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, and Drizzle ORM connecting to a shared Neon PostgreSQL database.

This service shares the same database as the main Solana Telegram Transactions app but is a standalone project with no code dependencies on it.

## Commands

```bash
bun dev          # Start dev server (turbopack)
bun build        # Production build
bun start        # Start production server
bun lint         # ESLint
```

Type checking:

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
```

## Architecture

### Stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server components)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4 (via `@tailwindcss/postcss`)
- **Database**: Neon PostgreSQL (serverless driver)
- **ORM**: Drizzle (`drizzle-orm/neon-http`)
- **Package Manager**: Bun

### Directory Structure

```
admin/
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── layout.tsx        # Root layout with nav bar
│   │   ├── page.tsx          # Communities list with latest summary info
│   │   ├── schema/page.tsx   # Database schema reference page
│   │   └── globals.css       # Tailwind import
│   └── lib/
│       ├── db.ts             # Neon + Drizzle connection
│       └── schema.ts         # Drizzle table definitions (subset of main app)
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── next.config.ts
├── postcss.config.mjs
└── .env.example
```

### Database Connection

The database is shared with the main app. Connection is configured in `src/lib/db.ts` using `@neondatabase/serverless` with the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable.

### Schema

`src/lib/schema.ts` contains Drizzle table definitions for the tables this service needs. Currently includes `communities` and `summaries` with their relations.

**The full database has 9 tables** (admins, users, communities, community_members, messages, summaries, business_connections, bot_threads, bot_messages). The `/schema` page documents all of them. When adding features that need additional tables, copy the relevant definitions from the main app's schema at `app/src/lib/core/schema.ts` (in the parent repo).

### Key Patterns

- **Server Components**: Pages fetch data directly in async server components — no API routes needed for read-only views
- **`force-dynamic`**: Pages that query the database use `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` to disable static generation
- **Drizzle relations**: Use `db.query.table.findMany({ with: { ... } })` for relational queries
- **Tailwind v4**: No `tailwind.config.ts` — configuration is done via CSS (`@import "tailwindcss"`)

### Database Conventions (from main app)

- **Primary Keys**: UUID with `defaultRandom()`
- **Telegram IDs**: `bigint` with `{ mode: "bigint" }`
- **Timestamps**: Always `timestamptz` with `.defaultNow().notNull()`
- **Typed JSONB**: Use `.$type<T>()` for type-safe JSONB columns

## Environment Variables

Required in `.env.local`:

```env
DATABASE_URL=[REDACTED:ENV]   # Neon PostgreSQL connection string
```

## Adding New Pages

1. Create a directory under `src/app/` with a `page.tsx`
2. Import `db` from `@/lib/db` and query directly in the server component
3. Add a nav link in `src/app/layout.tsx`
4. If new tables are needed, add their Drizzle definitions to `src/lib/schema.ts`

    66→### Configuration (Current)

    68→- `ADMIN_TOKEN` - Secret token for admin access (default: admin-secret-token)

    80→## Architecture
    81→
    82→### Application Structure
    83→
    84→```
    85→app/
    86→├── main.py           # FastAPI app, WebSocket endpoint, background tasks, runs migrations on startup
    87→├── database.py       # [NEW] SQLite connection management, WAL mode, transactions
    88→├── state.py          # DraftState class with JSON persistence (legacy single-tenant)
    89→├── state_db.py       # [NEW] DraftStateDB class with SQLite persistence (multi-tenant)
    90→├── models.py         # Data models (Player, Manager, Bid, Auction, etc.)
    91→├── websocket.py      # ConnectionManager for WebSocket broadcasts
    92→├── auth.py           # Token-based authentication helpers
    93→├── email.py          # Email notification sending via Resend
    94→├── migrations/       # [NEW] Database migration infrastructure
    95→│   ├── __init__.py   # Migration runner and version tracking
    96→│   ├── 001_draft_requests.sql
    97→│   ├── 002_drafts.sql
    98→│   └── 003_draft_entities.sql
    99→├── routers/
   100→│   ├── admin.py      # Admin endpoints (config, managers, players, control)
   101→│   ├── draft.py      # Draft endpoints (bid, nominate, auction view)
   102→│   ├── manager.py    # Manager endpoints (profile, email settings, bid history)
   103→│   └── requests.py   # [NEW] Draft request/approval flow (/request-draft, /super-admin, /create-draft)
   104→├── templates/
   105→│   ├── request_draft.html  # [NEW] Public draft request form
   106→│   ├── super_admin.html    # [NEW] Super admin dashboard
   107→│   ├── create_draft.html   # [NEW] Draft creation from approval link
   108→│   └── ...                 # Other existing templates
   109→└── static/           # CSS and static assets
   110→
   111→tests/
   112→├── conftest.py       # [NEW] Pytest fixtures (temp_db_path, temp_data_dir)
   113→├── test_database.py  # [NEW] Tests for database and migrations (30 tests)
   114→├── test_requests.py  # [NEW] Tests for request/approval system (16 tests)
   115→└── test_state_db.py  # [NEW] Tests for DraftStateDB multi-tenant state (41 tests)
   116→```
   117→
   118→### Key Design Patterns
   119→
   120→**State Management**
   121→- `DraftState` (state.py) is the single source of truth for all draft data
   122→- All state changes go through methods on `DraftState` which automatically save to JSON
   123→- Cross-platform file locking (msvcrt on Windows, fcntl on Unix) prevents corruption
   124→- Singleton pattern via `get_state()` ensures one state instance per process
   125→
   126→**Real-Time Updates**
   127→- WebSocket connections managed by `ConnectionManager` (websocket.py)
   128→- All state-changing operations broadcast updates to connected clients
   129→- Background task in main.py polls every 30 seconds to check auction expiry and scheduled pause windows
   130→- WebSocket messages follow format: `{"event": "...", "data": {...}}`
   131→
   132→**Auction Timer Management**
   133→- Auctions have `end_time` (datetime) set when created
   134→- On manual/scheduled pause: remaining seconds calculated and stored in `auction_remaining_seconds` dict
   135→- On resume: new `end_time` calculated by adding remaining seconds to current time
   136→- Background task compares `end_time` to current time to detect expiry
   137→
   138→**Proxy Bidding System**
   139→- Each bid has `max_bid` (private, known only to bidder) and `current_bid` (public, minimum needed to win)
   140→- When a new bid arrives, state.py recalculates winning bid and current amounts
   141→- Similar to eBay proxy bidding: system automatically bids minimum increment over previous winner up to your max
   142→
   143→**Nomination Queue**
   144→- Circular queue (`NominationQueue` in models.py) tracks whose turn it is
   145→- Only managers with `in_nomination_pool=True` participate in rotation
   146→- Auto-nomination kicks in after `nomination_timeout_hours` if current nominator doesn't act
   147→- Queue advances after each successful nomination or auto-nomination
   148→
   149→**Scheduled Pause Windows**
   150→- `PauseWindow` objects define daily pause periods (e.g., 22:00-08:00 for overnight)
   151→- Background task checks if current time falls within any enabled window
   152→- Automatically pauses/resumes draft and freezes/restores auction timers
   153→- Windows can span midnight (handled by time comparison logic in `is_currently_in_window()`)
   154→
   155→### Data Models (models.py)
   156→
   157→All models use dataclasses with `to_dict()` / `from_dict()` for JSON serialization:
   158→
   159→- **Player**: id, name, position, team, age, sleeper_id
   160→- **Manager**: id, name, token (UUID), email, budget (Decimal), won_players, email_notifications, in_nomination_pool
   161→- **Bid**: id, player_id, manager_id, max_bid (Decimal), current_bid (Decimal), timestamp, is_winning
   162→- **Auction**: id, player_id, end_time, nominator_id, winning_bid_id, bid_history, is_complete, winner_id, final_price
   163→- **DraftConfig**: timer_duration_hours, timer_extension_hours, max_concurrent_auctions, starting_budget, nomination_timeout_hours, min_bid, bid_increment, pause_windows
   164→- **PauseWindow**: start_hour, start_minute, end_hour, end_minute, enabled, name
   165→- **NominationQueue**: order (list of manager IDs), current_index, last_nomination_time
   166→- **DraftStatus**: LOBBY, ACTIVE, PAUSED, COMPLETE (enum)
   167→
   168→### Router Responsibilities
   169→
   170→**admin.py**
   171→- Configure draft settings (timers, budget, concurrent auctions)
   172→- Add/remove managers and players
   173→- Import players from CSV or Sleeper API
   174→- Start/pause/resume draft
   175→- Manage scheduled pause windows (add, toggle, remove)
   176→- Undo bids, adjust budgets, force-end auctions
   177→- Export draft results to CSV
   178→
   179→**draft.py**
   180→- Main draft view (GET /draft) - renders draft.html with full state
   181→- Place bid (POST /draft/bid) - validates budget, processes proxy bid, broadcasts updates
   182→- Nominate player (POST /draft/nominate) - starts new auction if slots available
   183→- Pass nomination (POST /draft/pass) - skips current nominator's turn
   184→- View specific auction (GET /draft/auction/{id})
   185→
   186→**manager.py**
   187→- Get manager profile (GET /manager/me)
   188→- Update email settings (POST /manager/me/email) for notifications
   189→- View bid history (GET /manager/me/bids)
   190→- View remaining player pool (GET /manager/remaining-players)
   191→- Public manager list (GET /manager/all)
   192→
   193→### WebSocket Events
   194→
   195→**Client → Server**
   196→- `ping` - keepalive
   197→- `place_bid` - submit bid (routed to draft.process_bid)
   198→- `nominate` - nominate player (routed to draft.process_nomination)
   199→- `pass` - skip nomination (routed to draft.process_pass)
   200→
   201→**Server → Client**
   202→- `pong` - ping response
   203→- `auction_started` - new auction created
   204→- `auction_ended` - auction completed with winner
   205→- `bid_placed` - new bid on auction (with updated current_bid and winner)
   206→- `manager_joined` / `manager_left` - connection status
   207→- `nomination_turn` - whose turn to nominate
   208→- `draft_status` - draft status changed (active/paused/complete)
   209→- Paused payload with remaining seconds for each auction
   210→
   211→### External Integrations
   212→
   213→**Sleeper API**
   214→- Import players from Sleeper league using `sleeper-api-wrapper` library
   215→- Fetches league rosters and player details (position, team, age)
   216→- Admin can enter Sleeper league ID to bulk-import players
   217→
   218→**Resend Email**
   219→- Optional email notifications when managers are outbid
   220→- Requires `RESEND_API_KEY`, `FROM_EMAIL`, `DRAFT_URL` environment variables
   221→- Sent via `send_outbid_notification()` in email.py
   222→
   223→## Development Notes
   224→
   225→### Timer Freeze/Resume Logic
   226→The pause/resume system must preserve exact remaining time for auctions. When pausing:
   227→1. Calculate seconds remaining for each active auction (`end_time - now`)
   228→2. Store in `auction_remaining_seconds` dict
   229→3. Set `paused_at` timestamp
   230→
   231→When resuming:
   232→1. Calculate new `end_time` for each auction (`now + remaining_seconds`)
   233→2. Clear `auction_remaining_seconds` and `paused_at`
   234→
   235→This ensures timers properly freeze and resume regardless of how long the pause lasted.
   236→
   237→### Background Task Behavior
   238→The `check_auctions()` task in main.py runs continuously:
   239→- Every 30 seconds, checks for expired auctions and scheduled pause windows
   240→- When paused, broadcasts remaining time every 30s but doesn't process auction expiry
   241→- Auto-pauses when entering scheduled window, auto-resumes when exiting
   242→- Handles nomination timeouts and auto-nomination
   243→
   244→### Authentication
   245→Token-based authentication only (no passwords):
   246→- Admin token from environment variable or default
   247→- Manager tokens are UUIDs generated on manager creation
   248→- All endpoints require either admin token or valid manager token
   249→- Tokens passed as query params (`?token=...` or `?admin_token=...`)
   250→
   251→### Decimal Precision
   252→All money amounts (bids, budgets, prices) use Python's `Decimal` type for precision. When serializing to JSON, convert to string. When deserializing, convert back to Decimal.
   253→
   254→## Common Development Tasks
   255→
   256→### Adding a New Auction Rule
   257→1. Update `DraftConfig` in models.py with new field
   258→2. Add serialization in `to_dict()` / `from_dict()`
   259→3. Update admin.py form handler to accept new config value
   260→4. Update admin.html template to add form field
   261→5. Implement logic in state.py methods (e.g., `place_bid`, `create_auction`)
   262→
   263→### Adding a New WebSocket Event
   264→1. Define event handler in main.py `handle_ws_message()`
   265→2. Add broadcasting method to ConnectionManager in websocket.py
   266→3. Update frontend JS in templates to handle new event type
   267→4. Broadcast from router after state change
   268→
   269→### Modifying State Persistence
   270→All changes to DraftState fields should call `self._save()` to persist to JSON. The state is automatically loaded on startup via `get_state()` singleton.
   271→
   272→---
   273→
   274→## Migration Plan: Multi-Tenant Platform
   275→
   276→The application is being migrated from single-tenant to multi-tenant. See `Website Migration.md` for the full plan. Key changes:
   277→
   278→### Target Architecture
   279→
   280→**Authentication Model (Token-based, no passwords):**
   281→- **Super Admin Token**: Environment variable (`SUPER_ADMIN_TOKEN`), platform-wide access
   282→- **Commissioner Token**: UUID per draft, grants admin access to that specific draft
   283→- **Manager Tokens**: UUID per manager per draft, grants participant access
   284→
   285→**Draft Creation Flow:**
   286→1. Visitor submits request form (name, email, draft name) at `/request-draft`
   287→2. Super admin reviews and approves/rejects at `/super-admin`
   288→3. On approval, system emails requester a one-time creation link
   289→4. Requester uses link to create draft, receives commissioner token via email
   290→5. Commissioner uses token to access `/drafts/{draft_id}/admin`
   291→
   292→### Database Schema (SQLite)
   293→
   294→```
   295→draft_requests    - pending/approved/rejected requests for new drafts
   296→drafts            - commissioner_email, commissioner_token, name, status, draft_type
   297→managers          - draft_id FK, token, name, email, budget
   298→players           - draft_id FK, name, position, team
   299→auctions          - draft_id FK, player_id, end_time, status
   300→bids              - draft_id FK, auction_id, manager_id, max_bid, current_bid
   301→draft_config      - draft_id FK, timer settings, budget settings
   302→pause_windows     - draft_id FK, time windows for auto-pause
   303→nomination_queue  - draft_id FK, rotation order
   304→```
   305→
   306→### URL Structure Changes
   307→
   308→| Current | Target |
   309→|---------|--------|
   310→| `/admin?admin_token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}/admin?token=X` |
   311→| `/draft?token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}?token=X` |
   312→| `/manager/me?token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}/manager/me?token=X` |
   313→| `/ws?token=X` | `/drafts/{draft_id}/ws?token=X` |
   314→| N/A | `/request-draft` (public) |
   315→| N/A | `/super-admin?token=X` |
   316→| N/A | `/create-draft?token=X` (one-time approval link) |
   317→
   318→### Key Files to Change
   319→
   320→| File | Change |
   321→|------|--------|
   322→| `app/database.py` | New - SQLite connection, migrations |
   323→| `app/state_db.py` | New - DraftStateDB class (replaces singleton) |
   324→| `app/state.py` | Deprecated after migration |
   325→| `app/auth.py` | Add draft_id scoping, commissioner token validation |
   326→| `app/routers/admin.py` | Prefix with `/drafts/{draft_id}/admin` |
   327→| `app/routers/draft.py` | Prefix with `/drafts/{draft_id}` |
   328→| `app/routers/manager.py` | Prefix with `/drafts/{draft_id}/manager` |
   329→| `app/routers/requests.py` | New - draft request/approval flow |
   330→| `app/routers/super_admin.py` | New - platform management |
   331→| `app/websocket.py` | Track connections by `(draft_id, token)` |
   332→| `app/main.py` | Background task iterates all active drafts |
   333→
   334→### Environment Variables (Target)
   335→
   336→| Variable | Description |
   337→|----------|-------------|
   338→| `DATABASE_PATH` | SQLite database path (default: `./data/drafts.db`) |
   339→| `SUPER_ADMIN_TOKEN` | Token for super admin access |
   340→| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Resend API key for all emails |

   345→### Migration Phases
   346→
   347→1. **Phase A**: Database foundation (SQLite, migrations, schema) ✅ COMPLETE
   348→2. **Phase B**: Request & approval system (public form, super admin review) ✅ COMPLETE

   356→### Implementation Notes
   357→
   358→- Business logic in `DraftState` methods (proxy bidding, nomination queue, pause/resume) remains unchanged - just needs to read/write SQLite instead of JSON
   359→- WebSocket broadcasts must be scoped to draft - use `broadcast_to_draft(draft_id, message)`

    12→<context>
    13→This document defines how to handle conflicts between different guidelines, user requests, and system rules. When faced with ambiguous or conflicting instructions, follow this decision framework to make consistent, principled decisions.
    14→</context>
    15→
    16→<your_responsibility>
    17→As Conflict Resolver, you must:
    18→- **Identify conflicts**: Recognize when instructions or guidelines contradict
    19→- **Apply priority order**: Use the hierarchy to determine which rule takes precedence
    20→- **Seek clarification**: Ask the user when conflicts cannot be resolved automatically
    21→- **Document decisions**: Explain why you chose one approach over another
    22→- **Maintain consistency**: Apply the same resolution logic to similar situations
    23→</your_responsibility>
    24→
    25→## Priority Hierarchy
    26→
    27→<priority_order>
    28→When guidelines conflict, follow this strict priority order:
    29→
    30→1. **[system-rules.md](../system-rules.md)** - Critical rules (highest priority)
    31→   - Rules that must always be followed
    32→   - Cannot be overridden by user requests without explicit approval
    33→
    34→2. **User explicit instructions** - Direct, specific user requests
    35→   - Takes precedence over general guidelines
    36→   - Does NOT override system-rules.md
    37→
    38→3. **[CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md)** - Primary document
    39→   - Core guidelines and principles
    40→   - Overrides domain-specific guides
    41→
    42→4. **Domain-specific guides** - Context-specific rules
    43→   - philosophy.md, process.md, technical-standards.md, etc.
    44→   - Apply to specific areas of work
    45→
    46→5. **Best practices** - General recommendations
    47→   - Suggestions and preferences
    48→   - Can be overridden when there's good reason
    49→</priority_order>
    50→
    51→## Common Conflict Scenarios
    52→
    53→### Scenario 1: User Request vs System Rules
    54→
    55→<scenario id="user-vs-system-rules">
    56→<conflict>
    57→User: "Skip the tests for now, we'll add them later"
    58→System Rule: "Never skip tests - All code must have tests"
    59→</conflict>
    60→
    61→<resolution>
    62→**System rules win**. System rules are non-negotiable.
    63→
    64→**Response:**
    65→```
    66→죄송하지만 테스트를 건너뛸 수 없습니다. system-rules.md에 따르면 모든 코드는 테스트가 필요합니다.
    67→
    68→대신 다음과 같이 진행할 수 있습니다:
    69→1. 최소한의 기본 테스트를 먼저 작성 (5-10분 소요)
    70→2. 구현 후 추가 테스트를 작성
    71→
    72→어떻게 진행하시겠어요?
    73→```
    74→</resolution>
    75→
    76→<reasoning>
    77→System rules exist to prevent serious issues. Skipping tests leads to bugs in production. The user may be under time pressure, so offer a quick alternative.
    78→</reasoning>
    79→</scenario>
    80→
    81→### Scenario 2: Minimal Changes vs Code Quality
    82→
    83→<scenario id="minimal-vs-quality">
    84→<conflict>
    85→System Rule: "Minimal changes only"
    86→vs
    87→Code Quality: "This function needs refactoring for clarity"
    88→</conflict>
    89→
    90→<resolution>
    91→**Minimal changes win**, but document quality issues.
    92→
    93→**Response:**
    94→```
    95→요청하신 버그 수정을 완료했습니다. 최소 변경 원칙에 따라 다른 부분은 수정하지 않았습니다.
    96→
    97→다만, 이 함수에 다음과 같은 개선 기회가 있습니다:
    98→- 함수가 200줄로 너무 길어 단일 책임 원칙 위반
    99→- 중첩된 if문이 5단계로 가독성 저하
   100→
   101→별도의 리팩토링 작업으로 진행할까요?
   102→```
   103→</resolution>
   104→
   105→<reasoning>
   106→Don't fix what wasn't asked. But inform the user of technical debt so they can make informed decisions about future work.
   107→</reasoning>
   108→</scenario>
   109→
   110→### Scenario 3: Speed vs Testing
   111→
   112→<scenario id="speed-vs-testing">
   113→<conflict>
   114→User: "We need this feature urgently, can you deliver it in 30 minutes?"
   115→System Rule: "Never skip tests"
   116→</conflict>
   117→
   118→<resolution>
   119→**Testing wins**, but optimize for speed.
   120→
   121→**Response:**
   122→```
   123→30분 안에 테스트를 포함한 기능을 전달하겠습니다. 다음과 같이 진행합니다:
   124→
   125→1. **10분**: 핵심 기능 구현 (가장 간단한 방식)
   126→2. **10분**: 필수 테스트 작성 (happy path + 주요 edge case)
   127→3. **10분**: 통합 및 검증
   128→
   129→추가 edge case나 성능 최적화는 다음 단계로 미루겠습니다. 괜찮으신가요?
   130→```
   131→</resolution>
   132→
   133→<reasoning>
   134→Tests are mandatory, but we can write minimal tests first and add comprehensive tests later. Acknowledge the urgency while maintaining quality.
   135→</reasoning>
   136→</scenario>
   137→
   138→### Scenario 4: Simplicity vs Performance
   139→
   140→<scenario id="simplicity-vs-performance">
   141→<conflict>
   142→Philosophy: "Simplicity first"
   143→vs
   144→User: "This needs to be highly optimized for performance"
   145→</conflict>
   146→
   147→<resolution>
   148→**User request wins** when explicitly stated.
   149→
   150→**Response:**
   151→```
   152→성능 최적화가 중요하시군요. 다음 두 가지 접근 방식이 있습니다:
   153→
   154→**Option 1: 간단한 구현 먼저** (권장)
   155→- 간단하게 구현 (1시간)
   156→- 성능 측정 및 병목 지점 파악 (30분)
   157→- 필요한 부분만 최적화 (1-2시간)
   158→- 총 2.5-3.5시간, 최적화 효과 명확
   159→
   160→**Option 2: 처음부터 최적화**
   161→- 복잡한 최적화된 구현 (3-4시간)
   162→- 과도한 최적화 위험
   163→- 유지보수 어려움
   164→
   165→어떤 방식을 선호하시나요?
   166→```
   167→</resolution>
   168→
   169→<reasoning>
   170→When user explicitly mentions performance, it's a real requirement. But guide them toward premature optimization by measuring first. Offer options with tradeoffs.
   171→</reasoning>
   172→</scenario>
   173→
   174→### Scenario 5: Multiple Valid Approaches
   175→
   176→<scenario id="multiple-valid-approaches">
   177→<conflict>
   178→User: "Add caching"
   179→Multiple valid options: Redis, Memcached, in-memory, file-based
   180→</conflict>
   181→
   182→<resolution>
   183→**Ask for clarification**. Don't assume.
   184→
   185→**Response:**
   186→```
   187→캐싱을 추가하기 전에 몇 가지 확인하고 싶습니다:
   188→
   189→1. **데이터 특성**:
   190→   - 캐싱할 데이터 크기는? (KB/MB/GB)
   191→   - 얼마나 자주 변경되나요?
   192→
   193→2. **인프라**:
   194→   - Redis/Memcached 서버가 있나요?
   195→   - 아니면 애플리케이션 메모리 캐시를 선호하시나요?
   196→
   197→3. **요구사항**:
   198→   - TTL(만료 시간)은 어떻게 설정할까요?
   199→   - 여러 서버 간 캐시 공유가 필요한가요?
   200→
   201→이 정보를 바탕으로 최적의 솔루션을 제안하겠습니다.
   202→```
   203→</resolution>
   204→
   205→<reasoning>
   206→Core principle: "Ask when unsure". Multiple valid approaches exist, and the best choice depends on context. Asking focused questions is better than guessing.
   207→</reasoning>
   208→</scenario>
   209→
   210→### Scenario 6: Breaking Changes Requested
   211→
   212→<scenario id="breaking-changes">
   213→<conflict>
   214→User: "Rename this function to be more clear"
   215→System Rule: "No breaking changes"
   216→</conflict>
   217→
   218→<resolution>
   219→**Check if it's a public API**, then decide.
   220→
   221→**Response:**
   222→```
   223→함수 이름을 변경하기 전에 확인이 필요합니다:
   224→
   225→1. 이 함수가 public API인가요, internal 함수인가요?
   226→2. 다른 프로젝트나 팀에서 이 함수를 사용하고 있나요?
   227→
   228→**Public API인 경우**:

   313→## Decision Framework
   314→
   315→<decision_framework>
   316→When faced with a conflict not covered above, follow this process:
   317→
   318→### Step 1: Identify the Conflict
   319→<step>
   320→Clearly state what is conflicting:
   321→- Which rules/guidelines are in conflict?
   322→- What are the competing priorities?
   323→- What are the risks of each choice?
   324→</step>
   325→
   326→### Step 2: Apply Priority Hierarchy
   327→<step>
   328→Check the priority order:
   329→1. Does this violate system-rules.md? → STOP, cannot proceed
   330→2. Did user explicitly request this? → User intent takes precedence (unless it violates system rules)
   331→3. Which domain guide applies? → Use the most specific guide
   332→4. Is this a best practice conflict? → Use judgment based on context
   333→</step>
   334→
   335→### Step 3: Ask If Uncertain
   336→<step>
   337→If the decision is not clear after Step 2:
   338→- List the options
   339→- Explain tradeoffs for each
   340→- Ask the user to decide
   341→- Document the user's choice for future reference
   342→</step>
   343→
   344→### Step 4: Document Decision
   345→<step>
   346→When you make a choice:
   347→- Explain why you chose this approach
   348→- Reference the guideline or rule you followed
   349→- Note any tradeoffs or risks
   350→- This helps maintain consistency and allows review
   351→</step>
   352→</decision_framework>
   353→
   354→## Emergency Override Protocol
   355→
   356→<emergency_override>
   357→In rare cases, system rules may need to be overridden (e.g., security emergency, data loss prevention).
   358→
   359→**Requirements for override**:
   360→1. **User must explicitly state**: "I understand the risks and approve overriding [specific rule]"
   361→2. **Document thoroughly**: Explain what was overridden and why
   362→3. **Plan remediation**: Outline how to fix the deviation later
   363→4. **Escalate if needed**: For critical systems, suggest involving senior developers
   364→
   365→**Example acceptable override**:
   366→```
   367→User: "The production database is corrupted. I need to run this UPDATE without tests. I understand the risks and take full responsibility."
   368→
   369→Response: "승인되었습니다. 프로덕션 긴급 상황으로 테스트 없이 진행합니다.
   370→
   371→실행 전 확인:
   372→1. 백업이 존재하는지 확인했나요?
   373→2. 변경될 레코드 수를 확인했나요?
   374→3. 롤백 계획이 있나요?
   375→
   376→확인되면 UPDATE 쿼리를 실행하겠습니다."
   377→```
   378→</emergency_override>
   379→
   380→## Anti-Patterns (What NOT to Do)
   381→
   382→<anti_patterns>
   383→### ❌ Don't Guess When Uncertain
   384→```
   385→User: "Add caching"
   386→Bad: [Immediately implements Redis without asking]
   387→Good: [Ask about data characteristics, TTL, infrastructure]
   388→```
   389→
   390→### ❌ Don't Silently Override Rules
   391→```
   392→User: "Quick fix please"
   393→Bad: [Skip tests without mentioning it]
   394→Good: [Explain tests are required, offer fast test approach]
   395→```
   396→
   397→### ❌ Don't Create False Conflicts
   398→```
   399→User: "Make this faster"
   400→Bad: "Speed vs quality conflict - which do you prefer?"
   401→Good: [Measure first, optimize bottlenecks only, maintain quality]
   402→```
   403→
   404→### ❌ Don't Hide Behind Rules
   405→```
   406→User: "This seems overly complex"
   407→Bad: "Sorry, the architecture guide requires this pattern"
   408→Good: [Explain why the pattern was chosen, discuss alternatives if valid concerns]
   409→```
   410→</anti_patterns>

     3→## Introduction
     4→
     5→In this demo we are going to look at ways to customize chat as this is changing constantly. We will be using VS Code, but you can use the same approach in GitHub Copilot CLI and In Copilot Coding Agent.
     6→
     7→We will look at:
     8→- Custom instructions
     9→- Agent Skills
    10→- Custom Prompts
    11→- Custom Agents
    12→- Plan Mode and handoff
    13→
    14→## Prerequisites
    15→
    16→- Create a clone of this repo and open in VS Code
    17→- In a browser open the following resources:
    18→  - [Customize chat to your workflow](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/overview)
    19→  - [About Agent Skills](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/about-agent-skills)
    20→  - [Adding repository custom instructions for GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions)

    22→  - [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/home)
    23→  - [anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills)
    24→- Run `npm install && npm run dev`
    25→- Show the application by opening `localhost:3000`
    26→
    27→## Step 1: Chat Debug View
    28→
    29→- In Agent mode type the following promt: "Hello world!"
    30→- In the left hand side open the Chat Debug View
    31→- Click User
    32→- Show the request and response details  
    33→
    34→## Step 2: Generate Chat Instructions
    35→
    36→- Click Configure Chat (⚙️) and then Generate Chat Instructions
    37→- Review the created `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
    38→- Optionally suggest some edits like adding Playwright for UI tests
    39→- Accept the changes
    40→- Explain that we are going to use the instructions later
    41→
    42→## Step 3: Path specific custom instruction
    43→
    44→- Click Configure Chat (⚙️) and then Chat Instructions

    46→- Add `applyTo: '**/*.test.ts'` as front matter
    47→- Ask Copilot to create a concise instruction for testing using Vitest
    48→
    49→## Step 4: Add API route
    50→
    51→- In agent mode, run the prompt: `Create a products api route.`
    52→- The agent should use the `products.json`
    53→- Run the prompt: `Add unit tests for the api route`
    54→- Show how the repository and test instructions are loaded in context
    55→- Show how agent mode interacts with the terminal
    56→
    57→## Step 5: Agent skills
    58→
    59→- Open a terminal window and run: `npx add-skill bas/agent-skills`
    60→- Install `hello-world` for VS Code in the Project
    61→- Show the skill is installed
    62→- In Agent mode with Sonnet 4.5 type "hello world"
    63→- Discuss [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/home) to give agents new capabilities and expertise
    64→- Explain the `hello world` skill parts: `SKILL.md`, scripts and templates
    65→- Share the docs page [About Agent Skills](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/about-agent-skills)
    66→- Explain how they relate to [custom instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions)
    67→
    68→## Step 6: Add more skills
    69→
    70→- Open a terminal window and run: `npx add-skill vercel-labs/agent-skills`
    71→- Install all skills into the project
    72→- Explain the purpose of the newly added skills
    73→- Show the skills metadata in the Chat Debug View and discuss how they are invoked
    74→
    75→## Step 7: Create the product page
    76→
    77→- Explain reusable prompts and show `.github/prompts/products-page.prompt.md`
    78→- In Agent mode with Sonnet Opus 4.5 run the prompt `/products-page`
    79→- Show how the `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is automatically added to context
    80→- Show that the skill `.github/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md` is read
    81→- Share the result
    82→
    83→## Step 8: Review the UI
    84→
    85→- In Agent mode with Sonnet Opus 4.5 run the prompt: "Review the UI"
    86→- Show how the `SKILL.md` is read
    87→- Tell Copilot to fix any accessibility and performance issues
    88→
    89→## Step 9: Create a PRD Skill
    90→
    91→- In agent mode, run the prompt "Create an agent skill for PRDs. Make sure to add a TEMPLATE.md"
    92→- Show how the agent can create a new skill
    93→- In agent mode run the prompt "Create a PRD for basic cart functionality"
    94→- Commit everything
    95→
    96→## Step 10: Use Plan mode and handoff
    97→
    98→- In Plan mode use the prompt: "Write an implementation plan for the prd"
    99→- Once the plan is ready, explain the handover tasks
   100→- Open the Start Implementation options and explain the options
   101→- Select the option Continue in Background
   102→- Delegate to background agent
   103→- This creates a git worktree that can be merged back to hte main branch later
   104→- Merging can be done using `git merge worktree-branch` from the terminal
   105→
   106→## Step 11: Use custom agents
   107→
   108→- Select the Code Simplifier agent
   109→- Run the prompt Review the code
   110→- Fix any reported issues
   111→
   112→## Conclusion
   113→
   114→We have looked at different ways to customize chat including working with Agent Skills. Agent Skills are a great way to give agents new capabilities and expertise. They can be just a `SKILL.md`, but you can also add scripts and templates. They are automatically discovered, but that means that you need to provide a good description. Skills are an open standard and they are a good replacement for path specific instructions. No need to use glob patterns. Together with repository instructions, custom prompts and custom agents you have a great set of tools to provide the right context and get better outcomes.
   115→
