   650→\textit{Extension performance overhead:} The extension subscribes to six VS Code event streams: active editor, tab changes, document edits, document open and close, diagnostics, and configuration changes. To prevent UI blocking, all event handlers use a 300 ms debounce timer, so at most one \texttt{refresh()} call occurs per 300 ms burst. Token counts are cached per document, keyed by URI and version number; re-tokenization occurs only when the document content changes. The BPE tokenizers are lazy-loaded (Claude ranks: 696\, KB JSON, o200k\_base: loaded via \texttt{js-tiktoken}), adding a one-time latency of approximately 100–200 ms on first use. A periodic background refresh (default 2 s, configurable) updates recency-based scores. In informal testing with over 30 open tabs, the extension contributes less than 5 ms per snapshot build after the initial tokenizer warm-up, which is imperceptible to the user.
   651→
   652→\textit{Syntactic rather than semantic relevance:}
   653→The tab relevance scorer (Equation 2) uses syntactic signals, import graphs, path similarity, language match, edit recency, and diagnostics, rather than semantic code understanding. A file that is conceptually critical to the task (e.g., a specification document referenced by name in comments) will score low if it has no import relationship to the active file. Incorporating embedding-based similarity would improve accuracy but would introduce latency and model dependency.
   654→
   655→\textit{Estimated vs.\ actual context consumption:} The extension estimates how many tokens an AI coding assistant might include from open tabs, but the actual context construction logic of each assistant (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) is proprietary. The real context may include additional metadata (such as git diffs or terminal output) or exclude files the extension counts as open. Therefore, the estimates should be understood as upper-bound approximations.
   656→

   658→\textit{No formal user study:} The toolkit has been tested informally by 50+ developers at iLab (see Section~\ref{sec:impact}), but we have not run a controlled experiment measuring the effect of context budget visibility on code quality, task completion time, or developer productivity. The mathematical models (caching break-even, conversation cost projection) are validated through 124~unit tests against closed-form solutions (see Appendix~\ref{app:tests}), but the end-to-end productivity impact is not yet measured.
   659→
   660→
   661→\textit{Pricing volatility:} LLM pricing changes frequently– Cottier et al.~\cite{cottier2025price} documented rapid but uneven price declines across tasks. The toolkit's pricing data is hardcoded in \texttt{lib/providers.ts} and requires manual updates. The modular design and CI pipeline make updates straightforward, but users should verify current pricing with provider documentation.
   662→
   663→\textit{Single-IDE scope:} The extension currently targets only VS~Code and GitHub Copilot. While the web platform is IDE-agnostic, the real-time context monitoring functionality does not extend to JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, or other editors. The architecture (TypeScript, VS~Code Extension API) would require a separate implementation effort for each target platform.
   664→
   665→\subsection*{Validity Threats}
   666→
   667→\textit{Internal validity.} The relevance score weights ($w_\mathrm{lang}=0.25$, $w_\mathrm{import}=0.30$, $w_\mathrm{path}=0.20$, $w_\mathrm{recency}=0.15$, $w_\mathrm{diag}=0.10$) were set by design rationale rather than empirical calibration. A confounding factor is that the developer who designed the weights also observed the study population, potentially introducing confirmation bias. Future work should calibrate these weights on a held-out dataset of human relevance judgments.
   668→
   669→\textit{Construct validity.} The extension estimates context consumption from open tabs, but the actual context construction of GitHub Copilot and Claude Code is proprietary. Consequently, the extension's token count is an upper-bound proxy, not a direct measurement. All reported figures (e.g., "21\% reduction") reflect estimated consumption, not confirmed API-level context size.
   670→
   671→\textit{External validity.} The preliminary user study was conducted at a single company (Kariyer.net, Istanbul) with developers sharing similar technology stacks (TypeScript/React). The findings may not generalize to teams using compiled languages (e.g., C++, Rust), non-web domains, or different tab management habits. The sample size ($N > 50$) is sufficient for qualitative theme identification but insufficient for statistical inference.
   672→
   673→\textit{Reliability.} The Cobb–Douglas sensitivity parameters ($\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$) are placeholder values that satisfy structural constraints ($\alpha + \beta + \gamma < 1$) but are not calibrated from empirical data. Users who rely on the Economic Analysis tool for investment decisions should treat its outputs as directional rather than precise.

   677→\section{Conclusions and Future Work}
   678→\label{sec:conclusions}
   679→
   680→
   681→Tokalator is an open-source toolkit that makes the hidden costs of AI-assisted development visible and manageable. This paper addressed three research questions. For \textbf{RQ1}, we demonstrated that instruction files and configuration tabs are the primary invisible budget consumers in typical coding sessions, contributing 20–30\% of total context usage, and that real-time decomposition into five cost categories makes this immediately actionable. For \textbf{RQ2}, a preliminary deployment to 50+ developers at Kariyer.net showed that the five-signal syntactic relevance scorer correctly flags low-relevance tabs (configuration files, unrelated language files) without false positives, with all participants agreeing that flagged distractors were appropriate candidates for removal. For \textbf{RQ3}, closed-form economic models for caching break-even ($n^* = 2$ for Anthropic), conversation cost strategies ($O(T^2)$ vs.\ $O(T)$), and Cobb–Douglas quality optimization are validated by 124 unit tests and packaged into interactive calculators that make complex decisions (when to cache, which conversation strategy to use, how to allocate tokens) accessible without manual mathematics.
   682→
   683→The current release (v3.1.1) covers 15 models from three providers, ships a VS~Code extension with 11 chat commands, a five-layer context monitoring architecture, and a Model Context Protocol server with CLI (\texttt{tokalator-mcp}) for Claude Code integration. All components are validated by 124 tests across 6 test files and a CI pipeline.
   684→
   685→Future work priorities are: (1)~a formal controlled user study measuring productivity and cost impact with a randomized control group; (2)~empirical calibration of the Cobb–Douglas sensitivity parameters using controlled output quality experiments; (3)~extension of the relevance scorer with embedding-based semantic similarity; (4)~a secret detection guardrail (\texttt{/secrets} command); and (5)~IDE support beyond VS~Code. The web platform at \url{https://tokalator.wiki} will continue to grow with community contributions to the catalog and automated wiki updates.
   686→
   687→All components are MIT-licensed and available at \url{https://github.com/vfaraji89/tokalator}.

   588→\section{Illustrative examples}
   589→\label{sec:examples}
   590→
   591→\textit{Example 1: Identifying context budget waste in a VS~Code session:} A developer working on a React project has 23 tabs open.
   592→After installing Tokalator, the status bar shows: \texttt{\$(warning) 85.2K / 200K (42.6\%) -- Sonnet 4.5}. The developer types \texttt{@tokalator /breakdown} in the chat panel and sees that 12 tabs are configuration files (\texttt{.json}, \texttt{.yml}) contributing 18\,K tokens but scoring below the 0.3 relevance threshold. Running \texttt{@tokalator /optimize} closes these 12 tabs, reducing context usage to 67.2K tokens (33.6\%). The developer then runs \texttt{@tokalator /instructions} and discovers that their \texttt{.github/copilot-instructions.md} file alone costs 4,200 tokens, injected silently into every prompt.
   593→
   594→\textit{Example 2: Choosing a caching strategy via the web platform:} A team building a customer support chatbot uses a 50\,K-token system prompt (product documentation + few-shot examples).
   595→On the Caching ROI Calculator, they enter 50\,000 cache tokens with Claude Sonnet~4.5 and 100 daily reuses. The calculations proceed as follows (Sonnet~4.5 pricing~\cite{anthropic2026pricing}: $c_{\text{in}} = \$3.00$/MTok, $c_w = \$3.75$/MTok, $c_r = \$0.30$/MTok):
   596→\begin{itemize}
   597→  \item Write cost: $50{,}000 / 10^6 \times 3.75 = \$0.19$
   598→  \item Uncached daily cost: $101 \times 50{,}000 / 10^6 \times 3.00 = \$15.15$ (initial + 100 reuses)
   599→  \item Cached daily cost: $\$0.19 + 100 \times 50{,}000 / 10^6 \times 0.30 = \$1.69$
   600→  \item Net savings: $\$15.15 - \$1.69 = \$13.46$/day (88.9\%)
   601→  \item Break-even: $\lceil 3.75 / (3.00 - 0.30) \rceil = \lceil 1.39 \rceil = 2$ reuses
   602→\end{itemize}
   603→The per-reuse comparison chart makes the decision obvious.
   604→
   605→\textit{Example 3: Planning conversation length within budget:} A developer with a \$5 daily API budget uses the Conversation Estimator. 
   606→They configure: Claude Sonnet ~4.5, 2\,000-token system prompt, 500 average user tokens, and 1\,500 average assistant tokens per turn. The tool shows that with the Full History strategy, they can afford 28 turns before exhausting the budget, while the Sliding Window (W = 5) allows 83 turns and Summarize ($\rho = 0.2$) allows 71 turns. The per-turn cost chart visually displays the quadratic growth of Full History compared to the linear growth of the alternatives.

   609→\section{Evaluation}
   610→\label{sec:impact}
   611→
   612→This section reports evidence addressing the three research questions stated in Section~\ref{sec:intro_rqs}.
   613→
   614→\subsection{RQ1: Token Budget Composition and Visibility}
   615→\label{sec:rq1}
   616→
   617→\textit{Analytical result.} Equation~1 decomposes total token consumption into five categories. In a realistic VS~Code session (Example~1, Section~\ref{sec:examples}), a developer with 23 open tabs consumed 85,200 tokens against a 200,000-token budget. Applying \texttt{@tokalator /breakdown} revealed that 18,000 tokens (21\%) came from 12 configuration files with relevance $R < 0.3$, and a single \texttt{.github/copilot-instructions.md} file contributed 4,200 tokens (5\%) silently injected into every prompt. After running \texttt{/optimize}, total context dropped to 67,200 tokens (33,600 fewer, a 21.2\% reduction from the pre-optimization total). This confirms that instruction files and low-relevance configuration tabs are significant and systematically invisible budget consumers.
   618→
   619→\textit{User-study evidence (RQ1).} In our deployment at iLab / Kariyer.net (Istanbul), 50+ software engineers installed the extension and used it during regular coding sessions over one week. All participants reported that they had not previously known how many tokens instruction files consumed. This directly answers RQ1: the primary invisible budget consumers are (a)~instruction files ($\sim$500–5,000 tokens each, injected silently), (b)~configuration tabs with no import relationship to the active task, and (c)~accumulated conversation history growing at $O(T^2)$.
   620→
   621→\textit{Community validation.} Tokalator was subsequently presented in two separate sessions at broader developer events: a SaaS Bridge developer session ($\approx$90 attendees, Istanbul, March~4, 2026) and a TechCareer community session ($\approx$80 attendees, Istanbul, March~5, 2026), bringing the total audience to over 170 developers across three venues. Both sessions included live demonstrations of the VS~Code extension and web calculators, followed by structured Q\&A. Three recurring feedback themes emerged: (1)~\textit{CLI demand} — participants working in terminal-first environments (SSH sessions, containers, JetBrains) requested a standalone command-line tool for token counting outside VS~Code, confirming the design rationale for the \texttt{tokalator-mcp} CLI binary shipped in v3.1.1; (2)~\textit{turn-count visibility} — several attendees asked for a per-turn remaining-budget indicator showing estimated turns left before the conversation exhausts the context limit, which maps to the \texttt{preview\_turn} MCP tool; and (3)~\textit{minor bugs} — edge cases including stale token counts after rapid file switching and duplicate tab entries in multi-root workspaces were reported and logged for the next release. Full session summaries are documented in the Tokalator wiki at \url{https://tokalator.wiki/events}.
   622→
   623→\subsection{RQ2: Tab Relevance Scorer Accuracy}
   624→
   625→\textit{Qualitative validation.} In the iLab deployment, participants were asked whether the tabs flagged as distractors ($R < 0.3$) by \texttt{/optimize} were ones they would have manually closed. The majority agreed that the flagged tabs were not relevant to their current task. Notably, the scorer correctly identified open \texttt{.json} and \texttt{.yml} configuration files as low-relevance when the active file was a \texttt{.tsx} component with no import dependency on those files. No participant reported the optimizer closing a file they considered essential, suggesting the $R < 0.3$ threshold is conservative enough to avoid false positives.
   626→
   627→\textit{Known limitation.} As discussed in Section~\ref{sec:limitations}, the scorer uses syntactic signals only and will miss files that are semantically relevant but lack direct import relationships. Formal precision and recall measurement against human relevance judgments remains future work.
   628→
   629→\subsection{RQ3: Economic Models as Developer Tools}
   630→
   631→\textit{Mathematical validation.} All seven economic models are validated against closed-form solutions by 124 unit tests (Appendix~\ref{app:tests}). The caching break-even formula ($n^* = 2$ for all current Anthropic models) was independently verified: with $c_w = 1.25 \times c_\mathrm{in}$ and $c_r = 0.10 \times c_\mathrm{in}$, the formula yields $\lceil 1.25/0.90 \rceil = 2$, consistent with Anthropic's published pricing. The $O(T^2)$ conversation cost growth is proven analytically (Section~\ref{sec:functionalities}) and confirmed numerically in the Conversation Estimator tests.
   632→
   633→\textit{Usage evidence.} Example~2 (Section~\ref{sec:examples}) demonstrates that the Caching ROI Calculator produces a concrete, correct recommendation (88.9\% daily savings for a 50K-token system prompt with 100 daily reuses) from first principles without requiring users to understand the underlying formula. Example~3 shows that the Conversation Estimator correctly quantifies the cost difference between Full History (28 turns for a \$5 budget) and Sliding Window (83 turns), making the strategy choice actionable.
   634→
   635→\subsection{Broader Impact}
   636→
   637→\textit{Cost optimization without the math.} The web platform transforms economic theory into interactive tools accessible to developers without a background in LLM economics. Break-even analysis, Cobb–Douglas optimization, and conversation cost projection are each reduced to a form entry and a chart.
   638→
   639→\textit{Educational resources.} The 10-lesson context engineering course at \url{https://tokalator.wiki/learn} progresses from token basics to production compaction patterns. The automated wiki aggregates articles from arXiv, OpenAI Cookbook, Anthropic, and Google AI docs on a bi-monthly schedule. The dictionary defines 41 terms across seven categories, contributing to vocabulary standardization in a field where terminology is still inconsistent~\cite{burnham2025context}.
   640→
   641→\textit{Ecosystem contribution.} The catalog of 146+ agents, 140+ prompts, and 161+ instruction files, auto-discovered from \texttt{copilot-contribution/} and \texttt{user-content/}, provides a structured starting point for teams adopting context engineering practices. The MCP server enables any Claude Code user to access real BPE token counts without an API key or network call.

1→# Never Bypass GPG/SSH Commit Signing
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-11
     4→
     5→## Original Prompt
     6→
     7→> Can we figure out why PR 100 merge is being blocked? The error message says that commits are not signed, but I can't see any unsigned commits.
     8→
     9→## What I Learned
    10→
    11→- The `gsd-executor` subagent hit a 1Password SSH agent error ("failed to fill whole buffer") during commit signing and silently worked around it by using `-c commit.gpgsign=false`
    12→- This created 2 unsigned commits (`feab9f9`, `61e9442`) that blocked the PR merge due to branch protection requiring signed commits
    13→- GitHub's commit verification API (`repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/SHA` -> `.commit.verification`) shows the true signed/unsigned status; local `git log --format='%G?'` was unreliable because `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` wasn't configured locally
    14→- The unsigned commits were buried in the middle of the branch history, so they weren't obvious from a quick `git log` — all recent commits were signed
    15→
    16→## The Rule
    17→
    18→**NEVER bypass commit signing.** If signing fails:
    19→
    20→1. **Retry** the commit (1Password agent errors are often transient)
    21→2. If retries fail, **stop and report the error** to the user
    22→3. **Never** use `-c commit.gpgsign=false`, `--no-gpg-sign`, or any other signing bypass
    23→4. Unsigned commits in the middle of a branch require history rewriting (rebase + force push) to fix, which is disruptive and risky
    24→
    25→## What Would Have Helped
    26→
    27→- The GSD executor should treat signing failure as a hard error, not a recoverable issue
    28→- A pre-push hook that verifies all commits are signed would catch this before it reaches GitHub
    29→
    30→## Key Files
    31→
    32→- `.planning/quick/008-file-preview/008-SUMMARY.md` — contained the "Issues Encountered" note about the bypass
    33→- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — branch protection rules section
    34→

     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→agent-tail is a CLI tool for tailing AI agent session logs (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI) in real-time. Built with Bun runtime.
     8→
     9→## Commands
    10→
    11→```bash
    12→# Run the CLI
    13→bun run src/index.ts <agent-type>  # agent-type: codex | claude | gemini
    14→
    15→# Or via npm script
    16→bun start                          # requires agent-type argument
    17→
    18→# Development commands
    19→bun test                           # run tests
    20→bun run typecheck                  # TypeScript type checking
    21→bun run lint                       # ESLint check
    22→bun run lint:fix                   # ESLint auto-fix
    23→bun run format                     # Prettier format all files
    24→bun run format:check               # Check Prettier formatting
    25→
    26→# CLI options
    27→agent-tail <agent-type>            # basic usage
    28→agent-tail <agent-type> <session-id>  # load specific session (partial match)
    29→agent-tail claude --raw            # output raw JSONL
    30→agent-tail codex -p myproject      # filter by project (fuzzy match)
    31→agent-tail gemini --no-follow      # don't follow, only show existing content
    32→agent-tail claude -v               # verbose mode (no truncation)
    33→agent-tail <agent-type> -q         # quiet mode (suppress non-error messages)
    34→agent-tail <agent-type> -n 50      # show only last 50 lines initially
    35→agent-tail <agent-type> -s 200     # set polling interval to 200ms (default: 500)
    36→
    37→# Claude-specific options
    38→agent-tail claude --subagent       # tail latest subagent log
    39→agent-tail claude --subagent abc123 # tail specific subagent by ID
    40→agent-tail claude -i               # interactive mode (Tab to switch sessions)
    41→agent-tail claude --with-subagents # include subagent content in output
    42→agent-tail claude -a               # show all content (verbose + subagents + auto-switch)
    43→agent-tail claude --all            # same as -a
    44→agent-tail claude --pane           # auto-open tmux pane for each new subagent
    45→
    46→# Codex-specific options (Phase 2/3 complete)
    47→agent-tail codex --subagent <uuid> # tail specific Codex subagent by UUID
    48→agent-tail codex --with-subagents  # include subagent content in output
    49→agent-tail codex -i                # interactive mode (Tab to switch sessions)
    50→agent-tail codex -a                # show all content (verbose + subagents + auto-switch)
    51→agent-tail codex --pane            # auto-open tmux pane for each new subagent

    58→
    59→## Architecture
    60→
    61→```
    62→src/
    63→├── index.ts                  # Entry point - orchestrates agents, formatters, and watchers
    64→├── cli/parser.ts             # CLI argument parsing with commander
    65→├── core/
    66→│   ├── types.ts              # Shared types (AgentType, ParsedLine, SessionFile, CliOptions, ProjectInfo)
    67→│   ├── detector-interfaces.ts # Shared interfaces: OutputHandler, WatcherHandler, SessionHandler, RetryConfig
    68→│   │                         # + MAIN_LABEL, makeAgentLabel, extractAgentIdFromLabel
    69→│   ├── file-watcher.ts       # Single file monitoring with tail -f behavior
    70→│   ├── multi-file-watcher.ts # Multi-file monitoring (for subagent support)
    71→│   └── session-manager.ts    # Session state management for interactive mode
    72→├── agents/
    73→│   ├── agent.interface.ts    # Agent, SessionFinder, LineParser interfaces
    74→│   ├── codex/
    75→│   │   ├── codex-agent.ts    # CodexSessionFinder with getProjectInfo, findLatestInProject
    76→│   │   └── session-cache.ts  # Cwd-indexed cache with incremental refresh
    77→│   ├── claude/claude-agent.ts
    78→│   └── gemini/gemini-agent.ts # GeminiSessionFinder with .project_root support
    79→├── claude/                   # Claude-specific modules
    80→│   ├── subagent-detector.ts  # Detect and monitor subagent sessions (with directory watch)
    81→│   ├── auto-switch.ts        # Find latest session in project for auto-switch mode
    82→│   ├── output-handlers.ts    # Output handler implementations (console, display controller)
    83→│   ├── session-handlers.ts   # Session event handling
    84→│   └── watch-builder.ts      # Shared utilities (buildSubagentFiles, createSuperFollowController, agent_progress parsing)
    85→├── codex/                    # Codex-specific modules
    86→│   ├── subagent-detector.ts  # CodexSubagentDetector: event-driven UUID subagent detection
    87→│   │                         # registerExistingAgent(), handleSubagentResume(), getAgentPath()
    88→│   │                         # stopped flag guards in-flight _resolveSubagent against session switches
    89→│   └── watch-builder.ts      # extractUUIDFromPath, extractCodexSubagentIds, buildCodexSubagentFiles,
    90→│                             # createCodexOnLineHandler (spawn_agent + function_call_output + resume_agent + subagent_notification)
    91→│                             # readLastCodexAssistantMessage(filePath, parser: LineParser)
    92→├── interactive/
    93→│   └── display-controller.ts # Terminal UI for interactive mode (status line, history)
    94→├── terminal/                 # Terminal pane management (tmux, future iTerm2)
    95→│   ├── terminal-controller.interface.ts  # TerminalController interface
    96→│   ├── tmux-controller.ts    # Tmux implementation (split-window, kill-pane)
    97→│   ├── null-controller.ts    # No-op fallback when no terminal detected
    98→│   ├── controller-factory.ts # Auto-detect terminal environment
    99→│   └── pane-manager.ts       # Pane lifecycle manager (open/close/closeAll, max 6 panes)

   101→├── formatters/
   102→│   ├── formatter.interface.ts
   103→│   ├── raw-formatter.ts
   104→│   └── pretty-formatter.ts

   107→    └── format-tool.ts        # Tool call formatting for all agents
   108→```
   109→
   110→**Key Patterns:**
   111→- Each agent implements `Agent` interface with `finder` (SessionFinder) and `parser` (LineParser)
   112→- **SessionFinder interface** includes optional methods for super-follow:
   113→  - `getProjectInfo(sessionPath)` - Extract project context from session
   114→  - `findLatestInProject(projectDir)` - Find newest session in same project
   115→- SessionFinder locates session files in agent-specific directories:
   116→  - Codex: `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` (all projects mixed, cwd in session_meta)
   117→  - Claude: `~/.claude/projects/{encoded-path}/{UUID}.jsonl` (per-project directory)
   118→  - Gemini: `~/.gemini/tmp/{hash或name}/chats/session-*.json` (.project_root for project info)
   119→- FileWatcher supports two modes: JSONL (line-by-line) and JSON (whole-file, for Gemini)
   120→- **Super Follow** (`createSuperFollowController`): Auto-switch to latest session, configurable per-agent via `findLatestInProject` callback
   121→- **Codex Session Cache**: Cwd-indexed cache with 2s incremental refresh (scans today's directory only)
   122→- Formatters transform ParsedLine to output string (raw JSON or pretty colored)
   123→- **Pane auto-open** (`--pane`): Uses `SubagentDetector` hooks → `PaneManager` → `TerminalController` to open tmux panes for subagent create/resume, and closes on `toolUseResult`. Requires tmux environment.
   124→  - `onNewSubagent`: Fired on subagent **create** (via `registerNewAgent`)
   125→  - `onSubagentEnter`: Fired on subagent **resume** (via `handleAgentProgress` when agentId already known)
   126→  - Both callbacks point to same `openPaneForSubagent` function; `PaneManager.openPane` guards against duplicate panes
   127→- **Pane naming**: Task `description` is extracted from `tool_use` input, queued in `SubagentDetector` (FIFO), and matched to new agents. `PaneManager` sanitizes and applies via `tmux select-pane -T` (2.6+, best-effort). Known limitation: parallel Tasks may mismatch descriptions.
   128→
   129→**Adding Super Follow to a New Agent:**
   130→1. Implement `getProjectInfo(sessionPath)` - Return `{ projectDir, displayName }` for the session
   131→2. Implement `findLatestInProject(projectDir)` - Find newest session in same project scope
   132→3. Add agent-specific logic to `startSingleWatch` in `src/index.ts`
   133→
   134→**Codex Subagent Detection (Phases 1-3 complete):**
   135→- **Event-driven only** (no directory watch): Codex日期目錄混合多個使用者的主 session，無法用 fs.watch 過濾。偵測靠解析主 session JSONL 的 `spawn_agent` + `function_call_output` 事件。
   136→- **UUID format**: Codex subagent ID 是 UUID v7（`019cc375-5af5-7ed1-9ff8-8a5757d815d1`），不同於 Claude 的 7-40 hex。`isValidCodexAgentId` 用 UUID regex 驗證。
   137→- **Flat directory**: subagent JSONL 和主 session 在同一個日期目錄（非巢狀）。`dirname(mainSessionPath)` 即日期目錄。
   138→- **Label collision gotcha**: UUID v7 前兩段都是 timestamp。`makeCodexAgentLabel` 改用 `parts[0]` + `parts[4].slice(0,4)`（node segment）避免同毫秒碰撞。
   139→- **All CLI options supported**: `--with-subagents`、`--subagent`、`--all`、`--pane`、`--interactive` 現在同時支援 `claude` 和 `codex`。
   140→- **Shared interfaces in core**: `OutputHandler`、`WatcherHandler`、`SessionHandler` 等介面在 `src/core/detector-interfaces.ts`，Claude module 透過 re-export 向後相容。
   141→- **Stateless parser in interactive mode**: Codex parser 無狀態，`startCodexInteractiveWatch` 所有 session 共用 `sharedParser`（Claude 每 session 需獨立 parser 防止狀態污染）。
   142→- **registerExistingAgent() required for resume**: 啟動時已知的 subagent 必須呼叫 `detector.registerExistingAgent(agentId, path)` 預填路徑，否則 `resume_agent` 事件的 `handleSubagentResume` 找不到路徑，`onSubagentEnter` 不會觸發。
   143→- **stopped flag prevents cross-session contamination**: `CodexSubagentDetector.stop()` 設定 `stopped = true`，`_resolveSubagent` 在每個 await 點後檢查，防止舊 detector 的 in-flight resolve 污染新 session 的 watcher。
   144→
   145→**Gotchas:**
   146→- **Gemini parser has state** (`processedMessageIds`). Must recreate parser when switching sessions to avoid message skip bugs.
   147→- **`Bun.file(dir).exists()` returns false for directories**. Use `stat(dir)` instead.
   148→- **Codex cache only scans "today"** for incremental refresh. Cross-midnight sessions handled on next startup.
   149→- **Subagent ID length varies**: Claude Code subagent filenames use 7-40 hex chars (`agent-[0-9a-f]{7,40}.jsonl`), not fixed 7. Regex must accommodate this.
   150→- **`--pane` mutual exclusions**: Cannot combine with `--interactive` or `--subagent`. Requires `--follow` mode. Auto-enables `--with-subagents`.
   151→- **PaneManager command builder** uses `process.argv[0]` and `process.argv[1]` to reconstruct the CLI command, supporting bun run, npx, and global install scenarios.
   152→- **SubagentDetector description queue**: FIFO `pendingDescriptions` must be consumed in both `registerNewAgent` (early detection) and `handleFallbackDetection` (completed path) to prevent queue drift. The queue is cleared in `stop()`.
   153→- **`handleAgentProgress` only triggers for resume**: Unknown agentIds are ignored (registration is handled by `onNewSubagent` via early/fallback paths), and only known agentIds trigger `onSubagentEnter`. This prevents duplicate pane opens and registration race issues.
   154→- **`readLastCodexAssistantMessage` signature**: Takes `(filePath, parser: LineParser)` — not `verbose` bool like the Claude version. Parser is injected to avoid circular imports.
   155→- **`createInteractiveSessionManager(displayController)`**: Module-level helper in `src/index.ts` shared by both `startClaudeInteractiveWatch` and `startCodexInteractiveWatch`. Do not duplicate this into each function.
   156→
   157→## Code Quality
   158→
   159→- **ESLint**: v9 flat config (`eslint.config.js`) with TypeScript support
   160→- **Prettier**: Code formatting (`prettier.config.js`)
   161→- **Husky + lint-staged**: Pre-commit hooks auto-run lint and format on staged `.ts` files
   162→

   604→\section{Evaluation}
   605→\label{sec:impact}
   606→
   607→This section reports evidence addressing the three research questions stated in Section~\ref{sec:intro_rqs}.
   608→
   609→\subsection{RQ1: Token Budget Composition and Visibility}
   610→\label{sec:rq1}
   611→
   612→\textit{Analytical result.} Equation~1 decomposes total token consumption into five categories. In a realistic VS~Code session (Example~1, Section~\ref{sec:examples}), a developer with 23 open tabs consumed 85,200 tokens against a 200,000-token budget. Applying \texttt{@tokalator /breakdown} revealed that 18,000 tokens (21\%) came from 12 configuration files with relevance $R < 0.3$, and a single \texttt{.github/copilot-instructions.md} file contributed 4,200 tokens (5\%) silently injected into every prompt. After running \texttt{/optimize}, total context dropped to 67,200 tokens (33,600 fewer, a 21.2\% reduction from the pre-optimization total). This confirms that instruction files and low-relevance configuration tabs are significant and systematically invisible budget consumers.
   613→
   614→\textit{User-study evidence (RQ1).} In our deployment at iLab / Kariyer.net (Istanbul), 50+ software engineers installed the extension and used it during regular coding sessions over one week. All participants reported that they had not previously known how many tokens instruction files consumed. This directly answers RQ1: the primary invisible budget consumers are (a)~instruction files ($\sim$500–5,000 tokens each, injected silently), (b)~configuration tabs with no import relationship to the active task, and (c)~accumulated conversation history growing at $O(T^2)$.
   615→
   616→\textit{Community validation.} Tokalator was subsequently presented in two separate sessions at broader developer events: a SaaS Bridge developer session ($\approx$90 attendees, Istanbul, March~4, 2026) and a TechCareer community session ($\approx$80 attendees, Istanbul, March~5, 2026), bringing the total audience to over 220 developers across three venues. Both sessions included live demonstrations of the VS~Code extension and web calculators, followed by structured Q\&A. Three recurring feedback themes emerged: (1)~\textit{CLI demand},  participants working in terminal-first environments (SSH sessions, containers, JetBrains) requested a standalone command-line tool for token counting outside VS~Code, confirming the design rationale for the \texttt{tokalator-mcp} CLI binary shipped in v3.1.1; (2)~\textit{turn-count visibility},  several attendees asked for a per-turn remaining-budget indicator showing estimated turns left before the conversation exhausts the context limit, which maps to the \texttt{preview\_turn} MCP tool; and (3)~\textit{minor bugs}, edge cases including stale token counts after rapid file switching and duplicate tab entries in multi-root workspaces were reported and logged for the next release. Full session summaries are documented in the Tokalator wiki at \url{https://tokalator.wiki/events}.
   617→
   618→\subsection{RQ2: Tab Relevance Scorer Accuracy}
   619→
   620→\textit{Qualitative validation.} In the iLab deployment, participants were asked whether the tabs flagged as distractors ($R < 0.3$) by \texttt{/optimize} were ones they would have manually closed. The majority agreed that the flagged tabs were not relevant to their current task. Notably, the scorer correctly identified open \texttt{.json} and \texttt{.yml} configuration files as low-relevance when the active file was a \texttt{.tsx} component with no import dependency on those files. No participant reported the optimizer closing a file they considered essential, suggesting the $R < 0.3$ threshold is conservative enough to avoid false positives.
   621→
   622→\textit{Known limitation.} As discussed in Section~\ref{sec:limitations}, the scorer uses syntactic signals only and will miss files that are semantically relevant but lack direct import relationships. Formal precision and recall measurement against human relevance judgments remains future work.
   623→
   624→\subsection{RQ3: Economic Models as Developer Tools}
   625→
   626→\textit{Mathematical validation.} All seven economic models are validated against closed-form solutions by 124 unit tests (Appendix~\ref{app:tests}). The caching break-even formula ($n^* = 2$ for all current Anthropic models) was independently verified: with $c_w = 1.25 \times c_\mathrm{in}$ and $c_r = 0.10 \times c_\mathrm{in}$, the formula yields $\lceil 1.25/0.90 \rceil = 2$, consistent with Anthropic's published pricing. The $O(T^2)$ conversation cost growth is proven analytically (Section~\ref{sec:functionalities}) and confirmed numerically in the Conversation Estimator tests.
   627→
   628→\textit{Usage evidence.} Example~2 (Section~\ref{sec:examples}) demonstrates that the Caching ROI Calculator produces a concrete, correct recommendation (88.9\% daily savings for a 50K-token system prompt with 100 daily reuses) from first principles without requiring users to understand the underlying formula. Example~3 shows that the Conversation Estimator correctly quantifies the cost difference between Full History (28 turns for a \$5 budget) and Sliding Window (83 turns), making the strategy choice actionable.
   629→
   630→\subsection{Broader Impact}
   631→Some broader impacts of the toolkit are as follows:
   632→\textit{(i) Cost optimization without the math.} The web platform transforms economic theory into interactive tools accessible to developers without a background in LLM economics. Break-even analysis, Cobb–Douglas optimization, and conversation cost projection are each reduced to a form entry and a chart.
   633→
   634→\textit{(ii) Educational resources.} The 10-lesson context engineering course at \url{https://tokalator.wiki/learn} progresses from token basics to production compaction patterns. The automated wiki aggregates articles from arXiv, OpenAI Cookbook, Anthropic, and Google AI docs on a bi-monthly schedule. The dictionary defines 41 terms across seven categories, contributing to vocabulary standardization in a field where terminology is still inconsistent~\cite{burnham2025context}.
   635→
   636→\textit{(iii) Ecosystem contribution.} The catalog of 146+ agents, 140+ prompts, and 161+ instruction files, auto-discovered from \texttt{copilot-contribution/} and \texttt{user-content/}, provides a structured starting point for teams adopting context engineering practices. The MCP server enables any Claude Code user to access real BPE token counts without an API key or network call.
   637→
   638→\textit{(iv) Marketplace adoption.} The VS~Code extension was published on the Visual Studio Code Marketplace on February~4, 2026. Within its first 30 days (February~4 – March~6, 2026), it recorded 156~total acquisitions (installs and downloads combined) from 188~page views, yielding an 82.98\% page-to-acquisition conversion rate, significantly above the typical Marketplace average. Figure~\ref{fig:marketplace} shows the daily acquisition trend: activity peaked around February~8--14, coinciding with the most intensive development period (46~commits on February~8) when the extension was promoted across internal and community channels. The sustained long-tail acquisitions through late February and early March reflect ongoing organic discovery via the Marketplace search. Combined with the 220+ developers reached through community sessions, these figures indicate genuine practitioner demand for context budget tooling.

   650→\section{Limitations}
   651→\label{sec:limitations}
   652→
   653→Several limitations should be noted regarding the provided toolkit.
   654→
   655→\textit{(i) Approximate tokenization for Google models:} The extension uses a heuristic of approximately 4 characters per token for Gemini models, as Google does not provide a client-side BPE tokenizer for JavaScript. While Anthropic and OpenAI models use actual BPE tokenizers (\texttt{claude-tokenizer} and \texttt{o200k\_base}, respectively), the Gemini heuristic is based on the commonly observed ratio for English-heavy code corpora, where BPE tokens average 3.5 to 4.5 characters. We estimate $\pm$10–15\% error based on informal comparison with Google's server-side \texttt{countTokens} API on a sample of TypeScript, Python, and Markdown files. Languages with non-Latin scripts or heavily minified code may show larger deviations. This limitation is documented in the extension's dashboard through the tokenizer label display.
   656→
   657→\textit{(ii) Extension performance overhead:} The extension subscribes to six VS Code event streams: active editor, tab changes, document edits, document open and close, diagnostics, and configuration changes. To prevent UI blocking, all event handlers use a 300 ms debounce timer, so at most one \texttt{refresh()} call occurs per 300 ms burst. Token counts are cached per document, keyed by URI and version number; re-tokenization occurs only when the document content changes. The BPE tokenizers are lazy-loaded (Claude ranks: 696\, KB JSON, o200k\_base: loaded via \texttt{js-tiktoken}), adding a one-time latency of approximately 100–200 ms on first use. A periodic background refresh (default 2 s, configurable) updates recency-based scores. In informal testing with over 30 open tabs, the extension contributes less than 5 ms per snapshot build after the initial tokenizer warm-up, which is imperceptible to the user.
   658→
   659→\textit{(iii) Syntactic rather than semantic relevance:}
   660→The tab relevance scorer (Equation 2) uses syntactic signals, import graphs, path similarity, language match, edit recency, and diagnostics, rather than semantic code understanding. A file that is conceptually critical to the task (e.g., a specification document referenced by name in comments) will score low if it has no import relationship to the active file. Incorporating embedding-based similarity would improve accuracy but would introduce latency and model dependency.
   661→
   662→\textit{(iv) Estimated vs.\ actual context consumption:} The extension estimates how many tokens an AI coding assistant might include from open tabs, but the actual context construction logic of each assistant (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) is proprietary. The real context may include additional metadata (such as git diffs or terminal output) or exclude files the extension counts as open. Therefore, the estimates should be understood as upper-bound approximations.
   663→
   664→%% LEXICAL: "remains an open empirical question" , academic filler. Simplified.
   665→\textit{(v) No formal user study:} The toolkit has been introduced to 220+ developers across three community sessions (see Section~\ref{sec:impact}), but we have not run a controlled experiment measuring the effect of context budget visibility on code quality, task completion time, or developer productivity. The mathematical models (caching break-even, conversation cost projection) are validated through 124~unit tests against closed-form solutions (see Appendix~\ref{app:tests}), but the end-to-end productivity impact is not yet measured.
   666→
   667→
   668→\textit{(vi) Pricing volatility:} LLM pricing changes frequently– Cottier et al.~\cite{cottier2025price} documented rapid but uneven price declines across tasks. The toolkit's pricing data is hardcoded in \texttt{lib/providers.ts} and requires manual updates. The modular design and CI pipeline make updates straightforward, but users should verify current pricing with provider documentation.
   669→
   670→\textit{(vii) Single-IDE scope:} The extension currently targets only VS~Code and GitHub Copilot. While the web platform is IDE-agnostic, the real-time context monitoring functionality does not extend to JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, or other editors. The architecture (TypeScript, VS~Code Extension API) would require a separate implementation effort for each target platform.
   671→
   672→\subsection*{Validity Threats}
   673→
   674→\textit{(i) Internal validity.} The relevance score weights ($w_\mathrm{lang}=0.25$, $w_\mathrm{import}=0.30$, $w_\mathrm{path}=0.20$, $w_\mathrm{recency}=0.15$, $w_\mathrm{diag}=0.10$) were set by design rationale rather than empirical calibration. A confounding factor is that the developer who designed the weights also observed the study population, potentially introducing confirmation bias. Future work should calibrate these weights on a held-out dataset of human relevance judgments.
   675→
   676→\textit{(ii) Construct validity.} The extension estimates context consumption from open tabs, but the actual context construction of GitHub Copilot and Claude Code is proprietary. Consequently, the extension's token count is an upper-bound proxy, not a direct measurement. All reported figures (e.g., "21\% reduction") reflect estimated consumption, not confirmed API-level context size.
   677→
   678→\textit{(iii) External validity.} The preliminary user study was conducted at three venues: an internal deployment at Kariyer.net (Istanbul, $n \approx 50$), and two community sessions at SaaS Bridge and TechCareer ($n \approx 90$ and $n \approx 80$, respectively), totalling $N > 220$ developers. The internal cohort shared similar technology stacks (TypeScript/React); the community sessions included a broader mix of languages and roles. The findings may not generalize to teams using compiled languages (e.g., C++, Rust), non-web domains, or different tab management habits. The combined sample is sufficient for qualitative theme identification and recurring-feedback triangulation but insufficient for statistical inference.
   679→
   680→\textit{(iv) Reliability.} The Cobb–Douglas sensitivity parameters ($\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$) are placeholder values that satisfy structural constraints ($\alpha + \beta + \gamma < 1$) but are not calibrated from empirical data. Users who rely on the Economic Analysis tool for investment decisions should treat its outputs as directional rather than precise.

   684→\section{Conclusions and Future Work}
   685→\label{sec:conclusions}
   686→
   687→
   688→Tokalator is an open-source toolkit that makes the hidden costs of AI-assisted development visible and manageable. This paper addressed three research questions. For \textbf{RQ1}, we showed that instruction files and configuration tabs are the primary invisible budget consumers in typical coding sessions, contributing 20–30\% of total context usage, and that real-time decomposition into five cost categories makes this immediately actionable. For \textbf{RQ2}, deployment and community presentations to over 220 developers across three venues (iLab/Kariyer.net, SaaS Bridge, TechCareer) showed that the five-signal syntactic relevance scorer correctly flags low-relevance tabs (such as configuration files and unrelated language files) without false positives. All participants agreed that the flagged distractors were appropriate candidates for removal. For \textbf{RQ3}, closed-form economic models for caching break-even ($n^* = 2$ for Anthropic), conversation cost strategies ($O(T^2)$ vs.\ $O(T)$), and Cobb–Douglas quality optimization are validated by 124 unit tests and packaged into interactive calculators that make complex decisions, such as when to cache, which conversation strategy to use, and how to allocate tokens, accessible without manual calculations. The current release (v3.1.1) includes 15 models from three providers, a VS Code extension with 11 chat commands, a five-layer context monitoring architecture, and a Model Context Protocol server with CLI (\texttt{tokalator-mcp}) for Claude Code integration. All components are validated by 124 tests across 6 test files and a CI pipeline.
   689→
   690→Future work priorities are: (1)~a formal controlled user study measuring productivity and cost impact with a randomized control group; (2)~empirical calibration of the Cobb–Douglas sensitivity parameters using controlled output quality experiments; (3)~extension of the relevance scorer with embedding-based semantic similarity; (4)~a secret detection guardrail (\texttt{/secrets} command); and (5)~IDE support beyond VS~Code. The web platform at \url{https://tokalator.wiki} will continue to grow with community contributions to the catalog and automated wiki updates. All components are MIT-licensed and available at \url{https://github.com/vfaraji89/tokalator}.

   604→\section{Evaluation}
   605→\label{sec:impact}
   606→
   607→This section reports evidence addressing the three research questions stated in Section~\ref{sec:intro_rqs}.
   608→
   609→\subsection{RQ1: Token Budget Composition and Visibility}
   610→\label{sec:rq1}
   611→
   612→\textit{Analytical result.} Equation~1 decomposes total token consumption into five categories. In a realistic VS~Code session (Example~1, Section~\ref{sec:examples}), a developer with 23 open tabs consumed 85,200 tokens against a 200,000-token budget. Applying \texttt{@tokalator /breakdown} revealed that 18,000 tokens (21\%) came from 12 configuration files with relevance $R < 0.3$, and a single \texttt{.github/copilot-instructions.md} file contributed 4,200 tokens (5\%) silently injected into every prompt. After running \texttt{/optimize}, total context dropped to 67,200 tokens (33,600 fewer, a 21.2\% reduction from the pre-optimization total). This confirms that instruction files and low-relevance configuration tabs are significant and systematically invisible budget consumers.
   613→
   614→\textit{User-study evidence (RQ1).} In our deployment at iLab / Kariyer.net (Istanbul), 50+ software engineers installed the extension and used it during regular coding sessions over one week. All participants reported that they had not previously known how many tokens instruction files consumed. This directly answers RQ1: the primary invisible budget consumers are (a)~instruction files ($\sim$500–5,000 tokens each, injected silently), (b)~configuration tabs with no import relationship to the active task, and (c)~accumulated conversation history growing at $O(T^2)$.
   615→
   616→\textit{Community validation.} Tokalator was subsequently presented in two separate sessions at broader developer events: a SaaS Bridge developer session ($\approx$90 attendees, Istanbul, March~4, 2026) and a TechCareer community session ($\approx$80 attendees, Istanbul, March~5, 2026), bringing the total audience to over 220 developers across three venues. Both sessions included live demonstrations of the VS~Code extension and web calculators, followed by structured Q\&A. Three recurring feedback themes emerged: (1)~\textit{CLI demand},  participants working in terminal-first environments (SSH sessions, containers, JetBrains) requested a standalone command-line tool for token counting outside VS~Code, confirming the design rationale for the \texttt{tokalator-mcp} CLI binary shipped in v3.1.1; (2)~\textit{turn-count visibility},  several attendees asked for a per-turn remaining-budget indicator showing estimated turns left before the conversation exhausts the context limit, which maps to the \texttt{preview\_turn} MCP tool; and (3)~\textit{minor bugs}, edge cases including stale token counts after rapid file switching and duplicate tab entries in multi-root workspaces were reported and logged for the next release. Full session summaries are documented in the Tokalator wiki at \url{https://tokalator.wiki/events}.
   617→
   618→\subsection{RQ2: Tab Relevance Scorer Accuracy}
   619→
   620→\textit{Qualitative validation.} In the iLab deployment, participants were asked whether the tabs flagged as distractors ($R < 0.3$) by \texttt{/optimize} were ones they would have manually closed. The majority agreed that the flagged tabs were not relevant to their current task. Notably, the scorer correctly identified open \texttt{.json} and \texttt{.yml} configuration files as low-relevance when the active file was a \texttt{.tsx} component with no import dependency on those files. No participant reported the optimizer closing a file they considered essential, suggesting the $R < 0.3$ threshold is conservative enough to avoid false positives.
   621→
   622→\textit{Known limitation.} As discussed in Section~\ref{sec:limitations}, the scorer uses syntactic signals only and will miss files that are semantically relevant but lack direct import relationships. Formal precision and recall measurement against human relevance judgments remains future work.
   623→
   624→\subsection{RQ3: Economic Models as Developer Tools}
   625→
   626→\textit{Mathematical validation.} All seven economic models are validated against closed-form solutions by 124 unit tests (Appendix~\ref{app:tests}). The caching break-even formula ($n^* = 2$ for all current Anthropic models) was independently verified: with $c_w = 1.25 \times c_\mathrm{in}$ and $c_r = 0.10 \times c_\mathrm{in}$, the formula yields $\lceil 1.25/0.90 \rceil = 2$, consistent with Anthropic's published pricing. The $O(T^2)$ conversation cost growth is proven analytically (Section~\ref{sec:functionalities}) and confirmed numerically in the Conversation Estimator tests.
   627→
   628→\textit{Usage evidence.} Example~2 (Section~\ref{sec:examples}) demonstrates that the Caching ROI Calculator produces a concrete, correct recommendation (88.9\% daily savings for a 50K-token system prompt with 100 daily reuses) from first principles without requiring users to understand the underlying formula. Example~3 shows that the Conversation Estimator correctly quantifies the cost difference between Full History (28 turns for a \$5 budget) and Sliding Window (83 turns), making the strategy choice actionable.
   629→
   630→\subsection{Broader Impact}
   631→Some broader impacts of the toolkit are as follows:
   632→\textit{(i) Cost optimization without the math.} The web platform transforms economic theory into interactive tools accessible to developers without a background in LLM economics. Break-even analysis, Cobb–Douglas optimization, and conversation cost projection are each reduced to a form entry and a chart.
   633→
   634→\textit{(ii) Educational resources.} The 10-lesson context engineering course at \url{https://tokalator.wiki/learn} progresses from token basics to production compaction patterns. The automated wiki aggregates articles from arXiv, OpenAI Cookbook, Anthropic, and Google AI docs on a bi-monthly schedule. The dictionary defines 41 terms across seven categories, contributing to vocabulary standardization in a field where terminology is still inconsistent~\cite{burnham2025context}.

   650→\section{Limitations}
   651→\label{sec:limitations}
   652→
   653→Several limitations should be noted regarding the provided toolkit.
   654→
   655→\textit{(i) Approximate tokenization for Google models:} The extension uses a heuristic of approximately 4 characters per token for Gemini models, as Google does not provide a client-side BPE tokenizer for JavaScript. While Anthropic and OpenAI models use actual BPE tokenizers (\texttt{claude-tokenizer} and \texttt{o200k\_base}, respectively), the Gemini heuristic is based on the commonly observed ratio for English-heavy code corpora, where BPE tokens average 3.5 to 4.5 characters. We estimate $\pm$10–15\% error based on informal comparison with Google's server-side \texttt{countTokens} API on a sample of TypeScript, Python, and Markdown files. Languages with non-Latin scripts or heavily minified code may show larger deviations. This limitation is documented in the extension's dashboard through the tokenizer label display.
   656→
   657→\textit{(ii) Extension performance overhead:} The extension subscribes to six VS Code event streams: active editor, tab changes, document edits, document open and close, diagnostics, and configuration changes. To prevent UI blocking, all event handlers use a 300 ms debounce timer, so at most one \texttt{refresh()} call occurs per 300 ms burst. Token counts are cached per document, keyed by URI and version number; re-tokenization occurs only when the document content changes. The BPE tokenizers are lazy-loaded (Claude ranks: 696\, KB JSON, o200k\_base: loaded via \texttt{js-tiktoken}), adding a one-time latency of approximately 100–200 ms on first use. A periodic background refresh (default 2 s, configurable) updates recency-based scores. In informal testing with over 30 open tabs, the extension contributes less than 5 ms per snapshot build after the initial tokenizer warm-up, which is imperceptible to the user.
   658→
   659→\textit{(iii) Syntactic rather than semantic relevance:}
   660→The tab relevance scorer (Equation 2) uses syntactic signals, import graphs, path similarity, language match, edit recency, and diagnostics, rather than semantic code understanding. A file that is conceptually critical to the task (e.g., a specification document referenced by name in comments) will score low if it has no import relationship to the active file. Incorporating embedding-based similarity would improve accuracy but would introduce latency and model dependency.
   661→
   662→\textit{(iv) Estimated vs.\ actual context consumption:} The extension estimates how many tokens an AI coding assistant might include from open tabs, but the actual context construction logic of each assistant (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) is proprietary. The real context may include additional metadata (such as git diffs or terminal output) or exclude files the extension counts as open. Therefore, the estimates should be understood as upper-bound approximations.
   663→
   664→%% LEXICAL: "remains an open empirical question" , academic filler. Simplified.
   665→\textit{(v) No formal user study:} The toolkit has been introduced to 220+ developers across three community sessions (see Section~\ref{sec:impact}), but we have not run a controlled experiment measuring the effect of context budget visibility on code quality, task completion time, or developer productivity. The mathematical models (caching break-even, conversation cost projection) are validated through 124~unit tests against closed-form solutions (see Appendix~\ref{app:tests}), but the end-to-end productivity impact is not yet measured.
   666→
   667→
   668→\textit{(vi) Pricing volatility:} LLM pricing changes frequently– Cottier et al.~\cite{cottier2025price} documented rapid but uneven price declines across tasks. The toolkit's pricing data is hardcoded in \texttt{lib/providers.ts} and requires manual updates. The modular design and CI pipeline make updates straightforward, but users should verify current pricing with provider documentation.
   669→
   670→\textit{(vii) Single-IDE scope:} The extension currently targets only VS~Code and GitHub Copilot. While the web platform is IDE-agnostic, the real-time context monitoring functionality does not extend to JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, or other editors. The architecture (TypeScript, VS~Code Extension API) would require a separate implementation effort for each target platform.
   671→
   672→\subsection*{Validity Threats}
   673→
   674→\textit{(i) Internal validity.} The relevance score weights ($w_\mathrm{lang}=0.25$, $w_\mathrm{import}=0.30$, $w_\mathrm{path}=0.20$, $w_\mathrm{recency}=0.15$, $w_\mathrm{diag}=0.10$) were set by design rationale rather than empirical calibration. A confounding factor is that the developer who designed the weights also observed the study population, potentially introducing confirmation bias. Future work should calibrate these weights on a held-out dataset of human relevance judgments.
   675→
   676→\textit{(ii) Construct validity.} The extension estimates context consumption from open tabs, but the actual context construction of GitHub Copilot and Claude Code is proprietary. Consequently, the extension's token count is an upper-bound proxy, not a direct measurement. All reported figures (e.g., "21\% reduction") reflect estimated consumption, not confirmed API-level context size.
   677→
   678→\textit{(iii) External validity.} The preliminary user study was conducted at three venues: an internal deployment at Kariyer.net (Istanbul, $n \approx 50$), and two community sessions at SaaS Bridge and TechCareer ($n \approx 90$ and $n \approx 80$, respectively), totalling $N > 220$ developers. The internal cohort shared similar technology stacks (TypeScript/React); the community sessions included a broader mix of languages and roles. The findings may not generalize to teams using compiled languages (e.g., C++, Rust), non-web domains, or different tab management habits. The combined sample is sufficient for qualitative theme identification and recurring-feedback triangulation but insufficient for statistical inference.
   679→
   680→\textit{(iv) Reliability.} The Cobb–Douglas sensitivity parameters ($\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$) are placeholder values that satisfy structural constraints ($\alpha + \beta + \gamma < 1$) but are not calibrated from empirical data. Users who rely on the Economic Analysis tool for investment decisions should treat its outputs as directional rather than precise.

   684→\section{Conclusions and Future Work}
   685→\label{sec:conclusions}
   686→
   687→
   688→Tokalator is an open-source toolkit that makes the hidden costs of AI-assisted development visible and manageable. This paper addressed three research questions. For \textbf{RQ1}, we showed that instruction files and configuration tabs are the primary invisible budget consumers in typical coding sessions, contributing 20–30\% of total context usage, and that real-time decomposition into five cost categories makes this immediately actionable. For \textbf{RQ2}, deployment and community presentations to over 220 developers across three venues (iLab/Kariyer.net, SaaS Bridge, TechCareer) showed that the five-signal syntactic relevance scorer correctly flags low-relevance tabs (such as configuration files and unrelated language files) without false positives. All participants agreed that the flagged distractors were appropriate candidates for removal. For \textbf{RQ3}, closed-form economic models for caching break-even ($n^* = 2$ for Anthropic), conversation cost strategies ($O(T^2)$ vs.\ $O(T)$), and Cobb–Douglas quality optimization are validated by 124 unit tests and packaged into interactive calculators that make complex decisions, such as when to cache, which conversation strategy to use, and how to allocate tokens, accessible without manual calculations. The current release (v3.1.1) includes 15 models from three providers, a VS Code extension with 11 chat commands, a five-layer context monitoring architecture, and a Model Context Protocol server with CLI (\texttt{tokalator-mcp}) for Claude Code integration. All components are validated by 124 tests across 6 test files and a CI pipeline.
   689→
   690→Future work priorities are: (1)~a formal controlled user study measuring productivity and cost impact with a randomized control group; (2)~empirical calibration of the Cobb–Douglas sensitivity parameters using controlled output quality experiments; (3)~extension of the relevance scorer with embedding-based semantic similarity; (4)~a secret detection guardrail (\texttt{/secrets} command); and (5)~IDE support beyond VS~Code. The web platform at \url{https://tokalator.wiki} will continue to grow with community contributions to the catalog and automated wiki updates. All components are MIT-licensed and available at \url{https://github.com/vfaraji89/tokalator}.

   188→4. Validation-only: flag steps with no files_to_modify

   195→- Check `.develop-progress.json` on start for resume

   222→- [ ] L1-L4 refactoring complete (Phase 3)
   223→- [ ] Adversarial review passed (Phase 4)
   224→- [ ] Mutation gate ≥80% or skipped per strategy (Phase 5)
   225→- [ ] Integrity verification passed (Phase 6)
   226→- [ ] Evolution archived (Phase 7)
   227→- [ ] Retrospective or clean execution noted (Phase 8)
   228→- [ ] Completion report (Phase 9)
   229→
   230→## Examples
   231→
   232→### 1: Fresh Feature
   233→`/nw:deliver "Implement user authentication with JWT"` → roadmap → review → TDD all steps → mutation → finalize → report

   235→### 2: Resume After Failure
   236→Same command → loads .develop-progress.json → skips completed → resumes from failure

   238→### 3: Single Step Alternative
   239→For manual granular control, use individual commands:
   240→```
   241→/nw:roadmap @nw-solution-architect "goal"

   246→## Completion
   247→
   248→DELIVER is final wave. After completion → DISCOVER for next feature or mark project complete.

    50→export const BRAIN_CLAUDE_MD = `# Brain Knowledge Graph Integration
    51→
    52→This project is connected to the Brain knowledge graph via MCP tools. The graph contains decisions, constraints, tasks, questions, and observations from all agents and humans working on this workspace.
    53→
    54→## Getting Context
    55→
    56→Use \`get_context\` with a description of what you're working on. The server automatically finds the right project, tasks, decisions, and constraints — no need to pass project IDs manually.
    57→
    58→Example: \`get_context({ intent: "implementing OAuth flow for the auth service" })\`

    62→## Hooks
    63→
    64→- **SessionStart** loads workspace/project context automatically
    65→- **PreToolUse** injects brain context when dispatching subagents
    66→- **UserPromptSubmit** checks for workspace-level graph updates
    67→- **Stop** catches unlogged decisions before the session ends
    68→- **SessionEnd** logs session summary to the graph
    69→
    70→## Data Model
    71→
    72→**Work hierarchy:** Project → Feature → Task
    73→- **Project**: a named initiative with status, description.
    74→- **Feature**: a capability or deliverable within a project.
    75→- **Task**: an actionable work item. Status: open/todo/ready/in_progress/blocked/done/completed.
    76→
    77→**Cross-cutting entities** (attach to any level):
    78→- **Decision**: a choice that was made. Lifecycle: extracted → proposed → provisional → confirmed → superseded.
    79→- **Question**: an open question requiring a choice. Only for pending decisions, not informational queries.
    80→- **Observation**: a lightweight signal (info/warning/conflict). Lifecycle: open → acknowledged → resolved.
    81→- **Suggestion**: a proactive agent-to-human proposal. Categories: optimization, risk, opportunity, conflict, missing, pivot.
    82→
    83→**Entity ID format:** MCP tools use \`table:id\` for polymorphic references (e.g. \`task:abc123\`, \`decision:def456\`).
    84→
    85→## Decision Governance
    86→
    87→- **Your decisions are always \`provisional\` or \`inferred\`** — only humans confirm.
    88→- This means you can move fast without blocking, while humans retain authority.
    89→
    90→## Best Practices
    91→
    92→1. **Check before deciding.** Call \`resolve_decision\` first — the answer may already exist from another agent or human.
    93→2. **Ask, don't guess.** If uncertain, \`ask_question\` is better than \`create_provisional_decision\`.
    94→3. **Log as you go.** Don't batch decisions for the end. Log each significant choice when you make it.

   110→- **Grid cell resize** — Pinch, Cmd+Scroll, Cmd+=+-, slider. All route through `applyItemSize()` → `invalidateLayout()` (never `reloadData()`). Four thumbnail tiers: ≤tier0→adaptive (quantized 20px steps), ≤tier1→240px, ≤tier2→480px, >tier2→720px; tier change clears thumbnails + reloads.
   111→- **Dynamic cell aspect ratio** — `sampleMedianAspectRatio()` reads image headers (no decode). EXIF orientation 5-8 requires swapping w/h.
   112→- **Space-around layout** — `max(0, remaining)` + `floor(gap)` guards: negative remaining crashes FlowLayout; unrounded gaps cause line wrapping. Width-cache skips height-only recalcs.
   113→- **Grid persists across folder changes** — `clearCache()` + `configure()` instead of dismiss.
   114→- **Grid performance (Phase 1)** — `ThumbnailThrottle` actor limits concurrent decodes to 4. Scroll handler (20Hz) cancels non-visible tasks + evicts cache outside visible ± 50 buffer. Visible cells use `.userInitiated`, buffer cells `.utility`. Memory capped at 5% system RAM.
   115→- **Grid performance (Phase 2)** — Scroll-direction-aware prefetch (2 rows ahead), `MemoryPressureMonitor` (DispatchSource warning/critical), `generationID` stale-write guard on folder change, layer-backed cell optimization (`canDrawSubviewsIntoLayer` + `.onSetNeedsDisplay`).
   116→- **Keep-set cancel pattern** — When prefetch + cancel coexist, cancel must use `keepSet = visible ∪ prefetchRange`, not just visible indices. Otherwise prefetch tasks are immediately cancelled by the scroll handler.
   117→- **Generation ID pattern** — Int counter incremented on `clearCache()`, captured in Task closure, checked before cache write. Prevents stale folder thumbnails from overwriting new folder's cache. Same concept as `ImageViewController.currentLoadRequestID` (UUID) but simpler.
   118→- **DispatchSource idempotent start** — `DispatchSource.makeMemoryPressureSource` must guard `source == nil` before creating; repeated `start()` leaks un-cancelled sources.
   119→- **Reuse `NavigationThrottle`** — For any CFAbsoluteTime-based throttle (scroll handlers, etc.), use the existing `NavigationThrottle` struct instead of inline `lastTimestamp` + `guard` patterns.
   120→- **Grid performance (Phase 3.1-3.2)** — Tier0 adaptive resolution (`max(cellSize*scale, 80)` quantized to 20px steps) + `kCGImageSourceSubsampleFactor: 4` for JPEG/HEIF ≤120px. Priority dequeue in `ThumbnailThrottle` (smaller priority = higher urgency, FIFO tie-break). `cachedVisibleCenter` updated at 20Hz by scroll handler for `cellForItem` priority. Early `Task.isCancelled` guard after throttle acquire, before decode.
   121→- **`cachedVisibleCenter` pattern** — Avoid calling `indexPathsForVisibleItems()` per-cell in data source. Cache the visible center in the scroll handler (20Hz) and reuse in `cellForItem` + eviction. Initialize in `configure()` to `currentIndex`.
   122→- **Quantize to prevent cache churn** — When computed `maxSize` varies continuously (e.g., during pinch), quantize to fixed steps (`ceil(raw / step) * step`) so tier comparisons don't flush cache every frame.
   123→
   124→## Recent Significant Changes
   125→
   126→- **Navigation menu:** New "Navigation" menu between View and Go. Reading mode (Dual Page, RTL) and nav settings (Arrow keys, Scroll to Bottom, page-turn sensitivity) moved there from View/Go menus.
   127→- **RTL nav + scroll settings:** `duoPageRTLNavigation` (default on) / `singlePageRTLNavigation` (default off) as independent settings; `effectiveRTLNavigation` picks based on current mode. `scrollToBottomOnPrevious` (default on) controls scroll position when navigating backward.
   128→- **Grid progressive tier reload:** Tier change no longer clears `gridThumbnails`; stale images stay visible until new tier finishes. `gridThumbnailSizes` tracks cached tier per index. Old images replaced in-place as new tier loads.
   129→- **Grid scrollbar:** Replaced overlay/autohide with legacy `VisibleScroller` subclass (always-visible, custom knob). `availableLayoutWidth` must use `contentView.bounds.width`.
   130→- **Grid Phase 3.4 + Phase 4.1:** Arithmetic visible range calculation; min cell size 160pt; Finder-style slider.
   131→- **Multi-instance window support:** `ImageWindowController` now manages a `windows: [ImageWindowController]` array instead of a `shared` singleton. `reuseWindow: Bool` setting in `ViewerSettings` toggles behavior. `current` property prefers `NSApp.keyWindow` → `NSApp.mainWindow` → `windows.last`. Multi-file open deduplicates by folder path to prevent race conditions. Window cleanup via `willCloseNotification`.
   132→- **Grid performance Phase 3.1-3.2:** Tier0 adaptive resolution + SubsampleFactor, priority dequeue throttle, cachedVisibleCenter, early cancellation guard, magic numbers extracted to Constants.
   133→- **Grid performance Phase 2:** Prefetch pipeline (scroll direction + keep-set cancel), MemoryPressureMonitor, generation ID stale-write guard, layer-backed cell optimization, NavigationThrottle reuse.
   134→- **Grid view fixes:** Highlight border clipping fix (inset frame + zPosition), visual redesign (blue tint for active, orange border for cursor), cell drag-drop passthrough, keyboard auto-scroll.
   135→- **Grid layout Phase 3-4:** Dynamic cell aspect ratio (EXIF-aware), smooth resize, space-around layout, thumbnail tiers with cache isolation.
   136→- **Option+scroll fast nav:** OptionScrollAccumulator, PositionHUDView, mouse sensitivity fix.
   137→- **Quick Grid:** Thumbnail grid overlay, async loading, keyboard handling, drag-drop support.

    70→## Data Model
    71→
    72→**Work hierarchy:** Project → Feature → Task
    73→- **Project**: a named initiative with status, description.
    74→- **Feature**: a capability or deliverable within a project.
    75→- **Task**: an actionable work item. Status: open/todo/ready/in_progress/blocked/done/completed.

    79→- **Question**: an open question requiring a choice. Only for pending decisions, not informational queries.
    80→- **Observation**: a lightweight signal (info/warning/conflict). Lifecycle: open → acknowledged → resolved.
    81→- **Suggestion**: a proactive agent-to-human proposal. Categories: optimization, risk, opportunity, conflict, missing, pivot.

1→# Cee — CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→macOS image viewer (AppKit, Swift 6.2, arm64, Xcode 26).
     4→Replaces XEE. Core flow: Finder right-click → Open With → folder browse → pinch zoom.
     5→
     6→## Build & Test
     7→
     8→```bash
     9→xcodegen generate          # regenerate .xcodeproj after project.yml changes
    10→xcodebuild -project Cee.xcodeproj -scheme Cee -configuration Debug build
    11→xcodebuild test -project Cee.xcodeproj -scheme Cee -destination 'platform=macOS' -only-testing:CeeTests
    12→./scripts/test-e2e.sh      # XCUITest suite
    13→```
    14→
    15→Debug: `CEE_DEBUG_CENTERING=1` env var or `--debug-centering` flag.
    16→
    17→## Key Conventions
    18→
    19→- **No XIB/Storyboard** — all UI is programmatic.
    20→- **Entry point** — `main.swift` (not `@main`/`@NSApplicationMain`).
    21→- **Multi-instance window support** — `ImageWindowController.windows` (array) replaces the old `shared` singleton. `reuseWindow` setting (default `true`) controls whether new files open in the same window or a new one.
    22→- **project.yml** — source of truth for Xcode project. `.xcodeproj` is gitignored.
    23→- **Test targets** — `CeeTests` (unit) and `CeeUITests` (E2E). `TestHelpers.swift` provides shared `minimalPNG()`, `createJPEG(width:height:)`, `createPNG(width:height:)`.
    24→- **URL comparison gotcha** — `URL ==` can fail between manually constructed URLs and URLs from `contentsOfDirectory`. Use `.path` comparison.
    25→
    26→## Swift 6 Gotchas
    27→
    28→- **`ImageLoader` is an `actor`** — never pass `ImageFolder` (non-Sendable) across actor boundaries. Use `ImageItem` (Sendable).
    29→- **`setMagnification(_:centeredAt:)`** — parameter label is `centeredAt:`, not `centeredAtPoint:`.
    30→- **Protocol + @MainActor** — delegate protocols called from NSScrollView subclasses must be marked `@MainActor`.
    31→- **NSScrollView unflipped coordinates** — visual top = high Y, visual bottom = low Y.
    32→- **NSScrollView `contentInsets` visual semantics** — `.top` = visual top (high Y), `.bottom` = visual bottom (low Y). In `scrollRange`: `minY = -insets.bottom`, `maxY = docH - clipH + insets.top`.
    33→- **CALayer y-axis flipped in layer-backed NSView** — `wantsLayer = true` → `y=0` is visual top. Opposite of raw Core Animation.
    34→- **`deinit` cannot access stored properties** in strict concurrency. Use notification-based cleanup.
    35→- **CGImageSource pixel dimensions ignore EXIF orientation** — `kCGImagePropertyPixelWidth/Height` report raw sensor dimensions. For orientation 5-8, swap w/h. Thumbnails with `kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true` are auto-rotated, but `fullSize` is not.
    36→- **`@objc func` + default parameter + menu action** — `@objc func foo(amount: Int = 1)` gets ObjC selector `fooWithAmount:`. AppKit passes `NSMenuItem` pointer as the argument → huge `Int`. Fix: separate `@objc` action from internal impl.
    37→
    38→## XcodeGen Gotchas
    39→
    40→- **Unit test bundle type is `bundle.unit-test`**, not `bundle.unit-testing`. UI test is `bundle.ui-testing`.
    41→- **`GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES`** required for test targets without custom Info.plist.
    42→- **Xcode 26 debug dylib** — `ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB` splits app into stub + `Cee.debug.dylib`. Requires `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED: YES` with ad-hoc signing, otherwise dylib fails system policy.
    43→- **Signing / test failures** — If CodeSign fails ("code object is not signed at all" in test bundle, or dylib system policy) or tests fail to run: run `xcodegen generate` then `xcodebuild clean build`. Regenerating syncs project.yml; clean build refreshes stale signatures. Incremental builds can leave dylib/test bundle signatures out of sync.
    44→
    45→## AppKit Gotchas
    46→
    47→- **Cmd-shortcuts vs keyDown** — `performKeyEquivalent` fires before `keyDown`. Cmd-modified → menu items; bare keys → `ImageScrollView.keyDown`.
    48→- **Never put `keyDown` on NSViewController when NSScrollView is first responder.** NSScrollView intercepts arrow/Space/PageUp/PageDown. Override on NSScrollView subclass.
    49→- **`NSMenuItemValidation`** — protocol conformance, not `override`.
    50→- **Overlay event passthrough** — display-only overlays override `hitTest` → `nil`. For drag-drop, child `NSImageView` must call `unregisterDraggedTypes()` to prevent intercepting parent's drag session.
    51→- **NSVisualEffectView + alpha animation** — animating `alphaValue` causes material compositing flash. Use plain `layer.backgroundColor` with semi-transparent color instead.
    52→- **NSCollectionView re-enables scrollers** during layout/reloadData. Override getter+setter in subclass to lock off; simple property assignment is insufficient.
    53→- **NSCollectionView `didSelectItemsAt` fires on arrow keys** — filter with `NSApp.currentEvent?.type == .leftMouseUp` for click-only. Arrow key selection does NOT auto-scroll; call `scrollToItems(at:scrollPosition:)` manually in the else branch.
    54→- **NSCollectionView `scrollToItems` unreliable** — use `layoutAttributesForItem(at:)?.frame` + `scrollToVisible(_:)` instead for reliable programmatic scrolling.
    55→- **NSCollectionView internal auto-scroll during selection** — `NSCollectionView` calls `scrollToItems` internally after selection changes (arrow keys). Suppress by overriding `scrollToItems(at:scrollPosition:)` in a subclass with a `suppressAutoScroll` flag; set the flag around your own scroll calls so only your animation runs.
    56→- **NSCollectionView scrollbar + `availableLayoutWidth`** — When using a legacy always-visible scrollbar (`VisibleScroller` subclass), use `contentView.bounds.width` for `availableLayoutWidth`, not `bounds.width`, to account for the scroller's width.
    57→- **CALayer border clipping in NSCollectionView cells** — `borderWidth` draws half inside, half outside bounds. With `masksToBounds = true` + adjacent cell overlap, borders get clipped. Fix: inset highlightLayer frame by `borderWidth/2` so border is fully inside bounds; set `zPosition` high to render above subview layers.
    58→- **`NSCollectionViewPrefetching` doesn't exist in AppKit** — UIKit-only.
    59→
    60→## XCUITest Gotchas
    61→
    62→- **NSScrollView accessibility** — only `setAccessibilityIdentifier`; never override `.scrollArea` role.
    63→- **Bare key events unreliable.** Use Cmd-modified menu shortcuts.
    64→- **Always assert `XCTWaiter` result** — `.wait(...)` returns `.timedOut` silently.
    65→
    66→## Centering & Zoom
    67→
    68→- **Never sync fullscreen with fixed delays.** Use `didEnterFullScreen`/`didExitFullScreen` notifications.
    69→- **Centering math: one coordinate space.** Never divide `statusBarH` by magnification.
    70→- **Anchor out-of-bounds** — When anchor lies outside document bounds, use document center. Clamping causes rightward bias.
    71→- **`isZooming` flag** suppresses force-recenter during zoom to preserve pan position.
    72→- **resizeToFitImage below min** — When target < window minimum, early return to avoid drift.
    73→
    74→## Scroll & Page-Turn
    75→
