   172→**Codex Subagent Detection (Phases 1-3 complete):**
   173→- **Event-driven only** (no directory watch): Codex日期目錄混合多個使用者的主 session，無法用 fs.watch 過濾。偵測靠解析主 session JSONL 的 `spawn_agent` + `function_call_output` 事件。
   174→- **UUID format**: Codex subagent ID 是 UUID v7（`019cc375-5af5-7ed1-9ff8-8a5757d815d1`），不同於 Claude 的 7-40 hex。`isValidCodexAgentId` 用 UUID regex 驗證。
   175→- **Flat directory**: subagent JSONL 和主 session 在同一個日期目錄（非巢狀）。`dirname(mainSessionPath)` 即日期目錄。
   176→- **Label collision gotcha**: UUID v7 前兩段都是 timestamp。`makeCodexAgentLabel` 改用 `parts[0]` + `parts[4].slice(0,4)`（node segment）避免同毫秒碰撞。
   177→- **All CLI options supported**: `--with-subagents`、`--subagent`、`--all`、`--pane`、`--interactive` 現在同時支援 `claude` 和 `codex`。
   178→- **Shared interfaces in core**: `OutputHandler`、`WatcherHandler`、`SessionHandler` 等介面在 `src/core/detector-interfaces.ts`，Claude module 透過 re-export 向後相容。
   179→- **Stateless parser in interactive mode**: Codex parser 無狀態，`startCodexInteractiveWatch` 所有 session 共用 `sharedParser`（Claude 每 session 需獨立 parser 防止狀態污染）。
   180→- **registerExistingAgent() required for resume**: 啟動時已知的 subagent 必須呼叫 `detector.registerExistingAgent(agentId, path)` 預填路徑，否則 `resume_agent` 事件的 `handleSubagentResume` 找不到路徑，`onSubagentEnter` 不會觸發。
   181→- **stopped flag prevents cross-session contamination**: `CodexSubagentDetector.stop()` 設定 `stopped = true`，`_resolveSubagent` 在每個 await 點後檢查，防止舊 detector 的 in-flight resolve 污染新 session 的 watcher。
   182→- **`handleSpawnAgentOutput` skips pre-registered agents**: 啟動時透過 `registerExistingAgent` 預填的 agentId，在歷史行重播時 `handleSpawnAgentOutput` 會跳過（避免對已知 subagent 重複 resolve + 重複 `onNewSubagent`）。
   183→- **Codex pane output filter needs shortId→fullId mapping**: Codex label 用短 ID（`019cc375-8a57`），但 `PaneManager` 用完整 UUID 作 key。`shouldOutput` 需透過 `shortIdToFullId` Map 反查。此映射在 `switchToSession` 時 `clear()`，並由 `prefillExistingSubagents` 和 `openPaneForSubagent` 填充。
   184→- **Use `RetryConfig` for retry loops**: `src/core/detector-interfaces.ts` 定義了 `RetryConfig` 介面（maxRetries, retryDelay, initialDelay）。Codex 的 `SUBAGENT_FILE_RETRY` 和 Claude 的 `EARLY_DETECTION_RETRY` / `FALLBACK_DETECTION_RETRY` 都應使用此介面，避免 magic numbers。
   185→
   186→**Cursor Agent (Phases 1-3 complete):**
   187→- **No timestamps**: Cursor JSONL entries have no timestamp field. Parser returns `''`, formatter shows `[--:--:--]`.
   188→- **Workspace slug is NOT reversible**: `-` in slug could be path separator, literal hyphen, or underscore. Only `.workspace-trusted` (present in ~10% of dirs) has authoritative `workspacePath`. Project filter (`-p`) checks both slug and workspacePath.
   189→- **Stateless parser**: Like Codex, no need to recreate on session switch. Uses `contentToString()` from `src/utils/text.ts` to handle content arrays.
   190→- **Tag stripping order matters**: Must run `stripAttachedFilesTags` before `stripUserQueryTags` — attached_files block can precede user_query, and user_query regex uses `^` anchor.
   191→- **`findLatestInProject` glob `*/*.jsonl`**: Only matches one level deep, so subagent files in `subagents/` subdirectory are naturally excluded — no explicit `/subagents/` check needed.
   192→- **Subagent detection is pure directory-watch**: Cursor JSONL has **no** spawn/resume/done events. `CursorSubagentDetector` uses only `fs.watch` on `subagents/` dir (with parent dir fallback for the ~88% of sessions that don't have subagents at startup).
   193→- **Subagent filenames have no prefix**: `{UUID}.jsonl` (not `agent-{hex}.jsonl` like Claude). Use `isValidCursorSubagentId` (UUID regex) for validation.
   194→- **`CursorSubagentDetector` rolls back on failure**: Unlike Claude's detector, Cursor's `tryAddSubagentFile` removes `agentId` from `knownAgentIds` on failure, since there are no JSONL events for fallback detection.
   195→- **Pane FIFO eviction**: Cursor has no subagent completion events, so panes accumulate. `startCursorMultiWatch` uses a FIFO array (`paneAgentOrder`) to evict the oldest pane when at 6-pane capacity. `paneAgentOrder` must be cleared on session switch.
   196→- **Interactive mode follows Codex pattern**: Shared stateless parser, no `detectionHandler`, no custom title support. Do NOT pass `session` to `CursorSubagentDetector` config in interactive mode — the detector's `registerExistingAgent` and `registerNewAgent` both call `session?.addSession?()` internally, which would cause double registration if combined with `onNewSubagent` callback.
   197→- **`--no-follow --with-subagents` uses sequential output**: NOT `outputTimeSorted` (which infinite-loops with stateless parsers). Output main session first, then subagents by birthtime.
   198→- **All CLI options supported**: `--subagent`, `--with-subagents`, `--all`, `--pane`, `--interactive` now supported for `claude`, `codex`, and `cursor`.
   199→- **`createInteractiveSessionManager(displayController)`** is shared by Claude, Codex, and Cursor interactive watches.
   200→
   201→**Gotchas:**
   202→- **Gemini parser has state** (`processedMessageIds`). Must recreate parser when switching sessions to avoid message skip bugs.
   203→- **`Bun.file(dir).exists()` returns false for directories**. Use `stat(dir)` instead.
   204→- **Codex cache only scans "today"** for incremental refresh. Cross-midnight sessions handled on next startup.
   205→- **Codex subagent sessions share same `cwd` as main session**: Both live in the same flat date directory with identical `rollout-*.jsonl` naming. The only reliable distinction is `session_meta.payload.source`: main sessions have `source: "mcp"` (string), subagents have `source: { subagent: { thread_spawn: { parent_thread_id, depth, ... } } }` (object). `readMainSessionMeta()` in `session-cache.ts` is the canonical helper for this check — use it instead of inline first-line parsing. Bump `CACHE_VERSION` when changing cache filtering logic to invalidate stale disk caches.
   206→- **Subagent ID length varies**: Claude Code subagent filenames use 7-40 hex chars (`agent-[0-9a-f]{7,40}.jsonl`), not fixed 7. Regex must accommodate this.
   207→- **`--pane` mutual exclusions**: Cannot combine with `--interactive` or `--subagent`. Requires `--follow` mode. Auto-enables `--with-subagents`.
   208→- **PaneManager command builder** uses `process.argv[0]` and `process.argv[1]` to reconstruct the CLI command, supporting bun run, npx, and global install scenarios.
   209→- **SubagentDetector description queue**: FIFO `pendingDescriptions` must be consumed in both `registerNewAgent` (early detection) and `handleFallbackDetection` (completed path) to prevent queue drift. The queue is cleared in `stop()`.
   210→- **`handleAgentProgress` only triggers for resume**: Unknown agentIds are ignored (registration is handled by `onNewSubagent` via early/fallback paths), and only known agentIds trigger `onSubagentEnter`. This prevents duplicate pane opens and registration race issues.
   211→- **Claude Code tool rename backward compat**: `Task` → `Agent` (subagent spawn) and `TodoWrite` → `TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskList/TaskGet` (task management). Use `isSubagentTool(name)` from `format-tool.ts` (backed by `SUBAGENT_TOOL_NAMES` Set) — do not inline `=== 'Task' || === 'Agent'`. `formatToolUse` and `getToolCategory` handle both old and new names.
   212→- **`readLastCodexAssistantMessage` signature**: Takes `(filePath, parser: LineParser)` — not `verbose` bool like the Claude version. Parser is injected to avoid circular imports.
   213→- **`createInteractiveSessionManager(displayController)`**: Module-level helper in `src/index.ts` shared by both `startClaudeInteractiveWatch` and `startCodexInteractiveWatch`. Do not duplicate this into each function.
   214→- **`prefillExistingSubagents(detector, files)`**: Helper in `startCodexMultiWatch` that combines `registerExistingAgent` + `registerShortId` into one loop. Used in both init and `switchToSession` — do not inline back into separate loops.
   215→- **`onTitleUpdate` is for interactive mode only**: In non-interactive multi-watch, the formatter already outputs `TITL Session renamed: "xxx"` via `onOutput`. Adding `onTitleUpdate` there causes duplicate output. Only interactive mode needs `onTitleUpdate` (to update `displayName` + refresh status line).
   216→- **`findLatestMainSessionInProject` intentionally skips `customTitle`**: Auto-switch polling runs every 500ms. Reading JSONL content for title would be wasteful. Title is read on-demand via `readCustomTitle()` only when a switch actually happens.
   217→- **Codex `findBySessionId` project filter matches file path, not cwd**: This is a known limitation. Codex file paths only contain date directories, so `-p` filtering in `findBySessionId` is effectively broken for Codex. `listSessions()` correctly filters on `session_meta.cwd`. `agent-pick` intentionally does NOT forward `-p` to the final tail command to avoid this issue.
   218→- **`--list` is mutually exclusive with most tail-mode options**: `--interactive`, `--subagent`, `--pane`, `--with-subagents`, `--auto-switch`, `--raw`, `--all`, and `[session-id]` positional arg. It auto-sets `--no-follow`.
   219→- **`customTitle` is NOT populated by `listSessions()`**: Too expensive (reads full JSONL per session). Only `findLatest()` for Claude reads it. Future enhancement: lazy load in `agent-pick` preview.
   220→- **`Bun.spawn` pipe chaining breaks fzf TTY**: Piping `listProc.stdout` directly to fzf's `stdin` via `Bun.spawn` prevents fzf from accessing `/dev/tty` for keyboard input (arrow keys show `^[[A`). Use `sh -c "cmd | fzf ..."` instead — the shell handles pipe setup while fzf gets proper TTY access. See `buildShellCommand()` in `src/pick/fzf-helpers.ts`.
   221→- **PaneManager logging belongs inside PaneManager, not in callbacks**: `onSubagentEnter` fires on every `agent_progress` event (repeatedly). Logging pane state in the callback causes duplicate messages. Instead, pass `logger` to `PaneManager` constructor; `openPane()` and `closePaneByAgentId()` log only when actually acting (after dedup checks). `openPane()` also re-throws errors so callers can surface `Failed to open pane` warnings.

1→# Wave Decisions: Agent Management (DISTILL)
     2→
     3→## Test Design Decisions
     4→
     5→### TD-1: Bun test runner with GWT comments, not Gherkin files
     6→
     7→**Status**: Decided
     8→
     9→Tests use `bun:test` with `describe/it/expect` and Given-When-Then comments inside each `it()` block. Gherkin `.feature` files are not used as executable specs.
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: Project convention (per `tests/AGENTS.md`) specifies that `.feature` files are documentation-only. All existing acceptance tests follow the `describe/it` pattern with GWT comments. The test framework is Bun's test runner, not Cucumber/pytest-bdd.
    12→
    13→### TD-2: Session-authenticated HTTP requests for all agent endpoints
    14→
    15→**Status**: Decided
    16→
    17→Agent CRUD endpoints are browser-facing routes authenticated via Better Auth session cookies. Tests use `createTestUser()` for signup and pass session cookies on all requests.
    18→
    19→**Rationale**: Per architecture design (DD-3), agent endpoints live under `/api/workspaces/:workspaceId/agents` and use session auth. DPoP/MCP auth is not used for these endpoints. This matches the existing pattern in learning, policy, and objective test suites.
    20→
    21→### TD-3: Walking skeletons enabled, R2/R3 scenarios skipped
    22→
    23→**Status**: Decided
    24→
    25→All 4 walking skeleton tests and 19 focused R1 scenarios are enabled (not skipped). R2 (sandbox creation) and R3 (operational dashboard) scenarios use `describe.skip()` blocks.
    26→
    27→**Rationale**: One-at-a-time TDD principle. Walking skeleton tests define "done" for R1. The crafter enables and implements them sequentially. R2/R3 tests are written now as specifications but skipped until their implementation phase.
    28→
    29→### TD-4: Workspace creation via HTTP for session edge wiring
    30→
    31→**Status**: Decided
    32→
    33→Tests use `createWorkspaceViaHttp()` (not `createWorkspaceDirectly()`) to create workspaces, which wires person-identity-member_of edges through the server. This ensures session-authenticated requests resolve workspace membership correctly.
    34→
    35→**Rationale**: Agent endpoints are browser-facing routes that resolve identity from the Better Auth session. `createWorkspaceViaHttp()` creates the full edge chain (person -> identity -> member_of -> workspace) that `resolveIdentityFromSession()` requires.
    36→
    37→### TD-5: Brain agents seeded directly for test isolation
    38→
    39→**Status**: Decided
    40→
    41→Brain agents are seeded via `seedBrainAgent()` helper (direct DB insert), not through the identity bootstrap that runs on workspace creation. This gives tests explicit control over which brain agents exist.
    42→
    43→**Rationale**: The identity bootstrap creates all 6 brain agents during workspace creation. Some tests need a specific set of brain agents. Direct seeding is more deterministic and faster than filtering the bootstrap output.
    44→
    45→### TD-6: Per-test workspace isolation
    46→
    47→**Status**: Decided
    48→
    49→Each `it()` block creates its own workspace and user. No shared `let` variables at `describe` scope.
    50→
    51→**Rationale**: Tests run with `--concurrent`. Shared mutable state at describe scope causes cross-test contamination. Per-test isolation is the project convention (per `tests/AGENTS.md`).
    52→
    53→## Mandate Compliance Evidence
    54→
    55→### CM-A: Hexagonal Boundary Enforcement
    56→
    57→All test files import exclusively from `agents-test-kit.ts`, which provides HTTP helper functions that invoke driving ports:
    58→- `listAgentsViaHttp()` -> `GET /api/workspaces/:ws/agents`
    59→- `createAgentViaHttp()` -> `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/agents`
    60→- `getAgentDetailViaHttp()` -> `GET /api/workspaces/:ws/agents/:id`
    61→- `deleteAgentViaHttp()` -> `DELETE /api/workspaces/:ws/agents/:id`
    62→- `updateAgentViaHttp()` -> `PUT /api/workspaces/:ws/agents/:id`
    63→
    64→Direct SurrealDB queries are used only for:
    65→- Given-step data seeding (`seedBrainAgent`)
    66→- Then-step verification (`agentExistsInDb`, `getAuthorityEdgesForIdentity`)
    67→
    68→Zero internal module imports (no `agents/routes.ts`, no `agents/queries.ts`).
    69→
    70→### CM-B: Business Language Purity
    71→
    72→Scenario names and GWT comments use business domain language exclusively:
    73→- "admin registers an external agent" (not "POST to /api/agents returns 201")
    74→- "authority scopes default to 'propose'" (not "authorized_to edges have permission='propose'")
    75→- "all related records are removed" (not "DELETE cascades through identity_agent edges")
    76→
    77→Technical terms appear only in test kit helper implementations (HTTP methods, RecordId), never in test scenario descriptions.
    78→
    79→### CM-C: Walking Skeleton + Focused Scenario Counts
    80→
    81→- Walking skeletons: 4 (WS-1 through WS-4)
    82→- Focused scenarios (R1): 19 (EC-1 through EC-19)
    83→- Total R1: 23 scenarios
    84→- Error ratio (R1): 43% (10/23)
    85→
    86→## Handoff Checklist
    87→
    88→- [x] Walking skeleton tests written and enabled
    89→- [x] Focused scenarios cover all R1 stories (US-01 through US-04)
    90→- [x] Error path ratio >= 40% for R1
    91→- [x] R2/R3 scenarios written and skipped
    92→- [x] Test kit provides business-language helpers
    93→- [x] All tests invoke through driving ports only
    94→- [x] Per-test workspace isolation (concurrent-safe)
    95→- [x] Mandate compliance evidence documented

2	name: 1natsu-document-harness-model
3	description: ハーネスドキュメント（CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/, docs/, feature README）の書き方・配置判断・粒度の基準を提供する内部リファレンス。document-harness 系スキルの共通知識として他のスキルから自動参照される。

6	metadata:
7	  author: 1natsu
8	  version: "1.1.0"

10	
11	# ハーネスドキュメントモデル リファレンス
12	
13	ハーネスドキュメントの判断基準を集約した内部リファレンス。「何を書くか」「どこに置くか」「どう書くか」の共通知識を提供する。
14	
15	## 3層モデル
16	
17	ハーネスドキュメントは役割に応じて3つの層に分かれる。各層には適切な配置先があり、混在させない。層を混ぜると、エージェントが「ルール」と「背景説明」を区別できず、指示の優先度を誤判断するリスクがある。
18	
19	| 層 | 役割 | 配置先 | 例 |
20	|---|------|--------|-----|
21	| **指示** | 「こうしろ / するな」 | `.claude/rules/` | コーディング規約、データ整合性ルール |
22	| **インデックス** | 「何が重要か / どこを読め」 | `CLAUDE.md` | パッケージ概要、重要な前提、`@` 参照 |
23	| **知識** | 「なぜこうなっているか」 | `docs/` / feature `README.md` | 設計背景、データフロー、依存関係、状態遷移 |
24	
25	### 3層分離の例
26	
27	認証モジュールのトークン有効期限を30分→15分に変更した場合:
28	
29	- **指示** (`.claude/rules/auth.md`): 「トークン有効期限は15分とする。変更する場合はセキュリティチームの承認が必要」
30	- **インデックス** (`CLAUDE.md`): 「認証仕様 → @docs/auth-design.md」
31	- **知識** (`docs/auth-design.md`): 「有効期限を30分から15分に短縮した。理由: セキュリティ監査でセッションハイジャックのリスク軽減を指摘されたため」
32	
33	## 書くべきもの / 書くべきでないもの
34	
35	ドキュメントの価値は「コードだけでは得られない情報」にある。コードから読み取れることを繰り返すと、コードとドキュメントの乖離が必ず起き、エージェントがどちらを信頼すべきか判断できなくなる。
36	
37	**書く:**
38	- コードから読み取れない設計判断とその理由
39	- 暗黙の依存関係（バッチ処理、外部サービス、ワーカー等）
40	- 複数レイヤーにまたがるデータフロー
41	- 非自明な制約や前提条件
42	- エッジケースや落とし穴
43	
44	**書かない:**
45	- コードから直接読み取れること（関数のシグネチャ、型定義の列挙等）
46	- git history から得られること（誰がいつ変更したか）
47	- 標準的な言語・フレームワークの慣例
48	- 自明な事実（「このファイルは X を export している」等）
49	
50	## 配置先ごとのルール
51	
52	### CLAUDE.md
53	
54	- **200行以下**に収める。詳細は `@` 参照で指し示す
55	- 「何が重要か」「どこを読めばいいか」だけを伝えるインデックスに徹する
56	
57	CLAUDE.md はエージェントのセッション開始時に常にコンテキストへ読み込まれる。肥大化するとトークンを浪費し、本当に重要な指示が埋もれる。詳細は `@` 参照で外に出し、必要な時だけ読ませる。
58	
59	### .claude/rules/
60	
61	- 1ファイル = 1トピック。`paths` frontmatter で適用範囲を限定する
62	- 「こうしろ / するな」の行動指示に徹し、理由（why）を簡潔に添える
63	- 知識や設計背景は書かない（それは docs/ の役割）
64	
65	rules/ ファイルは `paths` パターンにマッチした時だけコンテキストに読み込まれる。複数トピックを1ファイルに混ぜると、無関係な指示まで読み込まれてノイズになる。
66	
67	### docs/
68	
69	- 人間も読むドキュメントとして書く（Claude 専用にしない）
70	- 「なぜこうなっているか」の設計背景を中心に
71	- ファイル名は内容を表す具体的な名前にする（同階層に複数ある場合）
72	
73	### feature README.md
74	
75	- その機能の全体像を1ファイルで把握できるようにする
76	- レイヤー間の依存関係、非自明な設計判断とその理由、暗黙の前提（バッチ処理、外部ワーカー等）を記載する
77	
78	機能ディレクトリに README がないと、エージェントはコードを読んで構造を推測するしかなく、暗黙の依存関係を見落とす。
79	
80	## monorepo での注意点
81	
82	- パッケージ固有のコンテキスト → パッケージ直下の `CLAUDE.md`（ルートの `.claude/rules/` ではない）
83	- 横断的な規約のみルートの `.claude/rules/` に配置する
84	- パッケージの `CLAUDE.md` もインデックスに徹し、詳細は `docs/` に分離する
85	
86	パッケージ固有の情報をルートに集めると、無関係なパッケージの作業時にもコンテキストに読み込まれてしまう。
87	
88	## 配置判断リファレンス
89	
90	配置判断のフローチャート、早見表、迷った時の判断基準は [references/placement-guide.md](references/placement-guide.md) を参照。
91

1	# ドキュメント配置ガイド
2	
3	## 配置判断フローチャート
4	
5	```
6	変更内容を分析
7	│
8	├─ 横断的な規約・指示か？
9	│  ├─ 全パッケージ共通 → ルート .claude/rules/（paths なし）
10	│  └─ 特定ファイルパターン → ルート .claude/rules/（paths 付き）
11	│
12	├─ パッケージ固有の指示か？
13	│  └─ パッケージ内 .claude/rules/（paths 付き）
14	│
15	├─ パッケージの概要・前提が変わったか？
16	│  └─ パッケージ直下 CLAUDE.md を更新（200行以下、@参照で詳細へ）
17	│
18	├─ 設計背景・アーキテクチャの知識か？
19	│  ├─ パッケージレベル → packages/xxx/docs/
20	│  └─ アプリレベル → packages/xxx/docs/ or ルート docs/
21	│
22	└─ 機能固有の仕様・データフローか？
23	   └─ feature ディレクトリ直下の README.md
24	```
25	
26	## 配置先の早見表
27	
28	| 書きたいこと | 配置先 | ファイル形式 |
29	|-------------|--------|------------|
30	| 全パッケージ共通のコードスタイル | `.claude/rules/code-style.md` | paths なし |
31	| 特定ファイルパターンの規約 | `.claude/rules/xxx.md` | `paths: ["pattern"]` |
32	| パッケージ固有の禁止事項 | `packages/xxx/.claude/rules/xxx.md` | `paths: ["src/**"]` |
33	| パッケージの概要と重要な前提 | `packages/xxx/CLAUDE.md` | `@` 参照でインデックス |
34	| アーキテクチャの設計背景 | `(packages/xxx/)docs/architecture.md` | 通常の markdown |
35	| 外部依存・バッチ処理の仕様 | `(packages/xxx/)docs/xxx.md` | 通常の markdown |
36	| 状態遷移・ライフサイクル | `(packages/xxx/)docs/xxx-lifecycle.md` | 通常の markdown |
37	| 機能のデータフロー | `src/features/xxx/README.md` | 通常の markdown |
38	| 機能のレイヤー間依存 | `src/features/xxx/README.md` | 通常の markdown |
39	| 機能の非自明な設計判断 | `src/features/xxx/README.md` | 通常の markdown |
40	| ADR（アーキテクチャ決定記録） | `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md` | ADR テンプレート |
41	
42	## 判断に迷った時
43	
44	### rules/ vs docs/ で迷う
45	
46	- **「〜すること」「〜してはならない」** と書けるなら → `rules/`
47	- **「〜という背景で」「〜の理由で」** と書くなら → `docs/`
48	- 両方必要なら、`rules/` に指示を書き、`docs/` に理由の詳細を書く
49	
50	### docs/ vs feature README で迷う
51	
52	- 複数機能にまたがる知識 → `docs/`
53	- 1つの機能に閉じた知識 → feature `README.md`
54	- 迷ったら feature README に書いてから、必要に応じて docs/ に昇格させる
55	
56	### CLAUDE.md に書くか別ファイルに分けるか迷う
57	
58	- 3行以内で伝わる → CLAUDE.md に直接書く
59	- 4行以上の説明が必要 → 別ファイルにして `@` 参照

1→# OpenClaw Import
     2→
     3→Moltis can automatically detect and import data from an existing [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai) installation. This lets you migrate to Moltis without losing your provider keys, memory files, skills, sessions, personality, or channel configuration.
     4→
     5→> **Your OpenClaw installation is never modified.** The import is strictly read-only — Moltis copies data into its own directory and does not write to, move, or delete anything under `~/.openclaw/`. You can safely keep using OpenClaw alongside Moltis, and re-import at any time to pick up new data.
     6→
     7→## How Detection Works
     8→
     9→Moltis checks for an OpenClaw installation in two locations:
    10→
    11→1. The path set in the `OPENCLAW_HOME` environment variable
    12→2. `~/.openclaw/` (default)
    13→
    14→If the directory exists and contains recognizable OpenClaw files (`openclaw.json`, agent directories, etc.), Moltis considers it detected. The workspace directory respects the `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` environment variable for multi-profile setups.
    15→
    16→## What Gets Imported
    17→
    18→| Category | Source | Destination | Notes |
    19→|----------|--------|-------------|-------|
    20→| **Identity** | `openclaw.json` agent name, theme, and timezone | `moltis.toml` identity section | Preserves existing Moltis identity if already configured |
    21→| **Providers** | Agent auth-profiles (API keys) | `~/.moltis/provider_keys.json` | Maps OpenClaw provider names to Moltis equivalents (e.g., `google` becomes `gemini`) |
    22→| **Skills** | `skills/` directories with `SKILL.md` | `~/.moltis/skills/` | Copies entire skill directories; skips duplicates |
    23→| **Memory** | `MEMORY.md` and all `memory/*.md` files | `~/.moltis/MEMORY.md` and `~/.moltis/memory/` | Imports daily logs, project notes, and all other markdown memory files. Appends with `<!-- Imported from OpenClaw -->` separator for idempotency |
    24→| **Channels** | Telegram and Discord bot configuration in `openclaw.json` | `moltis.toml` channels section | Supports both flat and multi-account Telegram configs |
    25→| **Sessions** | JSONL conversation files under `agents/*/sessions/` | `~/.moltis/sessions/` and `~/.moltis/memory/sessions/` | Converts OpenClaw message format to Moltis format; prefixes keys with `oc:`. Also generates markdown transcripts for memory search indexing |
    26→| **MCP Servers** | `mcp-servers.json` | `~/.moltis/mcp-servers.json` | Merges with existing servers; skips duplicates by name |
    27→| **Workspace Files** | `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `BOOT.md` | `~/.moltis/` (root) or `~/.moltis/agents/<id>/` | Copies raw workspace files; skips if destination already has user content. Replaces auto-seeded defaults |
    28→
    29→### Workspace files explained
    30→
    31→These markdown files shape your agent's personality and behavior. Moltis uses them in the same way OpenClaw does:
    32→
    33→- **`SOUL.md`** — personality directives (tone, style, boundaries)
    34→- **`IDENTITY.md`** — agent name, emoji, creature/vibe theme
    35→- **`USER.md`** — user profile (name, preferences, context the agent should know about you)
    36→- **`TOOLS.md`** — tool usage guidelines and constraints
    37→- **`AGENTS.md`** — global workspace rules injected into every conversation
    38→- **`HEARTBEAT.md`** — periodic heartbeat prompt (what to check on each scheduled tick)
    39→- **`BOOT.md`** — startup context injected when the gateway starts
    40→
    41→If you customized any of these files in OpenClaw, they will carry over. If the destination already has user content, the import skips the file to avoid overwriting your work. Auto-seeded defaults (like the template `SOUL.md`) are replaced with your imported content.
    42→
    43→### Multi-agent support
    44→
    45→If your OpenClaw installation has multiple agents (defined in `openclaw.json`'s `agents.list` or detected from `agents/` directories), all of them are imported:
    46→
    47→- The **default agent** becomes Moltis's `main` agent
    48→- **Non-default agents** are created as separate agent personas with their name, theme, and emoji
    49→- **Per-agent workspace files** (`SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, etc.) are copied to `~/.moltis/agents/<id>/`, giving each agent its own personality
    50→- **Per-agent sessions** are prefixed with `oc:<agent_id>:` so they appear under the correct agent
    51→- Agents without per-agent workspace files inherit from the root files automatically
    52→
    53→## Importing via Web UI
    54→
    55→### During Onboarding
    56→
    57→If Moltis detects an OpenClaw installation at first launch, an **Import** step appears in the onboarding wizard before the identity and provider steps. You can select which categories to import using checkboxes, then proceed with the rest of setup.
    58→
    59→### From Settings
    60→
    61→1. Go to **Settings** (gear icon)
    62→2. Select **OpenClaw Import** from the sidebar
    63→3. Click **Scan** to see what data is available
    64→4. Check the categories you want to import
    65→5. Click **Import Selected**
    66→
    67→The import section only appears when an OpenClaw installation is detected.
    68→
    69→## Importing via CLI
    70→
    71→The `moltis import` command provides three subcommands:
    72→
    73→### Detect
    74→
    75→Check whether an OpenClaw installation exists and preview what can be imported:
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→moltis import detect
    79→```
    80→
    81→Example output:
    82→
    83→```
    84→OpenClaw installation detected at /Users/you/.openclaw
    85→
    86→  Identity:        available (agent: "friday")
    87→  Providers:       available (2 auth profiles)
    88→  Skills:          3 skills found
    89→  Memory:          available (MEMORY.md + 12 memory files)
    90→  Channels:        available (1 Telegram account)
    91→  Sessions:        47 session files across 2 agents
    92→  MCP Servers:     4 servers configured
    93→  Workspace Files: SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, TOOLS.md, HEARTBEAT.md
    94→```
    95→
    96→Use `--json` for machine-readable output:
    97→
    98→```bash
    99→moltis import detect --json
   100→```
   101→
   102→### Import All
   103→
   104→Import everything at once:
   105→
   106→```bash
   107→moltis import all
   108→```
   109→
   110→Preview what would happen without writing anything:
   111→
   112→```bash
   113→moltis import all --dry-run
   114→```
   115→
   116→### Import Selected Categories
   117→
   118→Import only specific categories:
   119→
   120→```bash
   121→moltis import select -c providers,skills,memory
   122→```
   123→
   124→Valid category names: `identity`, `providers`, `skills`, `memory`, `channels`, `sessions`, `mcp_servers`, `workspace-files`.
   125→
   126→Combine with `--dry-run` to preview:
   127→
   128→```bash
   129→moltis import select -c sessions --dry-run
   130→```
   131→
   132→## Importing via RPC
   133→
   134→Three RPC methods are available for programmatic access:
   135→
   136→| Method | Description |
   137→|--------|-------------|
   138→| `openclaw.detect` | Returns detection and scan results (what data is available) |
   139→| `openclaw.scan` | Alias for `openclaw.detect` |
   140→| `openclaw.import` | Performs the import with a selection object |
   141→
   142→Example `openclaw.import` params:
   143→
   144→```json
   145→{
   146→  "identity": true,
   147→  "providers": true,
   148→  "skills": true,
   149→  "memory": true,
   150→  "channels": false,
   151→  "sessions": false,
   152→  "mcp_servers": true,
   153→  "workspace_files": true
   154→}
   155→```
   156→
   157→The response includes a report with per-category status (`imported`, `skipped`, `error`) and counts.
   158→
   159→## Incremental Session Import
   160→
   161→If you continue using OpenClaw after the initial import, Moltis will detect new messages when you re-import. Sessions are compared by source file line count — if the source JSONL has grown since the last import, Moltis re-converts the full session and updates the metadata.
   162→
   163→On incremental update:
   164→- The session's original `id` and `created_at` are preserved
   165→- The `version` field is bumped
   166→- The markdown transcript is regenerated with all messages
   167→- The CLI report shows updated sessions separately: `2 imported, 1 updated, 3 skipped`
   168→
   169→Legacy metadata (from imports before incremental support) will trigger a one-time catch-up re-import to establish the baseline line count.
   170→
   171→## Automatic Background Syncing
   172→
   173→When the `file-watcher` feature is enabled (default), Moltis automatically watches the OpenClaw sessions directory for changes. Any new or appended session files are synced incrementally within seconds, without requiring a manual re-import.
   174→
   175→**How it works:**
   176→
   177→- Moltis uses OS-level file notifications (FSEvents on macOS, inotify on Linux) to detect `.jsonl` file changes in the OpenClaw sessions directory
   178→- Events are debounced with a 5-second window to batch rapid writes during active conversations
   179→- A 60-second periodic fallback ensures changes are caught even if file notifications are missed
   180→- Only sessions are synced automatically — provider keys, memory, skills, and other categories are handled by the manual import or their own dedicated watchers
   181→
   182→**What gets synced:**
   183→
   184→- New session files are imported with `oc:` prefixed keys
   185→- Existing sessions that have grown (new messages appended) are re-converted and updated
   186→- Markdown transcripts are regenerated for updated sessions so they remain searchable
   187→- Session metadata (`id`, `created_at`) is preserved across updates
   188→
   189→The watcher starts automatically at gateway startup when an OpenClaw installation is detected. You can see the status in the startup logs:
   190→
   191→```
   192→openclaw: session watcher started
   193→```
   194→
   195→To disable automatic syncing, compile without the `file-watcher` feature.
   196→
   197→## Idempotency
   198→
   199→Running the import multiple times is safe:
   200→
   201→- **Memory** uses an `<!-- Imported from OpenClaw -->` marker to avoid duplicating `MEMORY.md` content. Individual memory files skip if they already exist at the destination
   202→- **Skills** skip directories that already exist in the Moltis skills folder
   203→- **MCP servers** skip entries with matching names
   204→- **Sessions** use `oc:` prefixed keys that won't collide with native Moltis sessions. Unchanged sessions (same line count) are skipped; grown sessions are re-converted
   205→- **Provider keys** merge with existing keys without overwriting
   206→- **Workspace files** skip if the destination already has user content; replace only auto-seeded defaults
   207→
   208→## Provider Name Mapping
   209→
   210→OpenClaw and Moltis use different names for some providers:
   211→
   212→| OpenClaw Name | Moltis Name |
   213→|---------------|-------------|
   214→| `google` | `gemini` |
   215→| `anthropic` | `anthropic` |
   216→| `openai` | `openai` |
   217→| `openrouter` | `openrouter` |
   218→
   219→Unmapped provider names are passed through as-is.
   220→
   221→## Unsupported Channels
   222→
   223→Currently only Telegram and Discord channels are imported. If your OpenClaw configuration includes other channel types (Slack, WhatsApp, etc.), they will appear as warnings in the scan output but will not be imported.
   224→
   225→## Troubleshooting
   226→
   227→### Import not detected
   228→
   229→- Verify the OpenClaw directory exists: `ls ~/.openclaw/`
   230→- If using a custom path, set `OPENCLAW_HOME=/path/to/openclaw`
   231→- If using profiles, set `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=your-profile`
   232→
   233→### Provider keys not working after import
   234→
   235→OpenClaw stores API keys in agent auth-profiles. If the key was rotated or expired in OpenClaw, the imported key will also be invalid. Re-enter the key in **Settings** > **Providers**.
   236→
   237→### Memory import appears incomplete
   238→
   239→The import brings over `MEMORY.md` and all `.md` files from the `memory/` directory (daily logs, project notes, custom files). Non-markdown files are skipped. OpenClaw's SQLite vector database is not imported because embeddings are not portable across models — Moltis will re-index the imported files automatically.
   240→
   241→### Session transcripts
   242→
   243→When sessions are imported, Moltis also generates markdown transcripts in `~/.moltis/memory/sessions/`. These contain the user/assistant conversation text and are indexed by the memory system, making your imported OpenClaw conversations searchable.
   244→
   245→### Workspace files not appearing
   246→
   247→If a workspace file wasn't imported, it may already exist at the destination with custom content. The import never overwrites user-customized files. Check `~/.moltis/SOUL.md` (or `~/.moltis/agents/<id>/SOUL.md` for non-default agents) to see what's there. You can delete it and re-import to get the OpenClaw version.
   248→

16→## What Gets Imported
    17→
    18→| Category | Source | Destination | Notes |
    19→|----------|--------|-------------|-------|
    20→| **Identity** | `openclaw.json` agent name, theme, and timezone | `moltis.toml` identity section | Preserves existing Moltis identity if already configured |
    21→| **Providers** | Agent auth-profiles (API keys) | `~/.moltis/provider_keys.json` | Maps OpenClaw provider names to Moltis equivalents (e.g., `google` becomes `gemini`) |
    22→| **Skills** | `skills/` directories with `SKILL.md` | `~/.moltis/skills/` | Copies entire skill directories; skips duplicates |

    24→| **Channels** | Telegram and Discord bot configuration in `openclaw.json` | `moltis.toml` channels section | Supports both flat and multi-account Telegram configs |

     5→
     6→# CLAUDE.md Style Guide
     7→
     8→CLAUDE.md はプロジェクト固有の指示を Claude に提供するファイルです。コンテキストウィンドウを消費するため、簡潔かつ効果的な内容にすることが重要です。
     9→
    10→## Core Principles
    11→
    12→1. **簡潔さ優先**: コンテキストを消費するため、必要最小限の情報のみ記載
    13→2. **具体性**: 抽象的な説明より具体例を優先
    14→3. **実用性**: 実際の摩擦点を解決する内容のみ含める
    15→4. **境界設定**: Always/Ask first/Never の明確な区分
    16→
    17→## Required Sections
    18→
    19→### 日本語使用時のスタイリング
    20→
    21→必須で含める内容:
    22→
    23→```markdown
    24→# 日本語使用時のスタイリング
    25→
    26→ドキュメントやコードコメントなど、特に指示がない限りは下記を厳守します。
    27→
    28→- 技術用語や固有名詞は原文を維持
    29→- スペース: 日本語と半角英数字記号間に半角スペース
    30→- 文体: ですます調、句読点は「。」「、」
    31→  - 箇条書きリストやチェックリストはこの限りではない
    32→- 記号: 丸括弧は半角「()」、鉤括弧は全角「「」」
    33→
    34→例:
    35→
    36→- Terraform は、素晴らしい IaC (Infrastructure as Code) ツールです。
    37→- Claude Code は、Anthropic 社が開発しているエージェント型 AI コーディングツールです。
    38→```
    39→
    40→### コード参照
    41→
    42→```markdown
    43→# コード参照
    44→
    45→参照元・参照先の調査は Grep ではなく LSP を使用 (goToDefinition, findReferences, incomingCalls, outgoingCalls)
    46→```
    47→
    48→### 技術調査
    49→
    50→<!-- prettier-ignore -->
    51→```markdown
    52→# 技術調査
    53→
    54→優先順位: LSP → deepwiki MCP → Gemini MCP → context7 MCP → WebSearch
    55→
    56→※ Gemini MCP は mcp__gemini__ask-gemini で google_web_search を使用
    57→```
    58→
    59→## Content Guidelines
    60→
    61→### Include (効果的な内容)
    62→
    63→- 繰り返し入力するコマンド
    64→- アーキテクチャコンテキスト (コンポーネント間の関係)
    65→- ドメイン固有のパターン・規約
    66→- プロジェクト固有のワークフロー
    67→- ツール統合情報 (MCP サーバー等)
    68→
    69→### Exclude (含めるべきでない内容)
    70→
    71→- センシティブ情報 (API キー、認証情報、DB 接続文字列)
    72→- Claude が既に知っている一般的なベストプラクティス
    73→- IDE やエディタの使い方
    74→- 言語やフレームワークの基本的な構文
    75→- 冗長な説明文
    76→
    77→## Structure Recommendations
    78→
    79→### Optimal Length
    80→
    81→- 目標: 500-1,500 words
    82→- 最大: 3,000 words
    83→- 超過時: 内容を精査し、不要な情報を削除
    84→
    85→### Section Priority
    86→
    87→1. 必須: プロジェクト概要 (1-2 文)
    88→2. 必須: 主要コマンド
    89→3. 必須: スタイリングルール
    90→4. 推奨: アーキテクチャ概要
    91→5. 推奨: ワークフロー
    92→6. オプション: 詳細な規約 (別ファイル参照)
    93→
    94→## Boundary Setting Pattern
    95→
    96→3 層システムで行動境界を設定:
    97→
    98→```markdown
    99→# 行動ルール
   100→
   101→## 即座実行 (確認不要)
   102→
   103→- コード操作、ファイル管理
   104→- テスト実行
   105→- ドキュメント更新
   106→
   107→## 確認必須
   108→
   109→- アーキテクチャ変更
   110→- 新 API・外部ライブラリ導入
   111→- DB スキーマ変更
   112→- Git コミット・プッシュ
   113→
   114→## 禁止
   115→
   116→- 本番環境への直接操作
   117→- 認証情報のハードコード
   118→```
   119→
   120→## Optimization Strategies
   121→
   122→### Redundancy Detection
   123→
   124→以下は Claude が既知のため省略可能:
   125→
   126→- 一般的なコーディング規約 (PEP8, ESLint 等)
   127→- 標準的な Git ワークフロー
   128→- 言語固有のベストプラクティス
   129→- フレームワークの基本的な使い方
   130→
   131→### Consolidation Techniques
   132→
   133→- 類似ルールを統合
   134→- 例外は別途記載せず、ルールに組み込む
   135→- 詳細は外部ファイル参照 (`docs/` 等)
   136→
   137→### Update Checklist
   138→
   139→CLAUDE.md 更新時の確認項目:
   140→
   141→1. 重複コンテンツはないか
   142→2. Claude が既知の内容が含まれていないか
   143→3. 具体例 > 説明文の原則を守っているか
   144→4. 実際に使用されている情報か
   145→5. 境界設定は明確か
   146→
   147→## Quick Reference
   148→
   149→### Good Example
   150→
   151→```markdown
   152→# MyProject
   153→
   154→React + TypeScript のダッシュボードアプリ。
   155→
   156→## コマンド
   157→
   158→- `bun dev`: 開発サーバー起動
   159→- `bun test`: テスト実行
   160→- `bun lint`: Lint チェック
   161→
   162→## 日本語スタイリング
   163→
   164→[Required section content]
   165→
   166→## アーキテクチャ
   167→
   168→- `src/components/`: UI コンポーネント
   169→- `src/hooks/`: カスタム Hooks
   170→- `src/api/`: API クライアント
   171→```
   172→
   173→### Bad Example
   174→
   175→```markdown
   176→# MyProject
   177→
   178→これは React と TypeScript で作られたダッシュボードアプリケーションです。
   179→React は Facebook が開発した JavaScript ライブラリで...
   180→[冗長な説明が続く]
   181→
   182→## 開発方法
   183→
   184→開発を始めるには、まず依存関係をインストールします。
   185→npm install または yarn install を実行してください...
   186→[Claude が既知の内容]
   187→```
   188→
   189→## Implementation Workflow
   190→
   191→CLAUDE.md 作成時:
   192→
   193→1. プロジェクト構造を分析
   194→2. 必須セクションを追加
   195→3. プロジェクト固有の情報を追加
   196→4. 冗長性を確認・削除
   197→5. 文字数を確認 (1,500 words 以下目標)
   198→
   199→CLAUDE.md 更新時:
   200→
   201→1. 現在の内容を読み込み
   202→2. 各セクションの必要性を評価
   203→3. 冗長・重複コンテンツを特定
   204→4. 必須セクションの準拠確認
   205→5. 最適化・統合

1→# Generic Webhooks Plan
     2→
     3→## Summary
     4→
     5→Add a first-class **generic webhook** feature to Moltis so users can create
     6→named inbound HTTP endpoints from the web UI, bind them to an agent persona,
     7→apply execution restrictions, and turn each delivery into a persistent chat
     8→session that can be inspected and continued later.
     9→
    10→This should be a new feature area, not a hack on top of channel webhooks.
    11→Existing channel webhook middleware is for platform adapters like Slack and
    12→Teams, not for arbitrary user-defined webhook ingress.
    13→
    14→## Goals
    15→
    16→- Let users create, edit, view, and delete generic webhooks from the web UI.
    17→- Give each webhook a stable public endpoint with a high-entropy identifier.
    18→- Bind a webhook to an existing agent persona.
    19→- Allow webhook-specific execution overrides:
    20→  - model override
    21→  - extra system prompt suffix
    22→  - tool allow/deny policy
    23→  - optional sandbox override
    24→- Support common webhook authentication patterns used by major senders.
    25→- Persist every accepted delivery with metadata, status, and session linkage.
    26→- Create a normal persistent chat session per delivery by default.
    27→- Make resulting sessions easy to inspect and continue in the standard chat UI.
    28→- Expose clear examples in the admin UI, especially GitHub and GitLab flows.
    29→
    30→## Non-Goals
    31→
    32→- Do not make generic webhooks part of the existing `channels` feature.
    33→- Do not require users to define a full new agent per webhook.
    34→- Do not block webhook HTTP responses on full LLM execution.
    35→- Do not attempt a full workflow engine in v1.
    36→- Do not implement provider-specific adapters for every source in v1.
    37→
    38→## Product Shape
    39→
    40→### Conceptual Model
    41→
    42→A generic webhook is:
    43→
    44→- a public endpoint
    45→- a verification policy
    46→- a delivery log
    47→- an execution target
    48→
    49→The execution target should be:
    50→
    51→- an existing `agent_id`
    52→- plus optional webhook-local overrides
    53→
    54→This keeps Moltis aligned with existing agent personas and workspace files:
    55→
    56→- `IDENTITY.md`
    57→- `SOUL.md`
    58→- `AGENTS.md`
    59→- `TOOLS.md`
    60→
    61→The webhook should not define a completely separate identity stack unless we
    62→later decide generic webhooks are their own long-lived agent type.
    63→
    64→### Default Execution Behavior
    65→
    66→Default behavior for each accepted delivery:
    67→
    68→1. Verify auth and source policy.
    69→2. Deduplicate replayed deliveries.
    70→3. Persist the delivery record.
    71→4. Return `202 Accepted` quickly.
    72→5. Spawn async processing.
    73→6. Create a new persistent named session.
    74→7. Assign the configured `agent_id` to that session.
    75→8. Inject a normalized inbound message into chat.
    76→9. Run `chat.send`.
    77→10. Update delivery status and link to the resulting session.
    78→
    79→This should mirror cron in spirit, but each delivery should get its own
    80→persistent conversation by default so debugging stays sane.
    81→
    82→## Why Not Reuse Channels
    83→
    84→Channels are human-facing messaging surfaces with reply routing, streaming,
    85→presence semantics, and platform-specific behavior.
    86→
    87→Generic webhooks are infrastructure ingress. They do not map well to:
    88→
    89→- DM/group policies
    90→- outbound reply targets
    91→- channel account setup flows
    92→- channel capability flags
    93→
    94→The clean boundary is:
    95→
    96→- `channels`: human messaging transports
    97→- `webhooks`: machine event ingress
    98→
    99→## Session Model
   100→
   101→### Default
   102→
   103→Use **one new persistent session per delivery**.
   104→
   105→Reasons:
   106→
   107→- Easier debugging
   108→- Cleaner history
   109→- Easy to resume manually from the UI
   110→- Avoids one giant mixed thread from unrelated events
   111→
   112→### Optional Advanced Mode
   113→
   114→Support an advanced session strategy later:
   115→
   116→- `per_delivery` (default)
   117→- `named_session`
   118→
   119→`named_session` is useful for intentionally accumulative workflows, but should
   120→not be the default because it will become a garbage heap almost immediately.
   121→
   122→### Session Labels
   123→
   124→Suggested default label format:
   125→
   126→- `{webhook name} #{sequence}`
   127→
   128→Examples:
   129→
   130→- `GitHub PR Hook #42`
   131→- `Ops Alerts #7`
   132→
   133→Optional suffixes can include normalized event type:
   134→
   135→- `GitHub PR Hook #42 (pull_request.opened)`
   136→
   137→## Delivery Message Format
   138→
   139→The inbound message injected into chat should be normalized and stable, not raw
   140→verbatim headers pasted into the prompt in an ad hoc way.
   141→
   142→Suggested structure:
   143→
   144→```text
   145→Webhook delivery received.
   146→
   147→Webhook:
   148→- name: GitHub PR Hook
   149→- id: wh_xxxxx
   150→- source_type: github
   151→- event_type: pull_request
   152→- delivery_id: 12345678-...
   153→- received_at: 2026-04-06T12:34:56Z
   154→
   155→Request metadata:
   156→- method: POST
   157→- content_type: application/json
   158→- remote_ip: 203.0.113.10
   159→
   160→Selected headers:
   161→- x-github-event: pull_request
   162→- x-github-delivery: ...
   163→
   164→JSON payload:
   165→{...pretty-printed body...}
   166→```
   167→
   168→Rules:
   169→
   170→- Pretty-print JSON when payload is JSON.
   171→- For non-JSON payloads, include a safe body preview plus raw bytes length.
   172→- Redact known secrets.
   173→- Truncate large bodies and attach a note when truncation occurs.
   174→- Persist the full delivery body separately so the UI can inspect it.
   175→
   176→## Auth and Source Verification
   177→
   178→## Supported Modes for V1
   179→
   180→- `none`
   181→  - Only acceptable for local/testing. UI should warn loudly.
   182→- `static_header`
   183→  - User configures header name and expected value.
   184→- `bearer`
   185→  - Expect `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
   186→- `github_hmac_sha256`
   187→  - Verify `X-Hub-Signature-256` against configured secret.
   188→- `gitlab_token`
   189→  - Verify `X-Gitlab-Token` against configured secret.
   190→- `cidr_allowlist`
   191→  - Optional additional policy layered on top of auth mode.
   192→
   193→## Source Profiles
   194→
   195→The UI should expose convenient source presets:
   196→
   197→- Generic
   198→- GitHub
   199→- GitLab
   200→
   201→These presets prefill:
   202→
   203→- recommended auth mode
   204→- expected headers
   205→- example payload docs
   206→
   207→### GitHub Notes
   208→
   209→GitHub supports:
   210→
   211→- webhook secret with HMAC signature verification
   212→- delivery IDs for idempotency
   213→- event type headers
   214→- documented sender IP ranges
   215→
   216→Design guidance:
   217→
   218→- Verify `X-Hub-Signature-256`
   219→- Use `X-GitHub-Delivery` as the primary external idempotency key
   220→- Optionally layer CIDR allowlisting from GitHub meta IP ranges later
   221→
   222→Reference:
   223→
   224→- <https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries>
   225→- <https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks>
   226→
   227→### GitLab Notes
   228→
   229→GitLab supports:
   230→
   231→- `X-Gitlab-Token`
   232→- custom headers
   233→- `Idempotency-Key`
   234→
   235→Design guidance:
   236→
   237→- Verify `X-Gitlab-Token`
   238→- Use `Idempotency-Key` when present, otherwise derive a fallback key
   239→
   240→Reference:
   241→
   242→- <https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/integrations/webhooks/>
   243→
   244→## Security Requirements
   245→
   246→- Public webhook ID must be random and high entropy, not sequential.
   247→- ID is not authentication, only routing.
   248→- Authentication should use headers by default, not query params.
   249→- Support query-based auth only as an advanced escape hatch if added later.
   250→- Enforce request body size limits.
   251→- Enforce request timeout and fast acknowledgment behavior.
   252→- Persist rejection reasons for observability where safe.
   253→- Redact secrets in logs and UI.
   254→- Deduplicate deliveries.
   255→- Add rate limiting:
   256→  - per webhook
   257→  - global
   258→- Support CIDR allowlists as an additional guardrail.
   259→- Validate content types but do not reject valid JSON just because the sender
   260→  forgot the exact perfect header.
   261→
   262→## Data Model
   263→
   264→Add a dedicated webhook store, not a config-file-only feature.
   265→
   266→Likely tables:
   267→
   268→### `webhooks`
   269→
   270→- `id`
   271→- `name`
   272→- `description`
   273→- `enabled`
   274→- `public_id`
   275→- `agent_id`
   276→- `model`
   277→- `system_prompt_suffix`
   278→- `tool_policy_json`
   279→- `sandbox_policy_json`
   280→- `auth_mode`
   281→- `auth_config_json`
   282→- `source_profile`
   283→- `session_mode`
   284→- `named_session_key`
   285→- `allowed_cidrs_json`
   286→- `max_body_bytes`
   287→- `created_at`
   288→- `updated_at`
   289→
   290→### `webhook_deliveries`
   291→
   292→- `id`
   293→- `webhook_id`
   294→- `received_at`
   295→- `status`
   296→- `event_type`
   297→- `delivery_key`
   298→- `http_method`
   299→- `content_type`
   300→- `remote_ip`
   301→- `headers_json`
   302→- `body_bytes`
   303→- `body_storage_path` or blob reference
   304→- `session_key`
   305→- `run_error`
   306→- `started_at`
   307→- `finished_at`
   308→- `duration_ms`
   309→
   310→### Status Values
   311→
   312→- `received`
   313→- `deduplicated`
   314→- `rejected`
   315→- `queued`
   316→- `processing`
   317→- `completed`
   318→- `failed`
   319→
   320→## Execution Config
   321→
   322→The webhook should point at an existing `agent_id`, then layer overrides.
   323→
   324→### Why
   325→
   326→Moltis already has:
   327→
   328→- persona workspaces
   329→- per-session agent binding
   330→- prompt assembly from agent files
   331→
   332→Using `agent_id` preserves:
   333→
   334→- identity
   335→- soul
   336→- workspace instructions
   337→- memory boundaries
   338→
   339→Webhook-local overrides should be intentionally narrow:
   340→
   341→- `model`
   342→- `system_prompt_suffix`
   343→- `tool allow/deny`
   344→- `sandbox policy`
   345→
   346→### Important Implementation Detail
   347→
   348→Today, prompt persona and runtime tool filtering are loaded from the effective
   349→agent config during chat execution. We should make webhook overrides flow into
   350→that same runtime path instead of inventing a separate ad hoc executor.
   351→
   352→This likely requires adding a notion of **session-scoped execution overrides**
   353→or **webhook execution profile** so webhook sessions can:
   354→
   355→- keep agent persona files
   356→- apply tool restrictions
   357→- apply model override
   358→- append extra prompt text
   359→
   360→without mutating the base agent permanently.
   361→
   362→## HTTP API
   363→
   364→### Public Ingress
   365→
   366→- `POST /api/webhooks/{public_id}`
   367→
   368→Behavior:
   369→
   370→- Accept raw body bytes and headers
   371→- Verify according to webhook config
   372→- Persist delivery record
   373→- Queue async execution
   374→- Return fast acknowledgment
   375→
   376→Response suggestions:
   377→
   378→- `202 Accepted` on success
   379→- `401` or `403` on auth failure
   380→- `404` for unknown or disabled webhook
   381→- `409` or `200` for duplicates, depending on semantics chosen
   382→- `413` for payload too large
   383→- `429` for rate limiting
   384→
   385→### Admin / UI RPC or API
   386→
   387→Add CRUD and listing methods similar to existing settings surfaces:
   388→
   389→- `webhooks.list`
   390→- `webhooks.get`
   391→- `webhooks.create`
   392→- `webhooks.update`
   393→- `webhooks.delete`
   394→- `webhooks.deliveries`
   395→- `webhooks.delivery.get`
   396→- `webhooks.delivery.retry` (optional later)
   397→
   398→## Background Processing
   399→
   400→Processing must not happen inline in the HTTP request path.
   401→
   402→Reason:
   403→
   404→- GitHub recommends quick responses
   405→- GitLab retries if receivers are slow
   406→- LLM work is variable and can be long-running
   407→
   408→Preferred flow:
   409→
   410→1. HTTP handler validates and stores delivery.
   411→2. Delivery ID is queued onto a Tokio worker channel.
   412→3. Worker loads webhook config and delivery body.
   413→4. Worker creates session and assigns agent.
   414→5. Worker injects normalized message into `chat.send`.
   415→6. Worker stores final status and session linkage.
   416→
   417→This should be durable enough that crashes do not silently drop accepted
   418→deliveries. If possible, queue state should be reconstructible from persisted
   419→`received` or `queued` rows on startup.
   420→
   421→## UI Plan
   422→
   423→Add a dedicated settings page:
   424→
   425→- `Settings -> Webhooks`
   426→
   427→### Main View
   428→
   429→- Webhook table or cards
   430→- status badge
   431→- source profile
   432→- target agent
   433→- last delivery time
   434→- delivery counts
   435→- enabled toggle
   436→
   437→### Create / Edit Modal
   438→
   439→Fields:
   440→
   441→- name
   442→- description
   443→- source profile
   444→- auth mode
   445→- secret/token/header config
   446→- allowed CIDRs
   447→- target agent
   448→- model override
   449→- system prompt suffix
   450→- tool allow list
   451→- tool deny list
   452→- session mode
   453→- optional sandbox override
   454→
   455→Show generated endpoint clearly with copy button.
   456→
   457→### Delivery Inspector
   458→
   459→For each webhook:
   460→
   461→- recent deliveries list
   462→- status
   463→- event type
   464→- received time
   465→- session link
   466→- error details
   467→
   468→Per delivery:
   469→
   470→- normalized metadata
   471→- selected headers
   472→- body preview
   473→- raw body download if useful
   474→
   475→### Example Recipes
   476→
   477→The page should include examples such as:
   478→
   479→- GitHub PR opened
   480→- GitHub push to main
   481→- GitLab merge request opened
   482→- Generic JSON event from another service
   483→- Internal system posting alerts to Moltis
   484→
   485→This matters because users will otherwise stare at a blank form and invent
   486→terrible security setups.
   487→
   488→## Recommended UX Defaults
   489→
   490→- default source profile: `Generic`
   491→- default auth mode: `static_header`
   492→- default session mode: `per_delivery`
   493→- default target agent: current default agent
   494→- default body limit: conservative, for example 256 KB or 1 MB
   495→- default response mode: async `202`
   496→- default tool policy: inherit agent
   497→- default sandbox policy: inherit agent/session defaults
   498→
   499→## Observability
   500→
   501→Add metrics:
   502→
   503→- deliveries received
   504→- deliveries rejected
   505→- deliveries deduplicated
   506→- deliveries processed
   507→- processing duration
   508→- failures by webhook
   509→- failures by auth mode
   510→
   511→Add delivery logs that do not leak secrets.
   512→
   513→Expose recent delivery status in the web UI.
   514→
   515→## Testing Plan
   516→
   517→### Unit Tests
   518→
   519→- auth verification per mode
   520→- dedup behavior
   521→- payload normalization
   522→- session label generation
   523→- config validation
   524→- CIDR matching
   525→
   526→### Integration Tests
   527→
   528→- POST accepted delivery creates session
   529→- accepted delivery runs `chat.send`
   530→- rejected auth does not create session
   531→- duplicate delivery does not double-run
   532→- model override is applied
   533→- agent binding is applied
   534→- tool restrictions are applied
   535→
   536→### Web UI / E2E
   537→
   538→- create webhook in settings
   539→- edit webhook
   540→- delete webhook
   541→- inspect deliveries
   542→- follow delivery to chat session
   543→
   544→## Migration / Rollout
   545→
   546→### Phase 1
   547→
   548→- backend schema and store
   549→- public ingress endpoint
   550→- minimal auth modes
   551→- async execution worker
   552→- session creation and session linkage
   553→- basic UI CRUD
   554→
   555→### Phase 2
   556→
   557→- richer source presets
   558→- CIDR allowlists
   559→- delivery inspector
   560→- session strategy options
   561→- better retry and replay support
   562→
   563→### Phase 3
   564→
   565→- more providers
   566→- templated event extraction
   567→- richer trigger filters
   568→- optional workflow chaining
   569→
   570→## Open Questions
   571→
   572→- Should webhook sessions be tagged as a new session kind, for example
   573→  `webhook`, in runtime context?
   574→- Should a webhook be able to post follow-up outbound messages to channels, or
   575→  is that just normal tool use from the agent?
   576→- Should we support a tiny structured extraction layer in v1, for example
   577→  "prepend this template with selected JSON fields", or keep v1 raw and simple?
   578→- Should we store full payloads in SQLite blobs or on disk with references?
   579→- Do we want delivery replay from the UI in v1 or wait until the delivery model
   580→  has settled?
   581→
   582→## Recommendation
   583→
   584→Build this as a **new top-level feature** using the existing agent/session/chat
   585→primitives. The key design constraint is to avoid creating a second independent
   586→agent configuration system.
   587→
   588→The clean path is:
   589→
   590→- webhook targets an existing `agent_id`
   591→- webhook adds narrow execution overrides
   592→- each accepted delivery becomes a normal persistent chat session
   593→
   594→That gives users the feature they want without turning Moltis into a haunted
   595→forest of overlapping config models.

   126→- `{webhook name} #{sequence}`
   127→
   128→Examples:
   129→
   130→- `GitHub PR Hook #42`
   131→- `Ops Alerts #7`
   132→
   133→Optional suffixes can include normalized event type:
   134→
   135→- `GitHub PR Hook #42 (pull_request.opened)`
   136→
   137→## Delivery Message Format
   138→
   139→The inbound message injected into chat should be normalized and stable, not raw
   140→verbatim headers pasted into the prompt in an ad hoc way.
   141→
   142→Suggested structure:
   143→
   144→```text
   145→Webhook delivery received.
   146→
   147→Webhook:
   148→- name: GitHub PR Hook
   149→- id: wh_xxxxx
   150→- source_type: github
   151→- event_type: pull_request
   152→- delivery_id: 12345678-...
   153→- received_at: 2026-04-06T12:34:56Z
   154→
   155→Request metadata:
   156→- method: POST
   157→- content_type: application/json
   158→- remote_ip: 203.0.113.10
   159→
   160→Selected headers:
   161→- x-github-event: pull_request
   162→- x-github-delivery: ...
   163→
   164→JSON payload:
   165→{...pretty-printed body...}
   166→```
   167→
   168→Rules:
   169→
   170→- Pretty-print JSON when payload is JSON.
   171→- For non-JSON payloads, include a safe body preview plus raw bytes length.
   172→- Redact known secrets.
   173→- Truncate large bodies and attach a note when truncation occurs.
   174→- Persist the full delivery body separately so the UI can inspect it.
   175→
   176→## Auth and Source Verification
   177→
   178→## Supported Modes for V1
   179→
   180→- `none`
   181→  - Only acceptable for local/testing. UI should warn loudly.
   182→- `static_header`
   183→  - User configures header name and expected value.
   184→- `bearer`
   185→  - Expect `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
   186→- `github_hmac_sha256`
   187→  - Verify `X-Hub-Signature-256` against configured secret.
   188→- `gitlab_token`
   189→  - Verify `X-Gitlab-Token` against configured secret.
   190→- `cidr_allowlist`
   191→  - Optional additional policy layered on top of auth mode.
   192→
   193→## Source Profiles
   194→
   195→The UI should expose convenient source presets:
   196→
   197→- Generic
   198→- GitHub
   199→- GitLab
   200→
   201→These presets prefill:
   202→
   203→- recommended auth mode
   204→- expected headers
   205→- example payload docs
   206→
   207→### GitHub Notes
   208→
   209→GitHub supports:
   210→
   211→- webhook secret with HMAC signature verification
   212→- delivery IDs for idempotency
   213→- event type headers
   214→- documented sender IP ranges
   215→
   216→Design guidance:
   217→
   218→- Verify `X-Hub-Signature-256`
   219→- Use `X-GitHub-Delivery` as the primary external idempotency key
   220→- Optionally layer CIDR allowlisting from GitHub meta IP ranges later
   221→
   222→Reference:
   223→
   224→- <https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries>
   225→- <https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks>
   226→
   227→### GitLab Notes
   228→
   229→GitLab supports:
   230→
   231→- `X-Gitlab-Token`
   232→- custom headers
   233→- `Idempotency-Key`
   234→
   235→Design guidance:
   236→
   237→- Verify `X-Gitlab-Token`
   238→- Use `Idempotency-Key` when present, otherwise derive a fallback key
   239→
   240→Reference:
   241→
   242→- <https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/integrations/webhooks/>
   243→
   244→## Security Requirements
   245→
   246→- Public webhook ID must be random and high entropy, not sequential.
   247→- ID is not authentication, only routing.
   248→- Authentication should use headers by default, not query params.
   249→- Support query-based auth only as an advanced escape hatch if added later.
   250→- Enforce request body size limits.
   251→- Enforce request timeout and fast acknowledgment behavior.
   252→- Persist rejection reasons for observability where safe.
   253→- Redact secrets in logs and UI.
   254→- Deduplicate deliveries.
   255→- Add rate limiting:
   256→  - per webhook
   257→  - global
   258→- Support CIDR allowlists as an additional guardrail.
   259→- Validate content types but do not reject valid JSON just because the sender
   260→  forgot the exact perfect header.
   261→
   262→## Data Model
   263→
   264→Add a dedicated webhook store, not a config-file-only feature.
   265→
   266→Likely tables:
   267→
   268→### `webhooks`
   269→
   270→- `id`
   271→- `name`
   272→- `description`
   273→- `enabled`
   274→- `public_id`
   275→- `agent_id`
   276→- `model`
   277→- `system_prompt_suffix`
   278→- `tool_policy_json`
   279→- `sandbox_policy_json`
   280→- `auth_mode`
   281→- `auth_config_json`
   282→- `source_profile`
   283→- `session_mode`
   284→- `named_session_key`
   285→- `allowed_cidrs_json`
   286→- `max_body_bytes`
   287→- `created_at`
   288→- `updated_at`
   289→
   290→### `webhook_deliveries`
   291→
   292→- `id`
   293→- `webhook_id`
   294→- `received_at`
   295→- `status`
   296→- `event_type`
   297→- `delivery_key`
   298→- `http_method`
   299→- `content_type`
   300→- `remote_ip`
   301→- `headers_json`
   302→- `body_bytes`
   303→- `body_storage_path` or blob reference
   304→- `session_key`
   305→- `run_error`
   306→- `started_at`
   307→- `finished_at`
   308→- `duration_ms`
   309→
   310→### Status Values
   311→
   312→- `received`
   313→- `deduplicated`
   314→- `rejected`
   315→- `queued`
   316→- `processing`
   317→- `completed`
   318→- `failed`
   319→
   320→## Execution Config
   321→
   322→The webhook should point at an existing `agent_id`, then layer overrides.
   323→
   324→### Why
   325→
   326→Moltis already has:
   327→
   328→- persona workspaces
   329→- per-session agent binding
   330→- prompt assembly from agent files
   331→
   332→Using `agent_id` preserves:
   333→
   334→- identity
   335→- soul
   336→- workspace instructions
   337→- memory boundaries
   338→
   339→Webhook-local overrides should be intentionally narrow:
   340→
   341→- `model`
   342→- `system_prompt_suffix`
   343→- `tool allow/deny`
   344→- `sandbox policy`
   345→
   346→### Important Implementation Detail
   347→
   348→Today, prompt persona and runtime tool filtering are loaded from the effective
   349→agent config during chat execution. We should make webhook overrides flow into
   350→that same runtime path instead of inventing a separate ad hoc executor.
   351→
   352→This likely requires adding a notion of **session-scoped execution overrides**
   353→or **webhook execution profile** so webhook sessions can:
   354→
   355→- keep agent persona files
   356→- apply tool restrictions
   357→- apply model override
   358→- append extra prompt text
   359→
   360→without mutating the base agent permanently.
   361→
   362→## HTTP API
   363→
   364→### Public Ingress
   365→
   366→- `POST /api/webhooks/{public_id}`
   367→
   368→Behavior:
   369→
   370→- Accept raw body bytes and headers
   371→- Verify according to webhook config
   372→- Persist delivery record
   373→- Queue async execution
   374→- Return fast acknowledgment
   375→
   376→Response suggestions:
   377→
   378→- `202 Accepted` on success
   379→- `401` or `403` on auth failure
   380→- `404` for unknown or disabled webhook
   381→- `409` or `200` for duplicates, depending on semantics chosen
   382→- `413` for payload too large
   383→- `429` for rate limiting
   384→
   385→### Admin / UI RPC or API
   386→
   387→Add CRUD and listing methods similar to existing settings surfaces:
   388→
   389→- `webhooks.list`
   390→- `webhooks.get`
   391→- `webhooks.create`
   392→- `webhooks.update`
   393→- `webhooks.delete`
   394→- `webhooks.deliveries`
   395→- `webhooks.delivery.get`
   396→- `webhooks.delivery.retry` (optional later)
   397→
   398→## Background Processing
   399→
   400→Processing must not happen inline in the HTTP request path.
   401→
   402→Reason:
   403→
   404→- GitHub recommends quick responses
   405→- GitLab retries if receivers are slow
   406→- LLM work is variable and can be long-running
   407→
   408→Preferred flow:
   409→
   410→1. HTTP handler validates and stores delivery.
   411→2. Delivery ID is queued onto a Tokio worker channel.
   412→3. Worker loads webhook config and delivery body.
   413→4. Worker creates session and assigns agent.
   414→5. Worker injects normalized message into `chat.send`.
   415→6. Worker stores final status and session linkage.
   416→
   417→This should be durable enough that crashes do not silently drop accepted
   418→deliveries. If possible, queue state should be reconstructible from persisted
   419→`received` or `queued` rows on startup.
   420→
   421→## UI Plan
   422→
   423→Add a dedicated settings page:
   424→
   425→- `Settings -> Webhooks`
   426→
   427→### Main View
   428→
   429→- Webhook table or cards
   430→- status badge
   431→- source profile
   432→- target agent
   433→- last delivery time
   434→- delivery counts
   435→- enabled toggle
   436→
   437→### Create / Edit Modal
   438→
   439→Fields:
   440→
   441→- name
   442→- description
   443→- source profile
   444→- auth mode
   445→- secret/token/header config
   446→- allowed CIDRs
   447→- target agent
   448→- model override
   449→- system prompt suffix
   450→- tool allow list
   451→- tool deny list
   452→- session mode
   453→- optional sandbox override
   454→
   455→Show generated endpoint clearly with copy button.
   456→
   457→### Delivery Inspector
   458→
   459→For each webhook:
   460→
   461→- recent deliveries list
   462→- status
   463→- event type
   464→- received time
   465→- session link
   466→- error details
   467→
   468→Per delivery:
   469→
   470→- normalized metadata
   471→- selected headers
   472→- body preview
   473→- raw body download if useful
   474→
   475→### Example Recipes
   476→
   477→The page should include examples such as:
   478→
   479→- GitHub PR opened
   480→- GitHub push to main
   481→- GitLab merge request opened
   482→- Generic JSON event from another service
   483→- Internal system posting alerts to Moltis
   484→
   485→This matters because users will otherwise stare at a blank form and invent
   486→terrible security setups.
   487→
   488→## Recommended UX Defaults
   489→
   490→- default source profile: `Generic`
   491→- default auth mode: `static_header`
   492→- default session mode: `per_delivery`
   493→- default target agent: current default agent
   494→- default body limit: conservative, for example 256 KB or 1 MB
   495→- default response mode: async `202`
   496→- default tool policy: inherit agent
   497→- default sandbox policy: inherit agent/session defaults
   498→
   499→## Observability
   500→
   501→Add metrics:
   502→
   503→- deliveries received
   504→- deliveries rejected
   505→- deliveries deduplicated
   506→- deliveries processed
   507→- processing duration
   508→- failures by webhook
   509→- failures by auth mode
   510→
   511→Add delivery logs that do not leak secrets.
   512→
   513→Expose recent delivery status in the web UI.
   514→
   515→## Testing Plan
   516→
   517→### Unit Tests
   518→
   519→- auth verification per mode
   520→- dedup behavior
   521→- payload normalization
   522→- session label generation
   523→- config validation
   524→- CIDR matching
   525→
   526→### Integration Tests
   527→
   528→- POST accepted delivery creates session
   529→- accepted delivery runs `chat.send`
   530→- rejected auth does not create session
   531→- duplicate delivery does not double-run
   532→- model override is applied
   533→- agent binding is applied
   534→- tool restrictions are applied
   535→
   536→### Web UI / E2E
   537→
   538→- create webhook in settings
   539→- edit webhook
   540→- delete webhook
   541→- inspect deliveries
   542→- follow delivery to chat session
   543→
   544→## Migration / Rollout
   545→
   546→### Phase 1
   547→
   548→- backend schema and store
   549→- public ingress endpoint
   550→- minimal auth modes
   551→- async execution worker
   552→- session creation and session linkage
   553→- basic UI CRUD
   554→
   555→### Phase 2
   556→
   557→- richer source presets
   558→- CIDR allowlists
   559→- delivery inspector
   560→- session strategy options
   561→- better retry and replay support
   562→
   563→### Phase 3
   564→
   565→- more providers
   566→- templated event extraction
   567→- richer trigger filters
   568→- optional workflow chaining
   569→
   570→## Open Questions
   571→
   572→- Should webhook sessions be tagged as a new session kind, for example
   573→  `webhook`, in runtime context?
   574→- Should a webhook be able to post follow-up outbound messages to channels, or
   575→  is that just normal tool use from the agent?
   576→- Should we support a tiny structured extraction layer in v1, for example
   577→  "prepend this template with selected JSON fields", or keep v1 raw and simple?
   578→- Should we store full payloads in SQLite blobs or on disk with references?
   579→- Do we want delivery replay from the UI in v1 or wait until the delivery model
   580→  has settled?
   581→
   582→## Recommendation
   583→
   584→Build this as a **new top-level feature** using the existing agent/session/chat
   585→primitives. The key design constraint is to avoid creating a second independent
   586→agent configuration system.
   587→
   588→The clean path is:
   589→
   590→- webhook targets an existing `agent_id`
   591→- webhook adds narrow execution overrides
   592→- each accepted delivery becomes a normal persistent chat session
   593→
   594→That gives users the feature they want without turning Moltis into a haunted
   595→forest of overlapping config models.
   596→

1→# DESIGN Decisions — regorus-policy-eval
     2→
     3→## Key Decisions
     4→- [D1] Git submodule + vendored WASM build output: Regorus has no npm package; submodule at `vendor/regorus-src/` tracks upstream version, pre-built WASM at `vendor/regorus-wasm/` keeps CI Rust-free (see: ADR-088)
     5→- [D2] Engine-per-policy caching with global `Map<string, Engine>`: simple, adequate for < 50 active policies, no LRU needed (see: architecture-design.md)
     6→- [D3] Interpreter mode (`Engine` class), not compiled `Program` mode: simpler API, sufficient for governance policy complexity (see: architecture-design.md)
     7→- [D4] Required package convention `package osabio.policy`: enforced at compilation validation, queries `data.osabio.policy.allow/deny/evidence_requirement` (see: data-models.md)
     8→- [D5] Evidence requirements via Rego output field, not separate metadata: Rego policies can output `evidence_requirement` object, mapped to existing `PolicyEvidenceRequirements` type (see: data-models.md)
     9→- [D6] No `data` document beyond `input`: keep evaluation hermetic, extend `IntentEvaluationContext` if future policies need more context (see: architecture-design.md)
    10→- [D7] Policy-level evaluation replaces rule-level: one Rego source per policy, one trace entry per policy (see: component-boundaries.md)
    11→
    12→## Architecture Summary
    13→- Pattern: modular monolith with pure-core / effect-shell (existing pattern preserved)
    14→- Paradigm: functional (already set in CLAUDE.md)
    15→- Key components: `rego-evaluator.ts` (WASM loader + cache + evaluator), `rego-validation.ts` (compile check), `RegoEditor.tsx` (UI), `PolicyTestPanel.tsx` (UI)
    16→
    17→## Technology Stack
    18→- Regorus WASM (vendored): Rego evaluation engine, built from Rust source
    19→- No new npm dependencies
    20→- Existing stack unchanged (Bun, SurrealDB, React)
    21→
    22→## Constraints Established
    23→- Regorus version upgrades require Rust toolchain + wasm-pack (one-time build)
    24→- All Rego policies must declare `package osabio.policy`
    25→- WASM module loaded lazily on first evaluation (not at server startup)
    26→- Engine cache is process-global, keyed by `${policyId}:${version}`
    27→
    28→## Upstream Changes
    29→- DISCUSS wave-decisions D6 said "no backward compatibility" — confirmed, no changes needed
    30→- DISCUSS requirements FR-2 said "replace condition with rego_source" — design adds `evidence_requirement` as Rego output (extends FR-3, compatible with existing `PolicyEvidenceRequirements` type)
    31→- Story map walking skeleton step 0.1 ("load Regorus WASM") now includes vendoring step as prerequisite

The installer writes IDE identifiers to `config.yaml` under the `ides` key. Any workflow that rebuilds context files from `config.yaml` MUST map each entry to its context file and skill root using this table — it is the **single source of truth**.

75	## Four-Case Logic
76	
77	### Case 1: Create (No File Exists)
78	
79	Target file does not exist. Create new file with managed section only.
80	
81	```markdown

83	{managed section content}
84	<!-- SKF:END -->
85	```
86	
87	### Case 2: Append (File Exists, No Section)
88	
89	Target file exists but contains no `<!-- SKF:BEGIN` marker. Append managed section at end of file.
90	
91	1. Read existing file content
92	2. Append two blank lines
93	3. Append managed section with markers
94	4. Write file
95	
96	### Case 3: Regenerate (Existing Section)
97	
98	Target file contains `<!-- SKF:BEGIN` and `<!-- SKF:END -->` markers. Replace content between markers.
99	
100	1. Read existing file content
101	2. Find `<!-- SKF:BEGIN` line (preserve everything before it)
102	3. Find `<!-- SKF:END -->` line (preserve everything after it)
103	4. Replace everything between markers (inclusive) with new managed section
104	5. Write file
105	
106	### Case 4: Malformed Markers (Halt)
107	
108	Target file contains `<!-- SKF:BEGIN` but no matching `<!-- SKF:END -->` marker. This indicates a corrupted managed section.
109	
110	1. Halt workflow with error: "Malformed managed section — `<!-- SKF:BEGIN` found but no `<!-- SKF:END -->`. Fix the markers manually before re-running export."
111	2. Do not modify the file
112	
113	## Regeneration: Full Index Rebuild
114	
115	When regenerating (Case 3) or creating/appending (Cases 1-2), rebuild the skill index from the **exported skill set** only:
116	
117	1. Read `{skills_output_folder}/.export-manifest.json` (v2 schema — see [knowledge/version-paths.md](../../knowledge/version-paths.md)) to determine which skills have been explicitly exported and their `active_version` (if no manifest exists, only the current export target qualifies)
118	2. For each skill in the exported set, resolve the snippet at `{skills_output_folder}/{skill-name}/{active_version}/{skill-name}/context-snippet.md` (i.e., `{skill_package}/context-snippet.md`). Do NOT use glob patterns across version directories — always resolve via manifest `active_version` or `active` symlink
119	3. Count total skills and stack skills (from filtered set only)
120	4. Assemble filtered snippets into managed section
121	5. Sort alphabetically by skill name
122	6. Update the header line with correct counts
123	
124	**Rationale:** create-skill and update-skill also write `context-snippet.md` as a build artifact, but only export-skill is the publishing gate (ADR-K). The `.export-manifest.json` file tracks which skills have passed through export-skill, preventing draft skills from leaking into the agent's passive context.
125	
126	## Safety Rules
127	
128	- NEVER modify content outside the `<!-- SKF:BEGIN/END -->` markers
129	- ALWAYS preserve existing file content above and below markers
130	- ALWAYS verify file was written correctly after write
131	- If write fails, report error — do not attempt partial writes
